title: Deep Learning Approaches for Classifying Informal and Formal English Texts Using Linguistic Features
abstract: Effective techniques for automatically classifying texts are becoming increasingly necessary due to the exponential expansion of digital material.Differentiating between formal and informal documents can help students identify appropriate resources for their assignments and improve the effectiveness of information retrieval systems.Although machine learning is extensively utilized in classification of text, there is a lack of research focused to the effective differentiation of formal and informal writings through linguistic features.This gap highlights the necessity for advanced methodologies that improve classification accuracy and enhance the value of digital content in academic and retrieval systems.Our research addresses the problem by utilizing deep learning methodologies and a wide range of 13 linguistic attributes to get enhanced efficacy in text classification.Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTM) were considered.A dataset, including both formal (news articles, formal documents) and informal (personal letters, personal blogs) texts, were gathered from several web sources.We considered linguistic markers such as colloquialisms, contractions, modal verbs, slang, acronyms, pronouns, phrasal verbs, grammar complexity, vocabulary complexity, voice, and language type to generate the feature vector.The feature vectors were utilized to train and assess the classification models using several cross-validation techniques, particularly 3, 5, 7, and 10 folds.The efficacy of the models was evaluated using performance indicators, f-measure, accuracy, precision, and recall.With the highest accuracy of 99.8% and resilience in differentiating between formal and informal texts, the LSTM model outperformed than the others.Future research will examine big datasets, more linguistic characteristics, sophisticated deep learning models, and real-time and multilingual classification systems.

title: AI-Driven Wildfire Reasoning Utilizing Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Wildfires pose a major natural threat, causing sub-stantial loss of life and economic damage worldwide. Each year, vast areas are destroyed, and experts warn that climate change will likely intensify both the frequency and severity of these events in the future. To mitigate these hazards, a Visual Question Answering (VQA) system has been developed for the domain of wildfires, powered by multimodal RAG pipelines and large content models. The proposed solution processes multimodal input and provides logical, context-aligned responses to user prompts through a conversational user interface (CUI). Here, a multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework is designed for wildfire detection, which integrates dedicated IMAGE RAG and CSV RAG components. The IMAGE RAG component processes diverse visual data, including UAV imagery, drone captures, and mobile phone images, to identify fire signatures, smoke patterns, and burn severity assessments. Simultaneously, the CSV RAG component handles structured environmental data encompassing meteorological readings, historical wildfire records, and sensor outputs to provide contextual understanding of fire conditions and risk factors. The system achieved a performance of 74.13% accuracy on an evaluation dataset of wildfire-related question-answer pairs, which demonstrates its effectiveness in real-world information synthesis tasks. This multi-modal RAG framework addresses critical gaps in current wildfire monitoring systems by providing an intelligent, query-driven interface that can synthesize environmental data for improved decision-making in wildfire management and prevention strategies.

title: AI-Based Candidate Recommendation for Company Vacancies: Emphasizing Soft Skills and Competencies
abstract: Historically, the recruitment process relies predominantly on resumes, academic achievement, and technical testing, but these can overlook significant soft skills for workplace success. Soft skills such as confidence, communication, adaptability, and stress tolerance have direct influence on the performance of employees but are tested subjectively and non-systematically in an interview. This paper introduces a multimodal approach of an AI-recommended candidate system that objectively evaluates the soft skills of candidates through a multimodal approach. The framework integrates four modules: (i) speech and tone analysis for verbal confidence, (ii) hand movement recognition for confidence estimation, (iii) eye-contact detection for self-confidence and attentiveness, and (iv) facial expression analysis for stress. All the modules output binary decisions Confident/Non-Confident or Stress/Non-Stress, which are integrated to present a holistic perspective of the candidate. Minimum decision-making assessment is also offered to optimize evaluation. The application is implemented as a web app recording candidate interview, processing multimodal signals with machine learning models, and providing real-time recommendations to recruiters through an interactive dashboard. Experimental outcomes demonstrate superb accuracy from all modules and superb user acceptance, confirming the feasibility of applying multimodal AI to enhance fairness and richness in hiring. This study illustrates the potential of AI to reduce bias, increase transparency, and support data-driven decision-making that is more subtle than résumé-based assessment.

title: A Bilingual Plagiarism Detection Approach for Sinhala–English Text Using TF-IDF and Cosine Similarity
abstract: Plagiarism detection in bilingual and low-resource settings remains a difficult problem, especially in Sri Lanka where Sinhala and English are commonly mixed in academic writing. Popular plagiarism detection tools such as Turnitin do not handle Sinhala text, and cloud-based services raise data privacy and security concerns for local universities. In this work, a bilingual plagiarism detection system is presented with support for Sinhala FM-font to Unicode conversion, TF–IDF vectorization, and cosine similarity scoring. The system also generates sentence-level evidence to help instructors verify suspected overlap. A Flask backend, React-based frontend, and MongoDB repository were used for the prototype implementation. Evaluation on de-identified student essays and reports showed accuracy above 85% with processing times under 10 seconds for documents of about 3,500 words. Feedback from lecturers confirmed that the interface was usable and trustworthy for classroom use. The study also outlines design trade-offs, current limitations, and possible extensions with semantic NLP techniques.

title: Explainable Fish Disease Detection Using Ensemble Models of CNN and Vision Transformers
abstract: Early and accurate detection of fish infections is crucial in aquaculture systems to protect aquatic biodiversity, guarantee sustainable production, and reduce financial losses. Deep learning models enable automated fish disease diagnosis and enhanced aquaculture health management. Using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Transformer ensemble with explainable AI (XAI), this study develops a reliable system to precisely identify fish infections in response to this pressing demand. With more than 2,000 images across seven disease categories, the dataset, which was acquired from Kaggle, offers a varied and difficult standard for assessment. Although earlier research has investigated CNN and Transformer ensembles, none have used XAI approaches to improve transparency and trust. Our suggested EfficientNet_B0 and DeiT ensemble fills this gap by including Grad-CAM visualizations for both high performance and interpretability. Using several of performance metrics, the model's efficacy is assessed against the most advanced CNNs and Transformers. Experimental results show that the ensemble demonstrated improved predictive performance and interpretability for practical aquaculture applications, achieving optimum outcomes with 99.70% accuracy, an Area Under Curve (AUC) of 1.00, and F1-scores above 0.98 across all classes.

title: Detection and Classification of Pests and Diseases of Cassava Plants Using Deep Learning
abstract: Cassava, a crucial crop especially in tropical regions, faces significant productivity losses due to pests and diseases. This research presents a deep learning approach for classifying cassava pests and diseases using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with ResNet-18 architecture. A dataset of 6,300 images across nine disease classes was compiled from Sri Lankan cassava fields and supplemented with Kaggle data. The dataset was annotated and augmented to enhance model robustness. ResNet-18 was used for model development, trained with 70% of the data, validated on 20%, and tested on 10%. The model achieved a training accuracy of 96.21%, validation accuracy of 87.06%, and test accuracy of 88.25%, demonstrating good generalization and reliability. Additionally, a web interface was developed for disease detection, providing an efficient tool for cassava disease management and potential yield improvements. This research differs from prior studies by addressing a broader scope of pests and diseases rather than focusing solely on leaf-related diseases. By integrating multiple pest and disease categories, the study provides a more comprehensive solution for cassava health management. The successful integration of the model into a web interface enables efficient diagnosis and post-harvest quality assessment, benefiting farmers and stakeholders by reducing reliance on expert intervention, improving yields, and contributing to food security.

title: Integrating Changepoint Detection with Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Forecasting Sri Lanka’s Monthly Inflation
abstract: Inflation is the sustained increase in general price levels over time, which leads to a decline in the purchasing power of money. It impacts not only businesses but also the country’s overall economy. Sri Lanka’s inflation has experienced significant volatility in recent years due to internal factors such as weak economic strategies and political instability, as well as external shocks, including global price fluctuations and economic crises. These fluctuations have raised challenges for researchers attempting to develop accurate forecasting models, as classical approaches often fail to capture extreme variations. Building on this context, the study focuses on identifying the most suitable machine learning and deep learning models for forecasting Sri Lanka’s inflation rate. Emphasis is placed on capturing extreme fluctuations and accounting for recent crises and political changes during the period from January 2015 to July 2025. Multiple machine learning models were initially applied to the dataset. However, most models demonstrated poor generalization, reflected in relatively large RMSE values. A deep learning Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model provided the best initial fit, producing lower RMSE values and avoiding overfitting. A new inflation series was constructed by incorporating forecasted values from the LSTM model to reduce the influence of sudden changes and improve the model’s ability to capture the underlying pattern. This refined series was subsequently modeled, and the Feedforward Neural Network achieved the most reliable performance, giving accurate forecasts with the lowest RMSE and strong generalization. The findings highlight the potential of hybrid approaches in handling volatile economic series and provide valuable insights for decision-making not only in the corporate field but also for government policy makers. These results contribute to reliable inflation forecasting, particularly under uncertain and crisis-driven economic environments.

title: Systematic Literature Review of Explainable LLM-Powered ChatOps for CI/CD Pipeline Diagnostics and Developer Support
abstract: This systematic literature review examines how explainable Large Language Models (LLMs) transform chat-ops applications for CI/CD pipeline diagnostics and developer support. Analyzing contemporary research from 2021–2025, this review synthesizes findings from studies on conversational AI agents, LLM-driven DevOps automation, and explainable AI techniques in software development. Key methodological approaches include Domain-Specific Languages (DSLs) for chatbot development, multi-agent orchestration frameworks, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, and two-staged LLM frameworks for detecting and remediating failures. Key findings reveal significant advancements in automating root cause analysis, orchestrating pipelines intelligently, and creating natural language interfaces for complex DevOps operations. Integrating explainable AI principles with conversational interfaces improves developer productivity, reduces mean time to resolution (MTTR), and enhances collaboration between development and operations teams. However, persistent interpretability, security governance, integration complexity, and maintaining human oversight in automated decision-making processes. This review provides a comprehensive roadmap for researchers and practitioners seeking to leverage explainable LLM-powered chat-ops solutions for enhanced CI/CD pipeline management and developer support.

title: Enhancing the Performance of Open-Source LLMs for E-Commerce CRM Automation Using Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has heightened the need for efficient Customer Relationship Management (CRM) automation. Proprietary Large Language Models (LLMs) like GPT-4 excel in CRM tasks but are costly for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Open-source alternatives, such as LLaMA-3.1, offer affordability but are limited in terms of accuracy and contextual understanding. This paper presents a multi-agent framework to optimize open-source LLMs for three key CRM tasks: Named Entity Disambiguation (NED), Policy Violation Identification (PVI), and Knowledge-based Question Answering (KQA). Evaluated on the CRMArena benchmark with 390 queries, the framework using LLaMA-3.1-70B achieved accuracies of 92.31% (NED), 59.23% (PVI), and 85.38% (KQA), outperforming prior open-source benchmarks (<55%). The approach demonstrates cost-effective CRM automation comparable to proprietary models, with inference costs as low as $0.04 per task. Future enhancements include fine-tuning and real-world deployment to further improve robustness.

title: Uncovering Hidden Temporal Patterns in T20I Cricket Through Ball-by-Ball Data Analysis
abstract: Twenty20 International (T20I) cricket’s volatile nature makes static metrics inadequate for strategic decision-making. This paper presents a ball-by-ball, over-by-over analysis to capture the temporal dynamics of T20I matches, utilizing a comprehensive dataset of 1,118 men’s T20Is. Our analysis shows a sharp disconnect between Powerplay runs and later scoring (Pearson’s r = 0.129), but a strong penalty for Powerplay wickets, underscoring the premium on early wicket preservation. We demonstrate that strike-rate progression, not overall strike rate, is the more informative indicator of a batter’s role, some accelerate late (e.g., Kohli), while others sustain high rates from the start (e.g., de Villiers). Contextual analysis further reveals how statistics can mislead: for example, MS Dhoni’s contributions understate his value as a finisher when match situations are considered. Beyond individuals, we find that home advantage is concentrated among top-ranked teams. Collectively, these insights underscore the necessity of temporal, time-series metrics for refining player selection and batting orders. This approach moves beyond static analysis, offering a more granular and effective basis for tactical decision-making in T20I cricket.

title: Multilingual Text-To-Speech with User Specific Voice Cloning and Accent Adaptation
abstract: Personalized voice synthesis and accent adaptation are at the heart of this multilingual Text-To-Speech (TTS) system, developed to expand accessibility and inclusiveness in human computer communication. The system focuses on supporting individuals who have lost their natural voice due to medical conditions while enabling real time communication. Built on Microsoft's SpeechT5 transformer model with x-vector speaker embeddings, the system generates natural speech from minimal data, allowing unique voice synthesis across multiple languages. The methodology involved curating and preprocessing multilingual datasets in English, Sinhala and Tamil, where text was transliterated into a unified phonetic form for cross language compatibility. This design makes the system adaptable to virtually any language setting. The SpeechT5 model was fine tuned using transfer learning, which reduced data needs for low resource languages and enabled clear voice with 20-40 minutes of data. Evaluation was conducted using Word Error Rate (WER), cosine similarity, and Euclidean distance. Results showed that for short sentences, the system achieved a low WER of 0.1, whereas for long sentences the WER increased to 0.53, highlighting its effectiveness primarily for short sentence synthesis as reflected in the dataset design. Speaker identity was well preserved, with cosine similarity scores ranging from 0.94-0.97 and Euclidean distance values between 1.5-1.7. These results confirm the system's ability to produce natural, speaker specific speech in low resource settings. Beyond technical contributions, this study demonstrates real world impact by enabling voice recovery for patients, personalized communication, and inclusive support for underrepresented languages. By integrating transfer learning, phoneme alignment, and speaker embeddings, it offers a scalable framework for natural, user specific, accent aware TTS in diverse environments.

title: Leveraging Multimodal AI and Explainable AI for Early Detection of Oral Cancer
abstract: Early detection of oral cancer is critical in low- resource settings, yet current AI systems often rely solely on image data and operate as "black boxes," limiting clinical trust. We present an explainable multimodal screening model that combines smartphone intraoral images with patient metadata (age, gender, tobacco, alcohol, betel-quid use). Images are encoded with EfficientNetV2B0, metadata are processed through a compact dense branch, and features are early-fused for binary classification (benign vs. OPMD/OCA risk). The model was trained with transfer learning, class weighting, targeted augmentation, dropout, and early stopping on a patient-level split (80/20) to prevent data leakage. On the held-out set, the system achieved an accuracy of 83.3%, AUC 0.8615, sensitivity 81.7%, specificity 85.1%, NPV 84.2%, and MCC 0.66, demonstrating a balanced screening profile. Statistical testing (DeLong) showed the multimodal model significantly outperformed image-only and metadata-only baselines (p < 0.05). To support clinical adoption, we integrated XAI: Grad-CAM localizes lesion-focused regions in images, while SHAP quantifies metadata contributions; their agreement confirms that the model’s predictions are based on clinically meaningful cues. A lightweight web application delivers real-time inference with embedded explanations to facilitate frontline use. Results indicate that fusing image and risk-factor information yields a transparent, accurate, and deployable AI tool for community-level early oral cancer screening in resource- constrained environments.

title: Semantic Embedding-Based Zero-Shot and Few-Shot Learning for Cold-Start Movie Recommendation
abstract: This research proposes a novel recommendation system designed to effectively address the persistent cold-start problem in movie recommendation by leveraging semantic embeddings derived from natural language metadata and minimal user interaction data. Utilizing the widely recognized MovieLens dataset, the approach integrates advanced pre-trained language models, specifically Sentence-BERT, to transform movie titles, genres, and plot-related textual features into rich, high-dimensional semantic embeddings. By constructing user profile vectors based on a small number of positive user feedback instances, the system operates under both zero-shot learning (ZSL) and few-shot learning (FSL) paradigms. In zero-shot scenarios, it recommends new movies solely using item metadata without relying on historical interaction data, while in few-shot scenarios, it incorporates limited user ratings to enhance personalization. Experimental results demonstrate that embedding-based neural framework achieves robust generalization capabilities in zero-shot ranking tasks and yields high predictive accuracy in few-shot rating predictions, significantly outperforming baseline models. This study highlights the potential for embedding-driven recommendation architectures to provide scalable, content-aware personalization in dynamic media platforms where new items are frequently introduced. Moreover, the efficiency of the proposed method ensures computational practicality, making it suitable for real-world deployment. These findings contribute to the evolving landscape of recommender system research by emphasizing minimal supervision and semantic content understanding as effective strategies to overcome cold-start challenges.

title: TransUNet: Hybrid CNN-Transformer Model for Automated Breast Cancer Segmentation in Ultrasound Images
abstract: Breast cancer is a leading cause of mortality among women worldwide, and early detection is critical for effective treatment. Ultrasound imaging is widely used for diagnosis, but manual interpretation can be slow and error-prone. This study proposes a hybrid TransUNet model combining CNN and transformer encoders to accurately segment breast cancer in ultrasound images. Using the public BUSI dataset with 780 images and annotated masks, extensive data augmentation was applied to improve robustness. The model was trained with a combined Dice and binary cross-entropy loss function for 50 epochs. It achieved a Dice score of 0.6836 and an IoU of 0.5411 on test data, demonstrating promising segmentation accuracy. Future work will investigate comparative evaluation with UNet++, Swin-UNet, and Attention-UNet, and also advanced augmentations, attention mechanisms, and explainability for clinical utility improvement.

title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Healthcare
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a critical paradigm for training machine learning models on sensitive, decentralized healthcare data, yet it is often hampered by high communication costs. Concurrently, Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) have emerged as a parameter-efficient alternative to traditional Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs), promising higher accuracy with smaller models. This paper investigates the synergy between these two domains, proposing and evaluating a Federated Learning using KAN to address the communication bottleneck in healthcare AI. We design and implement task-specific KAN architectures, including novel Convolutional KAN (Conv-KAN) variants. We compare the performance and communication overhead of Fed-KANs against equivalently-sized standard models (MLPs) in a simulated federated environment. Our results consistently demonstrate that Fed-KANs achieve comparable or superior predictive accuracy in significantly fewer communication rounds. This work establishes that the architectural properties of KANs translate into substantial gains in communication efficiency in the federated setting. Our results reveal that KANs’ faster learning dynamics and parameter efficiency translate into fewer communication rounds and lower total costs, with RBF-KANs achieving a remarkable 92.13% test accuracy, significantly outperforming traditional MLP models (70.078%) and Spline-KANs (82.67%) after 100 communication rounds.

title: Bridging Communication Barriers: A Deep Learning Approach for Sinhala Sign Language Recognition
abstract: Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) communities and Sinhala-speaking communities in Sri Lanka face a significant challenge in effective communication, largely due to the lack of automated Sinhala Sign Language (SSL) translators. In this paper, this gap is bridged through the introduction of an AI-based system that aims at converting the SSL gestures to Sinhala text via deep learning technologies. To create a strong dataset, the 3,800 videos of the 19 different SSL gestures were gathered from publicly available and custom video recordings that are validated by the Deaf individuals and that are authentic and reliable. Preprocessing of each video included extracting 30 frames, resizing them to 64x64 pixels, and normalizing pixel values to improve model performance. It utilised three advanced deep learning architectures, including 3D Convolutional Neural Networks (3D CNN), a CNN with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture, and Temporal Segment Networks (TSN). Random search methods were applied in order to optimise model hyperparameters. Accuracy, confusion matrix analysis and classification reports were used as measures of evaluation. The results show that the CNN+LSTM model achieved an accuracy of 91.58%, indicating the usefulness of deep learning methods in recognizing gestures of SSL

title: Identify Dyscalculia, Dysgraphia Learning Disabilities in Deaf and Mute Primary Students and Help to Improve Learning Abilities
abstract: Learning disabilities, particularly Dyscalculia and Dysgraphia, significantly hinder students' academic, social, and future occupational outcomes. Deaf and mute primary students face amplified challenges due to limited availability of specialized educational resources and tools that cater to their unique communication needs. This research presents an innovative, intelligent learning environment designed specifically to identify and mitigate Dyscalculia and Dysgraphia among deaf and mute primary students. Leveraging advanced artificial intelligence, computer vision, and machine learning (ML) technologies, the developed system incorporates Sinhala Sign Language (SLSL) and interactive, adaptive learning methodologies. The identification process employs Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to analyze handwritten numerical inputs and sign language gestures, categorizing students based on the severity of their conditions. Subsequently, personalized, engaging instructional activities facilitate gradual skill development and continuous improvement. Robust data privacy measures ensure ethical standards, while automated tracking provides actionable insights for educators and parents. Initial findings indicate significant improvements in student performance and engagement, demonstrating the system's efficacy in delivering inclusive, culturally relevant, and accessible educational interventions tailored for deaf and mute students.

title: Dynamic Brightest Intensity ROI for Smartphone-Based PPG: A Comparative Analysis of Frame Selection Methods for Hemoglobin Estimation and Anemia Classification
abstract: Smartphone photoplethysmography (sPPG) has become one of the promising non-invasive methods of estimating hemoglobin and screening for anemia, especially where resources are limited. However, extracting PPG signals from smartphone fingertip videos is extremely sensitive to frame quality, changes in illumination and motion artifacts. This study fills a literature gap by introducing a frame selection algorithm, Dynamic Brightest Intensity Region of Interest (ROI) and compares its performance with five existing algorithms namely Fixed Center ROI, Right to Left ROI, Temporal Difference ROI, Template Matching ROI and Frame Adaptive ROI. The latter methodology uses a set of data augmentation and preprocessing techniques to improve the quality of PPG signals obtained based on fingertip videos. The signals are then processed by physiologically-informed feature extraction and then refined by systematic feature selection to accurately estimate hemoglobin and classify anemia severity by using XGBoost and Artificial Neural Networks.In this study, Frame Adaptive ROI method gave the best predictive performance; however, it involves intensive pixel-level operations and dynamic masking, which makes the method time-consuming and more computationally intensive. Conversely, the suggested Dynamic Brightest Intensity ROI algorithm showed a desirable trade-off between accuracy and efficiency with a high level of hemoglobin regression (RMSE = 0.5043) and anemia severity classification (accuracy = 0.9783). It has a reduced computational complexity, and thus is better applicable in real-time or mobile deployment environments where processing time is a key factor. These results indicate that the dynamic selection of the frame is significant in enhancing the quality of the signal.

title: Integrating Sentiment Analysis & Historical Data for Predicting Crude Oil Prices
abstract: Crude oil price forecasting remains a persistent challenge due to the volatility introduced by fast-moving geopolitical events and macroeconomic shocks. Currently available models mostly rely solely on time-series patterns or sentiment analysis. But these approaches do not capture the full complexity of short-term market dynamics. This research addresses this gap. Most times inaccurate forecasts can impact traders, risk managers, and policymakers globally. This study aims to develop a forecasting model that integrates domainspecific news sentiment with traditional market fundamentals to predict the next week’s crude oil price. We compiled a dataset of ~60,000 English oil-related news articles, cleaned and timestamped them, and derived weekly sentiment features using VADER, FinBERT, and a domain-adapted CrudeBERT. These were combined with market variables including production, inventories, imports/exports, benchmark WTI prices, the Weekly Economic Index, and Geopolitical Risk Indices. A range of models, including linear regressions, tree-based methods, neural networks, and SARIMAX, were evaluated, alongside an ensemble that fused the best-performing tree-based and neural approaches. Best results were given by the ensemble (Random Forest + XGBoost + LSTM) with CrudeBERT based sentiment, which achieves the best accuracy: MAE ≈ 1.19 USD, RMSE ≈ 1.48 USD, MAPE ≈ 1.57%, and R2≈ 0.935. These results substantially outperform models that exclude sentiment or rely on generic sentiment features. The findings shows that combining domain specific news sentiment with economic and market fundamentals significantly enhances short-term crude oil price prediction. The novelty of this work lies in its unified framework that combines large-scale sentiment analysis from news articles with traditional oil market variables and geopolitical risk indices providing new evidence that such integration delivers materially improved forecasting accuracy.

title: Topic Modeling and Speech Categorization for Sinhala Parliamentary Discussions Using Natural Language Processing
abstract: Natural Language Processing has become a powerful means of analyzing large-scale textual corpora, particularly within political communication. Parliamentary speeches are rich repositories of governance priorities and societal concerns. In Sri Lanka, Sinhala parliamentary speeches remain underexplored due to linguistic complexity and limited computational resources. This study introduces an automated system to categorize Sinhala parliamentary speeches into key policy domains such as Education, Agriculture, and Health. The methodology applies lemmatization to normalize morphological variations, Term Frequency Inverse Document Frequency for feature representation, and multinomial logistic regression for supervised classification. Unlike conventional binary classification approaches, the model predicts the most relevant domain for each speech while also providing the proportion of speech content attributed to each category, enabling fine-grained analysis of parliamentary focus. Empirical evaluations demonstrate strong and balanced classification performance, with consistent precision, recall, and F1-score values across all categories. Trend analysis further reveals sectoral priorities and variations by political party and speaker role. This study contributes to legislative transparency and advances Natural Language Processing research for Sinhala, a low-resource language.

title: Multimodal Browser Based System for Online Child Safety Through Real Time Content Filtering
abstract: The rapid spread of harmful online material poses significant risks to children and young users. Existing detection systems often focus narrowly on pornography or text-based filters and struggle with real time deployment across diverse content types. This research introduces a multimodal detection framework that integrates Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Computer Vision (CV) for safer browsing. For textual detection, a fine-tuned BigBird-RoBERTa model, trained on 14,000 samples, achieved an accuracy of 97.3%, significantly reducing false positives compared to prior BERT-based approaches. For visual detection, a YOLOv8m object detection model was trained on 13,708 annotated images across four harmful categories: adult, weapons, smoking, and gore, achieving a mean average precision (mAP@50) of 0.899. These models were combined into a custom Python-based web browser: text detection is deployed on an AWS server for efficient API-based inference, while the YOLOv8m detector runs locally to minimize latency and preserve user privacy. The integrated browser provides real time detection and automatic masking of harmful content in images, videos, and text, with average response times below 250 ms, enabling seamless browsing. Compared to existing methods, this system delivers broader coverage, real time usability, and privacy-aware deployment by performing visual inference entirely on the local device. The results demonstrate that lightweight multimodal AI can effectively enhance online child safety, offering a practical and scalable framework for future integration into consumer browsers.

title: LIME-Integrated Multi-Architecture Deep Learning for Interpretable Multi-Stage Alzheimer’s Disease Detection in MRI Scans
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a leading cause of dementia and presents significant challenges in diagnosis because it progresses and requires costly, invasive tests such as MRI and cognitive assessments. This paper addresses these issues by utilizing the OASIS MRI dataset, which includes 80,000 images categorized into four stages of AD: Non-Demented, Very Mild Demented, Mild Demented, and Demented. Several advanced deep learning models, including EfficientNetV2-S, MobileNetV3-Large, RegNetY-032, ConvNeCtV2-Tiny, as well as a combination of ResNet-50 and ViT-Tiny, were trained and fine-tuned using data augmentation techniques like random rotations and color jittering. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy,, precision, recall, and F1-score on split datasets, with RegNetY-032 achieving the highest metrics at 99.45%. Additionally, Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) was used to highlight important features influencing model decisions, such as key brain regions including the hippocampus. The results demonstrate improved accuracy and interpretability, offering a promising approach for the early detection of AD in clinical practice.

abstract: Undergraduate students in Sri Lanka struggle with presentation skills due to performance anxiety, insufficient guidance, and lack of real-time feedback. SPEAKRAFT addresses this gap as an AI-powered virtual trainer that delivers intelligent, real-time coaching. It integrates ML models to evaluate facial expressions using OpenCV/DeepFace, vocal loudness, speech pacing, and filler words. The modular web platform employs FastAPI for AI orchestration, React/JavaScript for frontend interactivity, and Express JS/Mongo DB for backend functionality. Users engage in targeted practice sessions or full presentations, receiving granular feedback and visual analytics. The system also enables institutional applications for academic and professional communication development.

title: Towards Non-Invasive Blood Group Prediction: Fingerprint Recognition with Advanced Deep Learning
abstract: Accurate and rapid identification of blood groups is critical in emergency medicine and healthcare delivery. Traditional serological methods are invasive, time-consuming, and require laboratory infrastructure. This study explores fingerprint images as a non-invasive biometric modality for blood group prediction using advanced deep learning architectures. The dataset of over 8,000 fingerprint images was preprocessed with augmentation, normalization, and noise reduction. Multiple models, including CNN variants, lightweight architectures, transformer-based models, and next-generation convolutional networks, were trained and evaluated. A weighted soft voting ensemble (0.5 EfficientNetV2-S + 0.5 MobileNetV3-Large) achieved the highest accuracy of 99.88%, outperforming individual models like MobileNetV3-Large (98.51%) and EfficientNetV2-S (97.79%). These results indicate that fingerprint-based deep learning provides a reliable, noninvasive approach for blood group prediction, with potential for deployment in mobile and point-of-care systems.

title: Random Forest Regression Approach for Balancing Vegetable Production and Price Forecasting in Sri Lanka
abstract: Sri Lanka’s agriculture sector, a pillar of the national economy, is extremely vulnerable to price volatility in essential crops such as potatoes, particularly in major production and trading hubs like Welimada, Bandarawela, and Nuwara Eliya. This research project addresses this critical issue by developing a supervised machine learning framework that leverages Random Forest regression to forecast wholesale potato prices, integrating market-specific prices, climatic indicators, rainfall, and inflation to model complex non-linear interactions. The methodology involved comprehensive data preprocessing, meticulous hyperparameter tuning, and rigorous five-fold cross-validation, ensuring resilient generalization despite a limited historical data window. Model evaluation yielded strong results: R2values were 0.470 for Welimada, 0.701 for Bandarawela, and 0.807 for Nuwara Eliya, with corresponding RMSE values of 35.87, 25.24, and 21.30, respectively. The entire workflow, from data ingestion, model training, and result analysis to application deployment, was implemented using Python’s data science stack and presented via a Streamlit web application for real-time access. Unique to this project, the application not only forecasts prices but also provides market analytics tailored to stakeholders, including revenue estimation and oversupply risk detection per region, empowering informed decisions for farmers, traders, and policymakers. By offering transparent, actionable, and context-aware price insights, the system alleviates uncertainty, enhances market participation, and ultimately supports greater stability and sustainability in Sri Lankan agriculture. This solution, designed to be extensible, paves the way for broader crop integration, real-time analytics, and further reinforcement of food system resilience in the future.

title: A Framework For Sequence Classification in Medical Diagnostics using Machine Learning Techniques: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Sequence data such as time-series signals and event sequences are increasingly central in medical diagnostics because they capture temporal patterns essential for disease detection and monitoring. Machine learning (ML) methods have rapidly evolved to analyze such data, progressing from early statistical models to modern deep learning architectures. This paper presents a systematic literature review of sequence classification in healthcare diagnostics, synthesizing studies published between 2020 and 2025. A PRISMA-guided search of IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect was conducted, focusing on sequence-based diagnostic ML models. The review categorizes existing contributions by ML techniques (from classical classifiers to CNNs, RNNs, and Transformers), architectural frameworks, clinical application domains, data sources and preprocessing approaches, and evaluation metrics. Deep learning—particularly recurrent networks and Transformers—now dominates sequence classification tasks, achieving high accuracy in arrhythmia detection, seizure prediction, and early sepsis recognition. Recent work also explores multimodal integration, interpretability techniques such as attention mechanisms, and efficient architectures like TinyTransformers for wearable devices. Emerging trends highlight increasing model complexity, interpretability, multimodal fusion, and improved generalization through domain adaptation. Persistent gaps remain, including limited support for differential diagnosis, insufficient integration of medical domain knowledge, data scarcity for rare conditions, and a lack of prospective clinical validation. Addressing these gaps is crucial for translating research progress into clinically reliable and widely deployable diagnostic systems. Overall, sequence-based ML demonstrates strong potential for enhancing modern clinical decision support through more accurate, interpretable, and generalizable diagnostic models.

title: Evaluating Out-of-Distribution Robustness of TabPFN on Tabular Data
abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization is a critical challenge in machine learning, especially for tabular data where real-world distributions often differ from training data. TabPFN is a recent transformer-based model that achieves strong performance on small tabular classification tasks by training only on synthetic data. However, its ability to generalize to OOD scenarios in real-world datasets has not been fully explored. In this work, the evaluation of the pre-trained TabPFN model is extended to the UCI Adult dataset, focusing on OOD splits based on education, age, and gender. TabPFN’s performance is compared with traditional models such as Random Forest, XGBoost, and LinearSVC. Experiments show that TabPFN consistently achieves higher accuracy and F1 scores on OOD samples across different demographic splits. Visualizations and statistical analysis are provided to support these findings. This study demonstrates the practical value of TabPFN for robust tabular classification in the presence of distribution shifts, and highlights its potential for real-world applications where fairness and reliability are important.

title: Hybrid Deep Learning approach for Paddy Leaf Disease Detection
abstract: Rice is a one of the most important staple food in the world. Considering almost half of people around the globe gets their food from paddy agriculture, it is imperative to find creative ways to boost output and resource efficiency. But the paddy leaf diseases have become a threat to global paddy cultivation and global food security. This study proposes a hybrid Deep Learning (DL) based system that uses MobileNetV2 as a feature extractor in combination with a base and hybrid model architecture to classify rice leaf diseases, including bacterial blight, blast, brown spot, and tungro. For the Data augmentation, this research used techniques like rotation, flipping, shifting, and zooming were applied to enhance model generalization. To improve model generalization, data augmentation methods like rotation, flipping, shifting, and zooming were used. Rescaling was kept constant throughout testing and validation to ensure a consistent assessment. The system can identify changes in data distribution over time thanks to the integration of a Simple Drift Detection Method (DDM), which constantly monitors concept drift throughout testing. The reliability of the suggested method for real-world implementation was demonstrated by its high classification accuracy of 98% and robust recall across all classes. This work is more valuable for farmers, researchers, and other agricultural stakeholders for order to improve the system's suitability for a variety of field scenarios, future research will concentrate on real-time deployment, adaptive learning, and dataset expansion.

title: Prototype-Based Dynamic Autoencoders for Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Explainability
abstract: Real-time detection of anomalies in data streams is a foundation of modern applied analysis in complex systems. It enables experts to design rapid, efficient, reliable, and high-performance decision support systems. Rapid identification of abnormal or unexpected behavior is often insufficient in high-risk contexts; therefore, it is essential to provide explanations for these predictions. Although the use of autoencoder-based algorithms has been shown to be effective in the detection of anomalies, it is important to note that their effectiveness decreases with time due to changes in the underlying data distribution. To solve this drawback, we introduce a solution that incorporates the dynamic updating of autoencoders based on the prototypes computed from their latent representations. We propose two algorithms: Update-Based Prototypes-v1, an algorithm specifically designed to detect anomalies through continual, prototype-informed updates, and ARCANA Prototypes-v1, which is developed to provide reliable explanations for anomalies detected over time. We used the Skoltech Anomaly Benchmark database for our experiments. The Update-Based Prototypes-v1 algorithm achieved a detection rate of 80% with a false alarm rate of 20%, compared to 49% for an implementation without updates. The results confirm that the proposed model offers high performance comparable to state-of-the-art architectures in the same field, even when data characteristics change. Additionally, ARCANA Prototypesv-1 provides precise explanations, which enhances the usefulness of the prototypes for explaining anomalies.

title: Artificial intelligence Attributes & socio psychological factors Influencing the usage of chatbot in Sri Lankan Systemically important banks
abstract: The research investigates the impact of artificial intelligence attributes (Perceived anthropomorphism, perceived intelligence, perceived animacy) and socio-psychological factors (perceived emotional awareness of chatbot and perceived social presence) on the usage of chatbots in Systemically important banks in Sri Lanka. In the positivism realm, deductive approach was followed using survey strategy and a mono-method to collect cross sectional data to investigate perceived anthropomorphism (PAT), perceived intelligence (PI), perceived animacy (PA), perceived emotional awareness of chatbot (PEA), and perceived social presence (PSP) were investigated as factors of usage of chatbots. The data was analyzed through SPSS. The findings revealed that perceived anthropomorphism, perceived intelligence, perceived emotional awareness, and perceived social presence predicted the usage of chatbots significantly and positively, while perceived animacy was non-significant. The results help banks develop chatbots that are highly intelligent and anthropomorphic, with emotional awareness and social presence to improve client happiness and adoption rates. Since perceived animacy was non-significant, banks may focus on emotional and functional components rather than realistic animations to boost the efficacy of digital services. This study uses the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA), Theory of Mind (TOM), and Social Presence Theory (SPT) as core theories and uses the TAM, UTAUT models as foundations for our research. In updating human-computer interaction models in banking settings, this study goes beyond the SPT, TOM, and CASA theories by showing that perceived and socioemotional factors, rather than animacy, which is not a crucial factor, form the basis of usage of chatbots.

title: Federated Learning and Data Mining-Based Botnet Attack Detection Framework for Internet of Things
abstract: Botnet attacks in Internet of Things (IoT) environments often occur as multi-stage campaigns, making early and reliable detection difficult across distributed and privacy-sensitive networks. Centralized detection approaches are often limited by heterogeneous traffic characteristics, severe data imbalance, and the need to aggregate large volumes of raw network data, raising scalability and privacy concerns. To address these challenges, this paper proposes FDA, a federated learning-based and data mining-driven framework for stage-aware botnet attack detection in IoT networks. FDA operates at network gateways, where anomalous traffic is first detected and then abstracted into compact and interpretable patterns using Frequent Itemset Mining (FIM). This pattern-based representation reduces noise and local traffic bias, enabling more robust learning across different IoT networks. Lightweight neural network models are trained locally at gateways, and a global model is learned through federated aggregation of model parameters, avoiding direct sharing of raw network data while enabling gateways to collaboratively learn evolving attack patterns across different IoT networks. Experimental results show that FDA achieves anomaly detection F1-scores above 99% across all gateways and multi-stage botnet attack classification F1-scores in the range of 48–49%, which are comparable to centralized machine-learning baselines while operating under decentralized and privacy-preserving constraints. Overall, FDA provides a practical, privacy-preserving, and effective solution for distributed botnet attack stage detection in real-world IoT deployments.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Tamil OCR Systems: A Survey, Dataset Creation, Benchmarking, and Error Analysis
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of Optical Character Recognition (OCR) systems for Tamil, a low-resource language that continues to trail behind high-resource counterparts in recognition accuracy despite substantial research efforts. Tamil OCR is inherently challenging due to the script’s intricate character shapes, numerous ligatures, and its large set of 247 characters, including complex vowel-consonant combinations. These features complicate segmentation and recognition far more than Latin scripts. To contextualize the evaluation, a literature survey was conducted, covering key aspects such as pre-processing, recognition, and post-processing techniques. A major barrier in Tamil OCR research is the absence of a standardized diachronic benchmark dataset. To address this, we curated a dataset of 164 scanned images from printed documents spanning from 1850 to the present, taken at 10-year intervals. The collection captures eleven types of page layouts and eight document characteristics, considering noise levels, monolingual, and multilingual content, and printing technologies, etc. Expert-verified ground-truth data, including full-page transcriptions, line segmentations, and bounding boxes, enable detailed system evaluation. Using this dataset, we evaluated both commercial and open-source OCR systems through three strategies: full-page recognition, line-level segmentation, and bounding-box-based processing. Results show that while commercial systems perform better in terms of character and word accuracy, they struggle with complex layouts, degraded text, and historical typefaces. Although the focus is on Tamil, the evaluation approach and findings offer broader relevance for OCR research in other complex-script languages. The dataset and evaluation results are publicly available on GitHub to support future work in this domain.

title: Exposure-Based Media Mix Modeling Using Machine Learning and Genetic Algorithms
abstract: Media budget allocation remains a persistent challenge in the advertising industry. Inefficient spending and biased planning decisions often reduce campaign effectiveness. Advertisers struggle to balance investments across television, radio, press, and digital platforms while managing diminishing returns. This study proposes a data-driven media mix determination model that integrates supervised machine learning with genetic algorithm-based optimization. The objective is to maximize audience reach while maintaining cost efficiency. Unlike traditional media mix models that rely on aggregated medium-level performance, this study adopts an audience exposure-based modelling approach. Facebook and YouTube are used as digital media platforms in this study. Television and digital models are trained using exposure-based reach measures, such as 1 plus and 2 plus reach. Machine learning models, including decision trees, random forests, XGBoost, and LightGBM, are evaluated to capture complex and nonlinear relationships between spend and exposure-based reach. Smoothed reach response curves are used to identify efficiency levels and saturation points for each medium. A genetic algorithm is then applied to derive the optimal budget allocation across media under efficiency, reach, and cost constraints. The model is trained using real advertising data from the Sri Lankan market, ensuring practical relevance and applicability. Although the analysis is based on a country-specific dataset, the model is transferable to markets of similar scale. This study contributes to the literature by introducing an exposure-driven media mix modelling approach that improves media budget planning accuracy and supports more effective advertising decision-making.

title: Effectiveness of Capsule Networks in Detecting Deepfakes Instead of Traditional CNNs
abstract: As artificial intelligence has advanced, computer-generated fake content has become increasingly prevalent. Deepfake is an advanced fake creation generated using deep learning-based technologies, and deepfake images, videos, and voices have spread rapidly. The distinction between real and fake content is very hard for the naked eye, making reliable detection essential. Existing deepfake detection methods have achieved success, but still face limitations in keeping pace with the rapid evolution of deepfake generation techniques. In particular, CNN-based approaches may require a large number of parameters and may not fully capture spatial hierarchies. In this research, we investigate whether Capsule Networks can provide an effective and parameter-efficient alternative for deepfake detection. We proposed four different Capsule Network architectures by altering the size, complexity, and configuration. A comparative analysis is conducted against state-of-the-art Capsule models and CNN models across various datasets, utilizing AUC% and the number of parameters as evaluation criteria. For transparency, we note that some baseline CNN and Capsule models follow the training protocols and datasets reported in their original studies, which may differ across implementations. Our experimental results show that the proposed Capsule Network models achieved over 98% AUC% on the evaluated datasets while using fewer parameters than several CNN-based models. These findings suggest that Capsule Networks exhibit greater efficacy in detecting deepfakes compared to traditional CNN-based methods and represent a promising direction for future research.

title: Monolingual Transformer-Based Detection of Altered Profanity in Sinhala Facebook Comments
abstract: This study investigates the detection of deliberately obfuscated profanity in Sinhala Facebook comments, where users intentionally modify words to bypass keyword-based filters. To support this task, we created a novel, manually annotated dataset of 4,000 Facebook comments, representing the first comprehensive resource for Sinhala altered profanity. We evaluated two monolingual transformer models, SinBERT-small and SinBERT-large, for binary classification. SinBERT-large achieved a micro-averaged F1-score of 0.562 (Profanity F1: 0.671; Altered-speech F1: 0.387), while SinBERT-small scored 0.554 overall (Profanity F1: 0.658; Altered-speech F1: 0.387). Both models performed well in detecting direct profanity but struggled with altered speech, with identical F1-scores indicating that increasing model size alone does not improve performance without more diverse training data. In terms of efficiency, SinBERT-small processed 1,148.752 samples/second, while SinBERT-large processed 637.363 samples/second. These results demonstrate the value of language-specific models for low-resource languages, with SinBERT-large recommended for higher accuracy and SinBERT-small for real-time applications.

title: Machine Learning-Based Framework for Predicting Vehicle Arrival Times in Public Transport
abstract: This paper presents a machine learning-based framework for predicting vehicle arrival times when the origin and destination are not fixed. Several models were developed and evaluated, including Linear Regression, Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Decision Trees, and Random Forests. The dataset was constructed using data collected from public transportation in Sri Lankan routes at fixed intervals. Model performance was assessed using Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Among the models, Linear Regression exhibited the highest error, while Random Forest achieved the lowest error. The results demonstrate that the effectiveness of the models was directly influenced by both the data collection methodology and the choice of features. With further improvements in dataset quality and model design, the proposed framework has strong potential for practical deployment in applications where accurate vehicle arrival time prediction is critical, such as public transportation management and taxi services.

title: COMPARISON OF HEURISTIC SEARCH ALGORITHMS IN SOLVING 11-PUZZLE PROBLEMS
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of the A and Iterative Deepening A (IDA) search algorithms to solve the 11-puzzle problems using the Manhattan distance heuristic.Both algorithms were implemented and evaluated based on performance metrics including nodes generated, nodesexpanded, solution depth, effective branching factor, and CPU time. The results indicate that A consistently outperforms IDAin computational efficiency and scalability with A reducing the node generation by 62.86%, node expansion by 61.60%, and CPU time by 51.46%, though IDA* remains more memory efficient. These findings validate the broader applicability of heuristic search strategies and reinforce the role of the Manhattan distance heuristic in optimal path finding.

title: Enhancing Papaya Disease Detection using Deep Learning and Data Augmentation Techniques: A Case Study in Sri Lanka
abstract: All farmers, particularly fruit growers, must take plant disease seriously. A significant problem for large farms is the spread of diseases that make the fruits unfit for consumption, thereby negatively impacting the farmer’s income. In order to stop the spread of disease, farmers must discover it early in its life cycle. Traditional fruit disease detection and identification rely on a person’s ability to see the diseased fruit. Even though this approach may suffice for small-scale farmers, it requires a high skill level for accurate identification. Machine Learning and Image Processing techniques have been used in recent research to develop computerised solutions to this challenge. This study considers Papaya, a popular fruit in Sri Lanka which suffers from a high post-harvest losses. Anthracnose, black spot, powdery mildew, phytophthora, and ringspot were selected among various papaya fruit diseases. They were choosen because they are the most prevalent papaya diseases in Sri Lanka. Data were collected from public image sources from the internet and actual fields. VGG 16, as a Convolutional Neural Network technique, was used to develop a computerised model for detecting papaya diseases. However, due to insufficient data, most image-based disease recognition systems have some limitations. However, novel data augmentation methods have promising advantages in expanding the limited data. This approach used Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network (DCGAN) to expand the data set. The VGG 16 model accuracy was found using the same pre-processed data set with and without subjected to DCGAN. According to the results, the VGG 16 model has shown high accuracy across diseases. The resulting accuracy for Anthracnose, black spot, powdery mildew, phytophthora, and ringspot were 90%, 85%, 70%, 65% and 90%, respectively. The results indicate that the proposed DCGAN model performs better than basic techniques.

title: Analysing Public Perception and Sentiment on the COVID-19 Booster Dose through Social Media
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, has emerged as a severe public health crisis, reshaping societies worldwide since its inception in December 2019. Amidst these challenges, vaccination emerged as a pivotal strategy to curb transmission and restore normalcy. The journey to develop and distribute vaccines encountered obstacles but ultimately led to significant progress. Vaccine hesitancy persists, impacting the uptake of booster shots. Therefore, this research analyses the acceptance of booster shots by examining the tweets that reflect public perceptions. Over 12,000 tweets provided insights into public perceptions, highlighting the need for nuanced approaches to address vaccine hesitancy. Leveraging topic modelling algorithms such as Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), the study identified pertinent topics and keywords, shedding light on variations in booster shot acceptance across different income categories. It further analysed the public acceptance of booster shots using machine learning techniques like Support Vector Machines (SVM), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). The ANN algorithm outperformed the LSTM, which is known for it´s semantic understanding. Persistent vaccine hesitancy remains a formidable challenge in the battle against COVID-19. Middle-income countries admit to the booster shot compared to high-income countries.

title: PREDICTIVE MACHINE LEARNING FRAMEWORK FOR POTENTIAL DELAY
abstract: Delays relating to order deliveries in elastic manufacturing can significantly disrupt production timelines, affect supply chain efficiency, and diminish customer satisfaction. This research presents a machine learning-based framework to address these challenges by predicting manufacturing delays, explaining their underlying causes, and estimating delay durations to improve operational reliability. The study employs a three-layer architecture: a binary classification layer to predict whether an order delivery delay will occur, an explainability layer using Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) to provide insights into each prediction, and a regression layer to estimate the duration of the delay and the expected delayed delivery date. The dataset, spanning more than three years (from 2021-01-08 to 2024-06-24), includes 37,411 order records and 75,723 delivery records, reflecting the complexities of elastic manufacturing order fulfillment. Extensive data preparation was conducted to standardize formats, handle missing values, and normalize features. Classification models such as Logistic Regression, XGBoost, and Neural Networks were utilized for classification tasks, while Linear Regression and XGBRegressor were employed for regression tasks. The findings demonstrate that the proposed framework not only accurately predicts delays but also offers actionable insights into their drivers, enabling proactive decision-making. By integrating predictive power with explainability, this study contributes to the advancement of intelligent supply chain management systems.

title: REAL VS. FAKE FACE CLASSIFICATION USING DEEP LEARNING-BASED CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORKS
abstract: The widespread use of artificial intelligence (AI) has accelerated the creation of hyperrealistic synthetic images, commonly referred to as deepfakes. These AI-generated faces present growing challenges in domains such as security, media verification, and digital identity. This study presents a primary research effort that investigates the classification of real and AI-generated facial images using a deep learning-based convolutional neural network (CNN). Unlike previous works that solely rely on existing public datasets, this study integrates a curated set of AI-generated and real faces from Kaggle with a custom-collected image set to enhance dataset diversity and realism. The experimental CNN architecture was developed using the Keras Sequential API and consists of four convolutional layers with ReLU activation, four max-pooling layers, one batch normalization layer, dropout regularization, and two fully connected dense layers. The training process incorporated data augmentation techniques such as rescaling, shearing, zooming, and horizontal flipping to improve generalization and mitigate overfitting. The model was compiled using the Adam optimizer and binary cross-entropy loss, with accuracy used as the primary metric. The model was trained for 25 epochs, achieving a test accuracy of approximately 82% on the final evaluation. Performance metrics indicate high precision (83.08%) and recall (82.44%), as reflected in the classification report and confusion matrix. These results confirm the model's effectiveness in accurately differentiating between real and AI-generated faces. Model performance was monitored through training and validation curves, revealing consistent accuracy gains and manageable loss fluctuations. In addition to model training, feature map visualizations were generated to illustrate how the CNN processes facial structures across layers. The findings suggest that intermediate convolutional outputs successfully capture critical features like facial symmetry, edge clarity, and texture anomalies, which are typically absent or uniform in synthetic faces. The inclusion of a custom dataset and extended experimental controls, such as validation monitoring and architectural tuning, elevate this work from a secondary to a primary research contribution. This study highlights the practical application of CNNs in deepfake detection and proposes future extensions to real-time video classification and architectural comparisons involving ensemble or transfer learning models.

title: ROBOTICS FOR SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE: OPPORTUNITIES AND OBSTACLES
abstract: Robotics has emerged as a transformative force in modern agriculture, addressing key challenges such as labor shortages, environmental sustainability, and resource optimization. This review presents an overview of current advancements in agricultural robotics, encompassing ground-based robots, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and autonomous tractors. Empirical evidence highlights significant gains, including herbicide reduction of up to 85%, weeding efficiencies exceeding 90%, and harvesting success rates of 75-90% for various crops. UAVs have improved early disease detection by 40%, while artificial intelligence (AI)-based weed identification achieved an F-score of 0.9843. Despite these promising results, most systems remain in prototype or field-testing stages, constrained by high costs ranging from US$50,000-US$120,000 and technical limitations in perception, navigation, and integration. This review systematically synthesizes existing literature to assess applications, technological capabilities, performance outcomes, and barriers to adoption, providing key insights into the future of robotics in agriculture.

title: THE USE OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR SELF-LEARNING IN UNIVERSITY STUDENTS
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence is promptly evolving, reshaping various perspectives of university academia. Therefore, it is necessary to understand how these tools are involved in study habits. This systematic review integrates the existing research on using Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) for self-learning in university students for their academic work. The main objectives of this review are to explore how students engage with generative AI tools to support independent learning processes, including content creation, problem-solving, and augmenting previous knowledge acquisition. It seeks to quantify the perceived advantages of using these technologies, particularly in personalized learning experiences, productivity gains, and overall ease of use. Furthermore, the research addresses the limitations and challenges of applying generative AI, such as those about accuracy issues, possible overdependence, ethical and moral factors that may arise when utilizing it in independent learning settings. To assess the impact of generative AI on students' critical thinking, creativity, and independent problem-solving skills. Using a systematic search of research papers [since 2024], we analyzed reported applications, benefits, challenges, and disadvantages regarding the above-mentioned theme. Mainly included individualized tutoring, self-researching, content creation, and writing assistance with benefits. As well as talking about disadvantages such as how AI affects critical thinking, plagiarism, and privacy concerns. Quantitative qualitative, and mixed-method research published in English exploring the Generative AI use for self-studying. The review involved 10 research studies comprising 2,608 individuals from several state universities. The findings clarify the need to develop students' AI literacy and clear university policies to ensure the use of those powerful tools is ethical and responsible.

title: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW OF EVALUATING THE ACCURACY OF NVIVO, R, AND LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS IN THEMATIC ANALYSIS OF INTERVIEW DATA: A COMPARATIVE STUDY
abstract: In response to the growing integration of computational tools in qualitative research, this study presents a systematic comparison of three widely adopted approaches for conducting thematic analysis on qualitative interview data: NVivo (proprietary), R-based text analysis packages (open source), and Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT. Thematic analysis remains a cornerstone of qualitative inquiry, and with increasing reliance on automated methods, it is essential to understand how accurately these tools replicate the depth, nuance, and contextual sensitivity of human-coded analysis. Interview transcripts, selected for their richness in expression and detail, provide a robust dataset for comparative evaluation. Manual thematic coding, grounded in Braun and Clarke's six-phase framework, is employed as the gold standard. Each tool then independently analyzes the same dataset to extract themes and patterns. The resulting outputs are assessed using established metrics such as Precision, Recall, F1 Score, and Thematic Overlap, which quantitatively capture the degree of alignment with the human-coded reference. This evaluation aims not only to identify the comparative strengths and weaknesses of each tool but also to highlight the contexts in which specific tools may be most effective or limited. Moreover, the study delves into the potential of hybrid approaches that combine human judgment with machine-driven analysis to improve both accuracy and efficiency. By systematically mapping the capabilities and limitations of these tools, the research provides valuable, evidence-based guidance for researchers and practitioners navigating the evolving domain of AI-supported qualitative analysis. The findings are intended to support more informed tool selection and promote the thoughtful integration of computational methods into human-centered research workflows.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Employee Well-Being: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming modern workplaces by offering opportunities to enhance employee well-being while simultaneously introducing significant challenges. Although scholarly interest in the intersection of AI and well-being is growing, empirical research in this domain remains limited and underdeveloped. This study's primary objective was to assess the current knowledge in this domain, with a secondary aim of identifying critical research gaps to inform future investigations. Adhering to PRISMA guidelines, this systematic literature review analysed 23 empirical studies published between 2015 and 2025, sourced from the Lens.org and ProQuest databases and was guided by the Job Demands Resources (JD–R) model. Keyword co-occurrence analysis using VOSviewer revealed five dominant themes: (1) Tech-induced stress, (2) AI-driven success, (3) Mental resilience, (4) Digital boundaries, and (5) Emotional wellness. The density visualisation map highlighted significant gaps in the existing literature. Despite increasing scholarly attention, the review reveals that significant empirical gaps still remain in the literature. By synthesising current knowledge and identifying critical research gaps, this review offers practical insights for developing human-centred AI strategies and establishes a research agenda for advancing employee well-being in increasingly digital workplaces.

title: Panelformer: An Enhanced Temporal Fusion Transformer for Robust Panel Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Panel time series forecasting presents unique challenges due to the heterogeneity of panel datasets, where existing models fail to perform consistently across diverse panel data characteristics. While the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) has proven effective for univariate and multivariate time series, it exhibits critical limitations when applied to panel data: its standard attention mechanisms struggle to capture localized temporal patterns, it lacks mechanisms for modeling interentity dependencies, and it processes all temporal information through a single pathway that may overlook important trendseasonal distinctions. To address these limitations, we propose Panelformer, a unified architecture that enhances TFT with five key innovations: (1) segment-wise attention for localized temporal pattern extraction, (2) cross-entity attention to model inter-entity dependencies, (3) multi-scale decomposition to isolate trend and seasonal components, (4) parallel processing paths for independent feature learning, and (5) adaptive weighting to dynamically prioritize trend or seasonal signals. Through comprehensive evaluation across 11 diverse datasets representing eight distinct panel type combinations, Panelformer achieves a 7.99% average improvement in Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) over the baseline TFT, demonstrating superior performance on 9 of 11 datasets while revealing specific challenges in volatile or sparse datasets.

title: GlioMap: MATLAB-based GUI for MRI Brain Tumor Segmentation and Feature Extraction
abstract: GlioMap is an open-source, MATLAB-based software designed for brain tumor segmentation and standardized feature extraction from MRI images. The software provides an interactive graphical user interface (GUI) that integrates preprocessing, skull stripping, semi-automatic segmentation, tumor masking, and both radiomic and morphological feature calculation. Unlike general-purpose imaging platforms, GlioMap is lightweight and accessible, reducing the technical barriers for students, clinicians, and researchers without programming expertise. A key contribution of GlioMap is its emphasis on reproducibility: all 100 radiomic and 33 morphological features are compliant with the Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative (IBSI) [1], ensuring consistency across studies and machine learning pipelines. Outputs, including tumor masks and feature spreadsheets, can be readily exported for integration into clinical research workflows or classification models. By combining accessibility with standardized radiomic analysis, GlioMap provides a practical and reproducible tool for advancing automated clinical decision-support in neuro-oncology.

title: Can Chatbots Advance Participatory Disaster Risk Reduction for Sustainable Development and Resilient Human Settlement? A Systematic Review With Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly used as a community engagement tool, yet their contribution to participatory disaster risk reduction (DRR) and sustainable development remains unclear. This study synthesises the state of knowledge on chatbots for participatory DRR and assesses how the evidence aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 11 (sustainable cities and communities), SDG 13 (climate action) and SDG 16 (inclusive institutions). Following PRISMA guidelines, 57 peer‐reviewed studies were selected from major academic databases. The synthesis reveals rapid growth of interest but limited rigorous evaluation of outcomes that matter for risk reduction and sustainable development, such as protective actions taken, long‐term mitigation, inclusion of marginalised groups, hybrid architecture integration and governance, including data stewardship and integration with local institutions. Findings reveal that chatbots are methodologically fragmented, reflecting limited integration between technology and disaster domains and minimal engagement with end users. By consolidating fragmented evidence and highlighting gaps, the review clarifies where chatbots can add value to people‐centred, participatory DRR.

title: Autopoietic Computing and the Emergence ofSentience in Brain Organoids
abstract: Contemporarybiocomputingoftenapproachesbrainorganoidsasallopoieticsub-strates for logical processing, neglecting the existential imperatives that drive biolog-ical cognition. This paper proposes a fundamental paradigm shift from AllopoieticComputing toward Autopoietic Computing, grounding the emergence of sentiencein the thermodynamic necessity of survival. By integrating the Mortal Computingparadigm, where computational software is physically indissociable from its degrad-able biological hardware, with the causal hierarchy of consciousness proposed byBennett et al., we investigate the theoretical and computational feasibility of sen-tience as a recursive strategy for energy optimization. We developed and analyzeda high fidelity digital twin of an Autopoietic Chamber using the Brian2 simulator,implementing a virtual metabolism where neural activity directly regulates nutrientaccess. Our simulation results demonstrate a clear progression from the entropiccollapse of reactive matter, Stage 0, to the stabilization of phenomenal, Stage 1, so-cial, Stage 2, and narrative, Stage 3, functional identities. These findings provide apredictive proof of concept indicating that each higher order of consciousness acts asa thermodynamic filter, minimizing metabolic dissipation through increasingly com-plex causal modeling. We argue that sentience is not a byproduct of complexity buta necessary compromise with thermodynamic economy, providing a new empiricaland computational roadmap for the science of consciousness and the developmentof mortal, sentient artificial agents.
