title: A Unified AI-Integrated Adaptive Learning Framework for Personalized Education in Blended Learning Environments
abstract: Personalized education has become a critical requirement in modern digital learning environments, as learners exhibit diverse abilities, learning speeds, and preferences. Traditional blended learning systems often rely on static content delivery approaches, limiting their ability to respond to individual learner needs. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an AI-integrated adaptive learning framework that dynamically personalizes learning pathways based on learner behavior, academic performance, and engagement patterns. The proposed framework leverages machine learning techniques to construct learner profiles, predict learning performance, and recommend adaptive content in near real time using pre-trained models. Experimental evaluation was conducted using real student interaction data collected from a blended learning environment. The results show that the proposed framework achieves a performance prediction accuracy of 86.9%, compared to 78.4% in a non-adaptive baseline (an improvement of 8.5 percentage points, i.e., 10.8% relative gain). In addition, learners in the adaptive condition achieved higher average assessment scores (71.5 vs. 62.3) and a higher course completion rate (83.6% vs. 74.1%), along with improved engagement behavior. These findings demonstrate the utility of the proposed framework in enhancing personalization accuracy and learning outcomes in mixed education environments.

title: Enhancing Mobile Security through Robust Smishing Detection Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
abstract: Social Engineering is a compromising method that manipulates victims from their psychology rather than manipulating them technically. Smishing, phishing, and vishing can be identified as primary social manipulation techniques. These techniques differ due to the content delivery method. To deliver the content, smishing uses SMSs, phishing uses Emails, and vishing uses voice calls. The danger of the smishing and phishing content is that it can include some malicious links that direct to malicious websites and asking about user credentials, rather than compared with vishing attacks. From these smishing and phishing content delivery methods, most of the population is familiar with the smishing delivery of SMSs on mobile devices. Therefore, preventing smishing attacks to enhance mobile security is a requirement in the current era. The current AIbased studies have used small datasets to detect smishing attacks. The proposed study has combined four publicly available datasets and created a 27,585 -sized dataset to overcome the gap. In addition to that, the study has used three approaches, including machine learning algorithms with the TF-IDF approach, machine learning algorithms with the Word2Vec approach, and the deep learning algorithm approach. There are five machine learning and five deep learning algorithms used in these three approaches, including Logistic Regression (LR), Naïve Bayes (NB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost (XGB), CNNBiGRU, RNN, CNN-LSTM, CNN-BERT, and DistilBERT. From these algorithms, the lightweight deep learning algorithm 'DistilBERT' has achieved the highest accuracy and recall score of 98.33% and 98.21%, respectively, with a quite minimal average inference time of$\mathbf{141. 79 ~ ms}$, average CPU utilization of 52.74%, and average main memory utilization of 0.01 MB to predict the results.

title: Lightweight Unified Network for Low-Light Image Enhancement and Sri Lankan Traditional Mask Classification
abstract: Low-light conditions present a significant challenge to high-level computer vision tasks such as image classification, often causing substantial performance degradation. This paper addresses this limitation by introducing the Adaptive Low-Light Classification Network (Mask-Net), a hybrid architecture designed for robust classification of Sri Lankan traditional masks under varying illumination. Mask-Net integrates a learnable illumination detection mechanism that selectively enhances images identified as low-light by the model, rather than relying on manually labeled illumination, combined with a MobileNetV3-small backbone for classification. This selective enhancement improves computational efficiency and prevents artifacts in normally illuminated images. The training pipeline incorporates weighted random sampling and dynamic class weighting to mitigate class imbalance and improve recall for underrepresented classes. Experimental results demonstrate that Mask-Net achieves high and stable classification performance on the test set and significantly outperforms conventional models in challenging low-light environments. This work contributes a practical and effective solution to a critical gap in hybrid low-light vision systems.

title: An Intelligent Hybrid Framework for Early Deadlock Detection in Distributed Systems Using Markov Models, Machine Learning, and Distributed Consensus
abstract: This paper presents a holistic proactive deadlock detection framework for distributed systems, such as cloud platforms, distributed databases, microservice based architectures. The proposed framework incorporates Markov based probabilistic modeling, ensemble machine learning, and multi-layer distributed consensus in order to allow predictive deadlock detection before system halt, instead of reactive identification after deadlock formation. A Markov model is used for estimating deadlock probability and Mean Time to Deadlock (MTTD), while analytically derived features are combined with ensemble machine learning models to enhance the accuracy of classification. To guarantee a system-wide reliable validation, a distributed consensus mechanism combines node-level predictions using a supermajority agreement strategy. Experimental evaluation on a largescale simulated data set with 21 system features shows that the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid framework is 93.33% accuracy, representing an absolute improvement of 5% compared to the best performing standalone model (XGB), while reducing both false positives (precision 92.86%) and false negatives (recall 90.00%).

title: Metadata-Driven RAG Architecture for Context-Aware University Information Retrieval
abstract: General-purpose Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently produce generic or hallucinated responses when addressing university-specific queries, as they lack personalization aligned with individual student contexts. This paper proposes an enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system that incorporates university ontology with rule-based metadata filtering to generate personalized and accurate responses tailored to students' academic profiles. The system integrates student metadata, such as batch, department, degree program, and academic year with institutional hierarchy modelling to filter and prioritize retrieved documents prior to response generation. The enhancement is driven by two core mechanisms: metadata-based filtering removes contextually irrelevant documents based on student profiles and document attributes, while ontology-driven prioritization ranks information sources according to institutional authority structures and temporal relevance. The system was evaluated using a diverse set of academic and non-academic queries from the University of Kelaniya, where it consistently outperformed the baseline RAG model across all evaluation metrics. Retrieval precision and recall showed notable improvements, answer generation quality increased substantially, and human assessments indicated significant gains in factual accuracy, relevance, and completeness, with lower hallucinations. Overall, the findings demonstrate that the integration of domain-specific ontological knowledge with metadata-driven filtering markedly improves RAG performance in educational settings, offering a scalable approach for context-aware academic support systems.

title: Unsupervised Phishing Campaign Discovery Using BERT-Based URL Embeddings and Clustering Algorithms
abstract: Despite the significant improvement in cybersecurity defenses, phishing remains one of the most enduring and destructive forms of cyber threats across the globe. The attackers continuously adapt and refine their tactics by utilizing short-lived domains, obfuscated URL paths, and polymorphic infrastructure in order to evade the typical detection mechanisms. Conventional supervised methods for phishing detection heavily rely on labeled datasets and handcrafted features, which decreases their efficiency against zero-day attacks and newly emerging phishing campaigns. This paper proposes a new, fully unsupervised phishing campaign discovery framework that employs clustering of URLs based on deep transformer-based embeddings generated by the URLBERT model. The proposed method encodes URLs as high-dimensional semantic vectors without any manual feature engineering in terms of structural, lexical, and contextual properties. These vectors undergo normalization and clustering through the K-Means algorithm with the number of clusters automatically determined using Silhouette analysis over a broad range of values. To make it useful for interpretative analysis as well as threat analysis, the clusters obtained are transformed into two-dimensional vectors through Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) techniques. The results obtained through experimentation on the large phishing URL dataset have been found to outline the effectiveness of the proposed framework in detecting semantic phishing campaigns and attack patterns without any overhead of labeled data. The results outline the promise of transformer-based unsupervised learning approaches in the field of proactive phishing analysis.

title: A Lightweight Incremental Learning Framework for Tomato Leaf Disease Detection in Dynamic Field Deployments
abstract: Effective deployment of deep learning models for plant disease detection in dynamic agricultural environments demands adaptive frameworks that can seamlessly integrate newly emerging disease categories without the need for computationally expensive retraining. This study proposes a lightweight Class Incremental Learning framework for tomato leaf disease detection, to deploy in dynamic real-world agricultural environments, where novel disease classes can emerge over time as a result of seasonal shifts, pathogen evolution, climate variability, and heterogeneous farming practices. Unlike conventional incremental learning approaches that rely on model fine-tuning and heavy computations, the proposed framework enables efficient knowledge expansion with computationally inexpensive and suitable for resource-constrained environments. The framework employs exemplar rehearsal and prototype-based classification to preserve previously learned knowledge while effectively incorporating new disease classes using only a limited number of samples. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method maintains competitive performance with average accuracies of 99.10%, 89.68%, 87.02%, and 86.39% across incremental tasks, while reducing training time by over 95% and data requirements by approximately 98% compared to full retraining. Moreover, controlled forgetting behavior, with most classes exhibiting low forgetting rates around 5%, confirms the framework's ability to effectively balance knowledge retention and adaptability. Further evaluation of the framework will be done using real-world field data, along with its extension to a broader range of disease categories and incremental learning tasks.

title: Emotion Detection and Automated Suggestion Generation from Student Feedback Using a Deep Learning-Based Framework
abstract: Student feedback is a vital resource for enhancing educational quality, yet traditional sentiment analysis techniques often fail to capture the nuanced emotional states embedded within learner narratives. This study proposes a deep learning-based framework that not only detects fine-grained emotions from diverse student feedback, including handwritten and digital sources, but also generates automated, contextsensitive pedagogical suggestions to inform course improvement. Leveraging transformer architectures, BERT and DistilBERT were fine-tuned for multi-label emotion classification, with DistilBERT achieving superior performance (macro-F1: 0.8235, accuracy: 93.26%) while offering reduced computational complexity. Additionally, a Flan-T5 model was employed to generate actionable improvement suggestions, achieving promising BLEU and ROUGE-L scores that reflect alignment with expert-curated feedback. Threshold optimization and per-class performance analyses further elucidate model strengths and limitations, particularly regarding ambiguous emotion categories. The results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating emotion-aware NLP with suggestion generation to close the feedback loop between students and educators, thereby advancing the application of AI for personalized educational enhancement.

title: Design of a Personalized AI-Powered Flutter UI Learning System Integrating Computer Vision, RAG, and LSTM
abstract: Mobile application development with Flutter is growing rapidly, yet beginners struggle to translate UI designs into functional code. Existing educational resources and AI tools often focus on isolated widgets or automated code generation, lacking contextual guidance and pedagogical reasoning. To address these gaps, this research proposes a learning platform that integrates multimodal AI for UI understanding, RetrievalAugmented Generation (RAG) for personalized instructional content, and sequential learning analytics (LSTM) for adaptive progress tracking. The system analyzes Figma-based UI designs, mapping visual components to Flutter widgets while providing conceptually grounded explanations. Personalized learning paths are generated using RAG, adapting content depth, pacing, and modality to learner needs. LSTM models monitor interactions, predict knowledge gaps, and recommend targeted interventions. Validation through surveys (N=49) and expert review demonstrates feasibility, alignment with learner needs, and potential improvements in learning efficiency, accuracy, retention, and engagement. Comparative analysis shows the design surpasses existing tools by combining visual analysis, adaptive instruction, progress tracking, and mobile-first accessibility. By unifying visual reasoning, personalized content, and longitudinal analytics, the platform supports scaffolded learning, proactive intervention, and scalable deployment, providing a novel approach to bridging the gap between design and implementation in Flutter education.

title: “GANITHA MITHURA” A Closed-Loop Adaptive Artificial Intelligence and Augmented Reality Framework for Multisensory Early Mathematics Learning
abstract: Early mathematics education plays a critical role in children's intellectual development. However, many students struggle to build strong conceptual foundations through traditional teaching methods. This paper presents GANITHA MITHURA, an integrated multisensory early mathematics learning system that leverages Augmented Reality (AR) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) within a closed-loop adaptive learning framework. The system consists of four main components: number sense development, adaptive arithmetic learning, geometry-based spatial reasoning, and experiential learning through real-world interactions. The system includes an AI-driven adaptive engine that analyzes learner behavior, identifies conceptual gaps, and dynamically adjusts teaching strategies. GANITHA MITHURA uses hybrid AI models to observe learner interactions, provide personalized instruction, and adjust learning paths in real time. This approach improves early mathematics learning by promoting conceptual understanding, increasing student engagement, and providing personalized learning experiences.

title: A Statistical Analysis on ChatGPT's Evaluation Bias on Handwritten Diagram Based Exam Scripts
abstract: AI has revolutionized almost all fields including education ensuring superior efficiency by streamlining processes. This study aims to investigate possibility of utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs) for assessment/exam scripts evaluation by the educators especially for handwritten diagrambased scripts. 120 handwritten answer scripts which were expected to provide a diagram-based response were utilized. Each script was graded for its concept awareness and clarity of the response by both human evaluators and ChatGPT 5.2 model. ChatGPT was prompted 120 times with the question, marking rubric and the scanned handwritten student's answer script. Statistical analysis including descriptive statistics, score difference analysis, paired t-tests, effect size measurement and correlation analysis bought very meaningful insight into ChatGPT's evaluations. The results highlight the need for a hybrid framework that encourage human-in -the-loop. Because results revealed that ChatGPT significantly ($\mathbf{p}<\mathbf{0. 0 5}$) over grade than human especially for the explanatory components including diagrams. The results indicate that ChatGPT applies a relatively lower penalization when key components, procedural steps, or explanations are missing. The study provides statistical evidence to the fact that the abovementioned over grading is script specific, not consistent with the same amount. Furthermore, the effect of the over grading results in a risk of grade inflation for overall grade although the effect on individual components is not trivial.

title: An Integrated and Explainable Framework for Type II Diabetes Risk Prediction, Severity Quantification, and Treatment Recommendation
abstract: Type II diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has affected over 830 million people worldwide, making it difficult for risk detection, accurate severity stratification and appropriate treatment recommendation, making effective disease management very crucial yet critical. Existing studies often focus on one aspect, such as risk prediction, severity assessment, or treatment recommendation, thereby limiting clinical usefulness and interpretability. By bridging this existing gap, this study proposes an integrated, explainable framework for the above-mentioned three aspects using population-scale data from the National Health and Nutrition Survey (NHANES) spanning from 1988 to 2018. First, a multi-factor diabetes risk prediction model is developed using LightGBM, integrating 43 attributes, selecting laboratory and lifestyle features through a multi- algorithm feature importance approach. Then, a novel multidimensional Diabetes Severity Index (DSI) and Mortality Weighted Diabetes Severity Index (DSI-MW) are developed to measure the severity of Diabetes Type II patients. Finally, a rule-based, explainable expert system for pharmacological treatment recommendation was developed, referring to the clinical guidelines provided by the American Diabetes Association Standards of Care (ADA). Overall, the entire system acts as an end-to-end explainable clinical decision support system for T2DM, providing strong support for early detection, severity quantification and personalised treatment planning while making this system a standout solution among the existing systems in this field of study.

title: Real Time Sinhala Lecture Transcription for Political Science
abstract: This research aims to develop an optimized automatic speech recognition system for transcribing Sinhala language lectures in the subject of Political Science. Current Automatic Speech Recognition systems, designed to work with any type of audio, often do not perform well in capturing domain-specific vocabulary; therefore, the models currently available will not provide robust transcription for lectures presented in the field of Political Science. The research executed a comparison study of Automatic Speech Recognition frameworks and chose the Wav2Vec2-XLS-R-300M model as the reference point because of its good equilibrium of precision and computational efficiency on CPU hardware. A significant gap in performance was identified when comparing the model's results to a domain-specific dataset, leading to a multi-staged improvement effort to close that gap. This approach consisted of adjusting the acoustic model for a specific Political Science dataset along with the addition of a 5-gram KenLM language model for phonetic error correction as a result of decoding. Following thorough refinement of the system's decoding parameters and the configuration for beam search, the system's transcription accuracy increased significantly. Ultimately, the final optimized system produced an average Word Error Rate of approximately 10.58% and an average Real Time Factor of 0.85, indicating that this Automatic Speech Recognition system is suitable for use in live academic environments.

title: Scalable and Efficient Traffic Classification in Software-Defined Networks Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Traffic classification in software-defined networking (SDN) is essential for enabling intelligent control and efficient utilization of network resources. This study explores the application of machine learning methods to improve traffic classification within SDN environments, with particular attention to scalability and performance. Machine learning models can effectively and efficiently recognize traffic patterns by utilizing flow-level features such as flow duration, packet count, and other related metrics, thereby improving network management. Incorporating machine learning into traffic classification addresses the shortcomings of traditional rule-based or port-based techniques, especially when handling encrypted or complex traffic. Our proposed machine learning methods are implemented using Mininet topologies, and the results demonstrate notable enhancements in resource allocation, reduced latency, and improved quality of service. Our empirical results indicate that incorporating machine learning techniques into network traffic classification can support scalable and intelligent software-defined networking frameworks that are capable of handling dynamic high-volume network environments.

title: Hybrid Sarima-XGBoost Framework for Sri Lankan Apparel Exports Using Social Media Sentiment
abstract: The inherent characteristics of the export performance in developing economies are of structural volatility, nonlinear market behaviour, and increased sensitivity to market perception, which makes the forecasting of export performance difficult. Traditional econometric models are suitable to long-term structural processes but fail to respond to sudden regime changes, whereas machine-learning methods are more flexible but require a lot of feature engineering and prone to instability when trained on small macroeconomic data sets. In this regard, this paper presents a hybrid forecasting system that unites econometric modelling, machine-learning procedures and sentiment analysis of social media to predict the performance of the Sri Lankan apparel export business in a variety of time frames. A custom dataset was created through a combination of monthly export and macroeconomic measures with domain specific sentiment using$\mathbf{X}$(Twitter). The model combines a Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average model to capture structural elements and Extreme Gradient Boosting model to represent nonlinear dynamics of residual component. Empirical evaluation combining fixed-window testing and rolling-origin cross-validation shows that the hybrid model achieves a root mean squared error of about 25, which is a reduction of almost 40% off a seasonal naive model. The least forecasting error of sentiment enhanced hybrid model, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) 21.09 is achieved at medium-to-long horizon. Findings also indicate that the socialmedia sentiment contributes primarily to the accuracy in the medium and long-term forecast but can have limited value in the short-run forecasts. Taken together, these results highlight the strength of the hybrid structures as well as provide fresh empirical insights into the horizon-sensitive impact of digital sentiment in the export-oriented economies.

title: Inclusive Multimodal Fraud Detection for Differently Abled Users in Digital Banking
abstract: AI-driven fraud detection systems in digital banking commonly assume uniform user behavior, often overlooking accessibility-driven interaction patterns, thereby disadvantaging differently abled users, senior citizens, and other vulnerable populations. This study proposes an Inclusive Multimodal Fraud Detection (IMFD) framework that integrates accessibility-aware signals, including voice biometrics, screen reader navigation behavior, haptic interaction patterns, and eye-tracking data, into a hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture with attention-based multimodal fusion. The framework was evaluated using a mixed-methods approach that combined simulated banking environments, public fraud datasets, and controlled user trials involving differently abled participants. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an overall accuracy of 96% under cross-validated settings, while significantly reducing false-positive fraud alerts for vulnerable user groups and maintaining a low-latency real-time performance. Embedded explainability, implemented through attention mechanisms and SHAP-based feature attribution, provides transparent and interpretable fraud decisions, supporting regulatory alignment with accessibility and data-protection standards. By explicitly modeling assistive interaction behaviors rather than treating them as anomalies, this study demonstrates how inclusive and explainable AI can enable secure, equitable, and scalable fraud detection in digital banking systems.

title: Transparent Quality Assurance for Low-Code/No-Code Workflows via Explainable AI and Automated Test Generation
abstract: Low-code/no-code (LC/NC) platforms speed up application delivery through visual workflows and reusable components, but their abstraction and limited observability make rigorous quality assurance challenging, especially for boundary conditions, exception handling, and stakeholder-friendly defect diagnosis. This paper presents an AI-driven Explainable Testing Framework for systematic and transparent validation of LC/NC workflows without relying on traditional source-code-centric methods. The framework (i) extracts visual workflow logic into a platform-neutral intermediate representation, (ii) automatically generates and executes functional, boundary, and exception-oriented test cases for comprehensive path exploration, and (iii) converts execution traces into multi-modal explanations using an explainable AI reasoning engine and role-specific interfaces for citizen developers, QA engineers, and executives. A prototype implemented on Microsoft PowerApps workflows shows strong extraction reliability across$N=147$workflows and generates an average of 24 test cases per workflow while reducing redundant executions. The explainability module also achieves high-quality results in readability, trace fidelity, decision-point coverage, and workflow-to-visual correspondence, helping stakeholders understand not only what failed, but why. Comparative evaluation against manual and baseline scripted validation shows better defect detection, lower testing and resolution time, and improved stakeholder understanding. Overall, the approach strengthens LC/NC quality assurance by combining automated rigor with stakeholder-oriented transparency, supporting governance-aligned adoption of citizen-developed workflows in enterprise settings. In doing so, it helps bridge the gap between automated workflow validation and stakeholder interpretability, enabling more evidence-driven release readiness in LC/NC systems.

title: Class-Wise Streaming for Detecting Minority Class Drift in Machine Learning Classifiers
abstract: Timely and effective detection of concept drift is essential for maintaining machine learning model performance in non-stationary environments. Among these models, classification systems are the most prevalent, and they often face a unique challenge: class imbalance. Typically, the minority class is not only underrepresented but also the most critical to predict accurately, as misclassifications of the minority class can lead to severe consequences.For example, in cancer detection, malignant cases are both rare and vital to identify. Therefore, it is crucial to pay special attention to drifts affecting the minority class. Despite this, most existing drift detection methods overlook changes affecting only the minority class, and this challenge remains largely underexplored in current research. To address this gap, we propose a heuristic methodology that can be applied to any existing concept drift detector through class-wise streaming.Our experiments show that in 84.26% of all evaluations, our method either outperformed or matched the performance of the conventional approach.Through this, we offer an important initial step toward a practical approach for improving the efficiency of drift detection, particularly when the drift occurs in the minority class.

title: Marker Based Human Following Robot Using Deep Learning Object Detection for Assistive Load Transportation
abstract: The next generation human following robot is the answer to a solution of autonomy in the field of assistive robots in healthcare, logistics, and the public service sector, but current systems suffer from limitations in both computational efficiency and the stability of tracking in a crowd setting. This paper presents a visual marker-based tracking system of an autonomous load carrying mobile robot that uses a custom trained YOLOv8 deep neural network to identify a unique red circular marker on the user, allowing it to perform effective human following behavior with real time performance at resource constrained embedded hardware. In contrast to the traditional full body human detection methods, the suggested marker based system allows for greatly reducing the high calculation burden and removing target confusion in the multi person scene. The system combines computer vision and multi sensor fusion, incorporating infrared sensors, to be able to avoid dynamic obstacles and navigate safely. The robot uses a Raspberry Pi 5 platform with a 720p web camera and can accurately detect markers with a precision of 98.8%, a Recall of 92.2%, and a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 97.1%, and can also perform real time inference at 28-32 milliseconds per frame. The lightweight and aluminum body allows it to carry loads of up to 15 kg and have stable autonomous mobility. Extensive experimental testing in diverse indoor environments demonstrates that our system is more consistent in tracking than old conventional human detection techniques, especially when dealing with full crowds, as the marker based system can ensure no false positives. The vertical-line-based tracking algorithm ensures smooth path following with dynamic maintenance of distance, and the$A$path Planning algorithm provides efficient obstacle avoidance in real time. The study provides an efficient and cost effective solution to assistive robotics by showing the empirical feasibility of marker based visual servoing of human following in dynamic real life settings.

title: Adaptive Personalized Multi-Task Federated Learning for Non-IID Diabetic Comorbidity Prediction
abstract: Federated learning (FL) has emerged as the requisite standard for privacy-preserving healthcare AI, supplanting traditional centralized models. However, standard FL approaches often fail to consider the non-IID nature of clinical data and the need to predict multiple comorbidities simultaneously. This work presents a Personalized Multi-Task Federated Learning (MTFL) framework for diabetes management. In this system, a shared-bottom neural architecture is utilized with three different task heads: Hypertension Detection, Heart Failure Prediction, and Comorbidity Risk Clustering. Unlike clustering-based personalization, our approach utilizes Federated Representation Learning (FedRep) via selective layer freezing. To tackle non-IID heterogeneity, we adopt a strategy of: (1) Global Aggregation (2) Local Adaptation, where clients freeze the shared feature extractor and fine-tune only task-specific heads and (3) Integrated Privacy Simulation via gradient clipping and noise injection. On the Diabetes 130-US Hospitals dataset, this framework results in a final personalized accuracy of 65.6%, a Heart Failure AUROC of 0.794, and a Comorbidity Cluster Macro-F1 score of 0.454. Personalization analysis demonstrates a massive immediate 30.14% relative accuracy improvement within the cold-start phase, validating the architecture's adaptability. Furthermore, we address communication efficiency by leveraging hard-parameter sharing, reducing model transmission overhead by 66.6% compared to deploying independent single-task baselines. Finally, we report a minimized demographic parity gap of 1.20 percentage points, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed framework in ensuring equitable AI deployment.

title: A Feedback-Driven Machine Learning Framework for Teaching Mode Decision Support in Higher Education Using Module Characteristics
abstract: The post-pandemic expansion of online and blended learning has intensified the need for systematic decision-support mechanisms in higher education. Universities are increasingly required to determine appropriate teaching modes for academic modules while balancing student engagement, pedagogical effectiveness, and resource constraints. However, delivery-mode decisions are often guided by intuition or retrospective evaluations rather than structured, data-driven analysis. This study presents a feedback-driven machine learning framework designed to support teachingmode decision making in higher education. The framework integrates comparative student feedback with structured module characteristics to provide advisory recommendations on whether a module is more aligned with online or physical delivery. A dataset comprising 245 undergraduate survey responses across 32 academic modules was analyzed, incorporating pedagogical variables such as module type, credit count, interaction level, assessment type, semester, and academic year. Supervised learning models, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost, were evaluated. Experimental results indicate that module-level pedagogical characteristics contribute meaningfully to differentiating teaching-mode suitability, with the XGBoost model demonstrating the strongest overall performance (Accuracy$=63.3 \%$, Macro-F1$=0.58$, AUC$=0.63$). Rather than emphasizing predictive accuracy as a standalone objective, the study positions machine learning as a decision-support tool that complements academic planning processes. The proposed framework enables transparent, feedback-informed, and context-sensitive teaching-mode planning, particularly relevant for resource-constrained higher education systems.

title: Ontology-Driven Framework for Knowledge Graph Construction from Multimodal Wildfire Data
abstract: Wildfires are increasingly spreading worldwide, posing severe environmental, economic, and societal challenges. Most existing wildfire screening systems rely primarily on unimodal data sources, limiting their ability to capture the complex, dynamic nature of wildfire events. Therefore, recent research has shifted toward integrating multimodal data to achieve richer situational awareness. Ontologies play a crucial role in this context by enabling semantic representation, integration, and reasoning over heterogeneous data. This study proposes Forest-Fire Ontology (FFOnto), a novel wildfire ontology developed using the Networked Ontologies (NeOn) and the On-To-Knowledge Methodology (OTKM) to support the semantic integration of multimodal data. This includes data from image, audio, and tabular sources. Prior to ontology instantiation, relevant features are extracted from image and audio data and then semantically represented using FFOnto. FFOnto is structured around the ForestFire class, complemented by modules for fire characteristics, fire management, multimodal observation, and related components. Evaluation of the ontology focused on main tree ways such as technology-focused evaluation, user-focused evaluation and formal evaluation of ontology. A multimodal wildfire knowledge graph (KG) is constructed and managed using GraphDB. To facilitate knowledge access, SPARQL Protocol and Resource Description Framework (RDF) Query Language (SPARQL) is used to query the KG, and a natural language (NL)–to–SPARQL mechanism is implemented to enable intuitive querying through NL questions. Experimental results show that the proposed system successfully supports NL querying over a multimodal wildfire KG, enabling effective retrieval of integrated wildfire knowledge. The future of this study lies in integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) and agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) for autonomous decision-making.

title: Explainable Writer Verification with Autoencoders, Feature Fusion, and LLM-Based Explanations
abstract: Handwriting-based writer verification remains challenging due to style variations and lack of explainable models for real-world use. This work presents an explainable, writer-dependent framework for offline, text-independent handwriting verification balancing accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability. We propose a lightweight autoencoder, fusing line-level hand-crafted features (pressure, direction) with character-level features from the anchor letter ‘e ’. A denoising autoencoder is trained per writer, with outputs explained using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) attributions interpreted through a Large Language Model (LLM) for human-readable explanations. The framework achieves 91.8% accuracy and 6.3% Equal Error Rate (EER) on a private ruled-paper dataset with normal and fast-speed samples, running in minutes on consumer CPUs. Results demonstrate that combining handcrafted features with autoencoders enables effective explainable verification. Integration of SHAP with LLM-generated interpretations enhances transparency and forensic applicability, providing a scalable solution for practical handwriting verification.

title: Deep Learning-Based Early Detection of Neurodevelopmental Disorders Using Multimodal Behavioral and EEG Data
abstract: Neurodevelopmental disorders such as Autism Spectrum Disorder, Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Intellectual Disability, and Epilepsy affect cognitive, motor, behavioral, and social development in children, often resulting in long-term challenges across the lifespan. Early detection of these conditions is essential, as interventions during critical stages of brain development can significantly improve learning, adaptability, and overall quality of life. However, traditional diagnostic methods, including neuroimaging, clinical observation, and behavioral assessments, are often limited by restricted accessibility, high costs, subjective interpretation, and overlapping symptoms among disorders. Additionally, frequent comorbidities further complicate accurate diagnosis. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, offer powerful tools to address these limitations by identifying complex patterns within large-scale multimodal datasets. This research proposes a deep learning-based framework for early detection in neurodevelopmental disorders, utilizing publicly available datasets that integrate behavioral, cognitive, and developmental information to develop reliable and scalable predictive models.

title: Few-Shot Facial Emotion Recognition Through South Asian Geographic Transfer Learning
abstract: State-of-the-art emotion recognition systems demonstrate systematic failure across cultural boundaries, with performance degrading from 85 percent on Western benchmarks to$\mathbf{1 6}$percent on South Asian populations, a disparity that effectively excludes billions from emotion recognition technology while perpetuating Western-centric bias in affective computing. This work introduces the first systematic geographic transfer learning framework addressing cross-cultural facial emotion recognition under extreme data scarcity by exploiting morphological proximity between culturally similar populations for few-shot adaptation. The framework advances three critical innovations. First, strategic geographic transfer through morphologically proximate intermediate domains from India to Sri Lanka achieves 62.8 percentage point improvement where direct Western transfer catastrophically fails. Second, calibrated 60 percent experience replay integrated with progressive three-stage training prevents catastrophic forgetting while enabling comprehensive six-emotion recognition despite target data covering only four emotions, representing a novel continual learning paradigm unaddressed in existing literature. Third, mobile-efficient architecture ensures practical deployment for resource-constrained populations. Experimental validation demonstrates$\mathbf{7 8. 8}$percent test accuracy with 93 percent sample efficiency relative to conventional$\mathbf{7 0, 0 0 0}$-sample approaches while maintaining$\mathbf{5. 0}$percent generalization gap, establishing unprecedented scalability for underrepresented populations. The observed 43.8 percentage point accuracy differential between universal and culturally variable emotions provides empirical validation of dialect theory in computational contexts. This framework establishes a transformative pathway for developing culturally adaptive artificial intelligence systems applicable to 3.8 billion individuals in underserved regions globally, fundamentally advancing equitable technology access beyond Western-centric paradigms.

title: Privacy-Preserving Real-Time Crowd Counting on IoT Enabled Edge Devices Using YOLOv8n and Norfair
abstract: The implementation of smart crowd management and intelligent infrastructure systems necessitates real-time crowd monitoring to ensure safety, efficiency and responsiveness. Recent developments in deep learning methods and IoT devices have opened new avenues for addressing real-world problems. This study presents a lightweight framework for real-time crowd counting, that utilizes YOLOv8n model for human head detection and the Norfair tracking algorithm for multi-object tracking. The complete system is deployed on a Raspberry Pi 5 edge device connected to a USB camera for video input. Integrating deep learning models on edge devices significantly reduces reliance on high bandwidth data communication and cloud processing. A ThingsBoard-based dashboard provides real-time occupancy visualization and historical crowd data. Experimental evaluations conducted across diverse indoor and outdoor environments demonstrate up to 94% counting accuracy under varying lighting and crowd conditions. The proposed edge-AI solution is scalable, cost-effective and privacy-preserving, as it avoids raw video data transmission for smart crowd monitoring applications.

title: Word Sense Disambiguation: Resolving Lexical Ambiguity in Word-Level Translation - Tamil-to-English
abstract: Word Sense Disambiguation is a vital task in resolving lexical ambiguity, which is one of the major challenges in NLP. In Tamil-to-English translation, this challenge occurs when a single Tamil word has multiple English meanings. The correct meaning depends on the context in which the word appears. This research constructs a robust WSD approach for Tamil-to-English word-level translation. The model utilizes Tamil-specific syntactic and semantic structures to improve contextual understanding. By incorporating linguistic rules and context analysis, the work aims to improve translation accuracy. The main contribution of the research will be that this kind of effort has great demand in low-resource languages like Tamil due to poor availability of NLP tools. This improvement can significantly enhance translation models. It also facilitates better communication and knowledge sharing between Tamil and English speakers. Compared to existing WSD systems such as Word Overlapping$(71 \%)$, Cumulative Similarity (84.3%), WSDPCS (78.3%), and Google Translate$(79.7 \%)$, the proposed hybrid model achieved a notable improvement with 82.5% accuracy in target word identification and 90% accuracy in gloss sense prediction.

title: An Optimization-Based Neural Network Method for Detection and Classification of Faults in PV-Integrated Low-Voltage Systems
abstract: The increasing penetration of grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems in low-voltage (LV) distribution networks has introduced new operational challenges related to fault detection and system protection. Conventional protection and monitoring techniques are often inadequate for accurately identifying diverse fault types under dynamic operating conditions, especially in PV-integrated environments. This study focused on a real-world PV-integrated low-voltage distribution network located in the Galle district of Sri Lanka. The network was modelled using ETAP software, incorporating a distribution transformer, four outgoing feeders, approximately 130 single-phase and three-phase loads, and 23 residential PV customers. Various fault scenarios, such as line-to-ground (LG), line-to-line (LL), line-to-line-to-ground (LLG), and three-phase faults, were simulated at different bus locations. Time-series electrical parameters were collected and processed to develop a fault classification dataset. A baseline Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network (NN) was developed and trained, followed by performance enhancement using optimisation techniques. The Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO)-optimised LSTM achieves the highest overall performance (99.8%) with the lowest prediction time and highest throughput, making it the most suitable model for real-time LV network protection. This research proposes an optimisation-based NN framework for accurate and efficient fault detection and classification in PV-integrated low-voltage distribution systems, highlighting its suitability for intelligent protection and monitoring applications.

title: An Ensemble Deep Lerning Approach for Emotion-Driven TikTok Video Classification and Hashtag Recommendation
abstract: Emotion recognition has come to be an important aspect of affective computing, especially in the case of shortvideo applications like TikTok, where users can convey emotions in the form of spontaneous facial expressions, speech, and dynamic audiovisual effects. Besides the visual emotional clues, user-created hashtags are essential in content discovery and social interaction, as they represent the semantic meaning and the emotional intent. Nevertheless, the automatic analysis and the creation of emotional matching hashtags in the real-life video using TikTok are difficult because of uncontrolled lighting, rapid motion, various user behaviors, and noisy backgrounds. To overcome these issues, this paper suggests the cohesive emotion-aware system that combines emotion recognition ensemble CNNs with a hybrid hashtag generation based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Knowledge Graph (KG) reasoning, and Large Language Models (LLMs). An online dataset consisting of 4,000 true TikTok videos that captured four emotions (happiness, sadness, anger, and surprise) was downloaded and processed in order to share it with the model to be trained and evaluated. Emotion classification was done using MobileNet, VGGNet, and ResNet, and an ensemble model was created by combining their results to enhance robustness and accuracy. As demonstrated in the experiments, the ensemble model is higher performing with an accuracy of 96.3% and a higher recall and lower error rate. In generating hashtags, video transcripts and emotion labels were used along with the retrieval of the vectors database and semantic reasoning based on knowledge to control the LLM generation. Comparative analysis proves that the RAGimproved FLAN-T5 model performs better compared to KGbased and LLM-only models in Precision@k, Recall@k, and F1@k. The suggested framework is generally a solid multimodal approach to understanding emotions in content and hashtag generation on short-video platforms.

title: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models for Linkedin Popularity Classification
abstract: The popularity of social media, and that of LinkedIn in particular, serves a key role in increasing career visibility, professional impact, and access to opportunities. Proper forecasting of followers is a useful source of information on personal branding, recruitment intelligence, and digital professional network dynamics. The report proposes a multimodal deep learning model that forecasts the range of follower counts on LinkedIn by using professional characteristics, demographic factors, as well as facial-emotional attributes obtained through profile images. The framework employs a multi-branch neural network in order to integrate structured tabular data with the visual-emotional features, which has multifaceted, non-linear correlations between heterogeneous features. Through the use of professional and visual-emotional portrayal, the model takes into consideration those aspects which contribute to acquisition of followers, such as career advancement, credibility, appeal, as well as engagement tendencies. The prediction of the multimodal 1D CNN is tested on classical machine learning controls, such as, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and Gradient Boosting Machine. The findings indicate that the suggested model works better than the conventional ones with better accuracy, higher F1-scores, and fewer errors, proving the usefulness of deep learning modeling multimodal interactions. Explainable AI methods, such as SHAP and LIME, take the decisions made by the model and measure the significance of various groups of features. Professional attributes are found to be the strongest predictors, facial-emotional features play a moderating role, and demographic characteristics play a minor role in deciding, which shows how career development and profile presentation are more crucial than demographic factors.

title: A Computational Approach for Music-Driven Group Dance Formation Generation
abstract: Designing group dance choreography requires careful coordination of positional formations that align with musical rhythm while maintaining visual balance, spacing, and collision avoidance among dancers. This research has explored music-driven dance generation. Most existing approaches focus on individual dancer motion and do not effectively address the challenges of group level positional coordination. This limitation reduces their practicality to real-world choreography scenarios involving multiple dancers. This paper presents a music-driven system for automatic group dance formation generation using a modular learning-based approach. The proposed system breaks down the problem into three main stages: music structure analysis, positional formation generation, and transition optimization. Musical features such as tempo, rhythmic emphasis, and energy variation are extracted to identify suitable moments for formation changes. These features are then used to condition deep generative models that produce positional formations for a specified number of dancers. Two generative approaches, a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE), and a diffusion-based model, are investigated and compared to analyze their effectiveness in generating stable and visually balanced formations. To ensure smooth and physically feasible transitions between formations, dancer movement is modeled as a multi agent navigation problem and optimized using reinforcement learning based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Experimental evaluation demonstrates that diffusion-based formation generation produces more structured and stable positional layouts, while reinforcement learning based transition planning significantly reduces collision occurrences compared to non-learning baselines. The results highlight the effectiveness of combining music analysis, deep generative modeling, and reinforcement learning for group dance choreography. The proposed framework provides a flexible foundation for future research in automated choreography and creative performance applications.

title: Multimodal Federated Learning for Undiagnosed Diabetes Detection with Explainable AI
abstract: The rising prevalence of diabetes requires robust and automated screening mechanisms to prevent complications like Diabetic Retinopathy (DR). However, current Artificial Intelligence (AI) solutions often rely on centralized data aggregation, which raises privacy concerns under regulations such as GDPR and HIPAA. Furthermore, most systems are unimodal, utilizing either Electronic Health Records (EHR) or retinal imaging in isolation, thereby limiting diagnostic comprehensiveness. This paper proposes a novel Multimodal Federated Learning (FL) framework that integrates structured clinical data with retinal fundus images to detect undiagnosed diabetes while preserving data privacy. We employ a Late Fusion architecture utilizing a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) for tabular features and an EfficientNet-B2 backbone for imaging. To address the “black box” nature of deep learning, we integrate Explainable AI (XAI) modules, specifically SHAP for EHR features and Grad-CAM for retinal images, ensuring clinical interpretability. Experimental results demonstrate that this federated multimodal approach achieves superior performance compared to unimodal baselines while maintaining strict data localization.

title: Artificial Intelligence Based Smart Glass for Navigating Vision Impaired Individuals
abstract: The proposed research is an AI-based indoor navigation system that helps visually impaired people navigate with the assistance of object detection, depth estimation, and natural-language guidance. The system operates on a stereo-vision camera with a YOLOv8 model which has been trained to locate two important objects of the interior space, namely, tables as a navigation object and chairs as an obstacle object, to model mobility in controlled conditions. The depth estimation is carried out based on stereo disparity mapping, which allows measuring the distance and obstacle avoidance in real-time. A rule-based navigation module converts spatial knowledge to step-by-step voice instructions produced by a Rule-based language model and passed on to TTS. Several indoor configurations of different table-chair layouts were used to test the system with different multiple configurations to assess the performance of the system in terms of accuracy in detection, reliability in navigation and performance in terms of user-safety. The findings indicate that the system has high accuracy in object detection and is able to circumvent obstacles and direct users to the target point. This prototype shows that it is possible to use vision-based indoor mobility aids at low cost and give them a basis to be expanded to multi-object environment, autonomous path finding, and wearable embedded implementation.

title: AI-Based Line-Level Defect Prediction Using a Hybrid GNN Framework for Large-Scale Python Projects
abstract: Line-level defect prediction plays a critical role in improving software quality and developer productivity by enabling the precise localization of defect-prone code segments. Existing defect prediction approaches often operate at limited granularities, such as file or module level, and struggle to effectively capture the combined semantic, sequential, and structural characteristics required for fine-grained defect localization in large-scale software systems. To address these gaps, the paper presents GNNLineDef, a preliminary investigation on an AI-based line-level defect prediction framework for large-scale Python projects. The GNNLineDef follows a modular three stage architecture: (1) source code lines are generated using CodeBERT, a pre-trained transformer model trained on large- scale code and natural language corpora, (2) sequential contextual dependencies among code lines within a file are modeled using a bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network, enabling the capture of both forward and backward contextual information, and the (3) structural dependencies are modeled through a lightweight Code Property Graph (CPG), where a Graph Attention Network (GAT) is employed to learn relational interactions among code lines while emphasizing defect. Preliminary experiments were conducted on a subset of open-source Python repositories under limited computational resources. The initial experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid architecture improves prediction performance and effectively prioritizes defect-prone code lines by integrating semantic, sequential, and structural relationships. The model shows strong results across BalAcc (82%), Recall@20% (78%), Effort@20% (1%), highlighting its effectiveness in both classification and ranking-based evaluations while reducing inspection effort. Although evaluated on a limited scale, these findings establish a promising foundation for fine-grained line-level defect prediction in large-scale codebases. Future improvements, including model fine-tuning, optimized lightweight graph construction, cross-project evaluation, and the integration of explainable AI techniques, can further enhance the model's effectiveness, efficiency, and real-world applicability.

title: Reconstructing Sinhala Sentences from Early Brahmi-Driven Text Using a Hybrid Neural and Rule Based Pipeline
abstract: This research, a novel computational approach to reconstruct grammatically correct and meaningful Sinhala sentences from direct Brahmi - Sinhala translations found in ancient inscriptions. Direct translations are typically unordered and morphologically improvised. With semantic ambiguity, challenging for semantic interpretation by modern readers. To deal with these issues, a modular pipeline was developed and comprise three core stages: Syntactic Analysis - With a custom trained Stanza Parser, Sentence Reordering with a fine-tuned ByT5 model, and Morphology Correction with a second ByT5 model. The system combines rule-based precision with data driven generalization, enabling structural aware sentence transformation. The suggested POS tagger implemented an overall accuracy of 95.43% and thus filtered critical linguistic categories relevant to inscriptional Sinhala. The sentence reordering model showed excellent results with an exact match accuracy of 8 6. 4% and high BLUE and METEOR scores, the morphological completion model achieved 81.4% exact match accuracy with an average BLUE score of 0. 9 0. Expert evaluation carried out together with the Department of Archaeology which confirmed that the output maintained the grammaticality and the historical context of inscriptions. This work not only introduces the first custom Sinhala syntactic parsing pipeline tailored for inscriptional text but also contributes to architecture for low resource and historical languages. The results show that the computational linguistic methods can significantly facilitate the accessibility and understanding of ancient Sri Lankan inscriptions.

title: An AI-Driven Approach for User-Personalized Interior Color Matching Using Room Complexity and Visual Context
abstract: Interior color selection plays a critical role in shaping the aesthetic quality and psychological comfort of indoor spaces. However, most existing interior design tools rely on predefined color palettes or rule-based systems that fail to consider individual user preferences, room characteristics, and existing visual context simultaneously. As a result, color recommendations often lack personalization and practical relevance. This paper proposes an AI-driven framework for user-personalized interior color matching that integrates multiple complementary models into a unified system. The framework integrates a fuzzy logic-based room complexity analysis, user preference clustering, color and texture detection, and a color recommendation strategy to generate context-aware and personalized color palettes. Room complexity is quantified using area-based, entropy-based, and visual clutter metrics, which are fused through a fuzzy logic decision system. User preferences are collected through a structured questionnaire and grouped using K-means clustering to identify dominant preference patterns. In parallel, computer vision techniques are applied to detect wall regions, identify textures, and extract dominant wall colors from interior images. The outputs of these models are integrated within a color recommendation module that applies color harmony principles while adapting color vibrancy based on room complexity and user cluster characteristics. A lightweight real-time visualization approach is employed to allow users to preview recommended colors directly on room images without relying on hardware-intensive augmented reality technologies. Experimental evaluations and user studies confirm improved user satisfaction (84% realism, 88% preference) and efficient mobile performance (1.7 s per image) for the proposed personalized color recommendation framework. This research highlights the potential of combining user modeling, environmental analysis, and visual context to advance AI-assisted interior design systems.

title: The Role of Prompt Engineering in AI Essay Scoring: A Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT's Scoring Stability Across Varying Prompt Designs
abstract: The rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs), including ChatGPT, in educational contexts has renewed interest in their potential use for automated essay scoring (AES). While prior studies report moderate to strong agreement between ChatGPT and human raters, the role of prompt engineering in shaping scoring reliability and validity remains insufficiently examined. This study investigates how different prompt designs influence the consistency and human alignment of ChatGPT-based essay scoring. Using a stratified sample of 100 learner essays from the ICNALE corpus, each essay was evaluated under four prompt conditions with increasing levels of instructional structure. Scoring outcomes were analyzed using descriptive statistics, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), repeated-measures ANOVA, and error-based metrics. The results reveal statistically significant differences across prompt conditions, with rubric-aligned prompts yielding substantially lower score variability and the highest agreement with human ratings (average-measure ICC$>0.92)$. Distributional analyses further demonstrate that structured prompts effectively constrain stochastic scoring behavior. These findings provide empirical evidence that prompt design is a critical methodological factor in LLM-based AES and that reliability limitations commonly attributed to ChatGPT can be mitigated through principled prompt engineering. The study offers practical guidance for the responsible deployment of AI-assisted assessment systems and contributes to the growing literature on prompt-sensitive behavior in educational applications of LLMs.

title: The Impact of LLMs on Software Development
abstract: The rapid adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) in software development has raised expectations regarding improved productivity, code quality, and development efficiency. However, empirical evidence on their impact across different stages of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) remains limited. This study examines how software professionals use LLMs in practice and the benefits and limitations of their use. The study combines a systematic review of 75 peer-reviewed studies with survey data from 207 software professionals, supported by semi-structured interviews. LLM usage was examined across eight software engineering outcome areas, including Productivity and Efficiency, Code Quality and Reliability, Security and Vulnerability Management, Governance, Ethics and Trust, Client Experience and Satisfaction, Communication and Collaboration, Job and Role Transformation, Innovation and Creativity. The findings indicate perceived improvements in productivity, innovation, and professional role transformation alongside a substantial impact on security and vulnerability management practices. In the security domain, LLMs influence vulnerability identification and remediation while also introducing new security risks and biases. In contrast, no clear improvements were reported in code quality, client satisfaction, or team collaboration. These findings suggest that current benefits are largely confined to individual workflows, while broader system-level outcomes remain less affected. This study offers empirical, multi-dimensional insights evidence to inform future integration strategies emphasizing structured adoption, enhanced quality assurance, and collaborative development practices.

title: Electronic Nose-Driven Classification of Sri Lankan Teas: An Ensemble Learning Approach Based on Aroma Profiles
abstract: Geographical authentication of tea is critical for quality assurance, brand protection, and fraud prevention in the global tea market. However, conventional approaches based on sensory evaluation and chemical analysis are often subjective, labor-intensive, time-consuming, and costly, limiting their scalability for routine authentication. This study proposes an integrated electronic nose (E-Nose) and machine learning framework for the geographical origin classification of Sri Lankan tea using aroma profiles. Aroma data were collected from 367 dry tea samples representing seven major tea-growing regions using a custom-developed metal oxide semiconductor (MOS)-based Digi-Nose device equipped with seven gas sensors. The acquired sensor responses were digitally recorded and structured for supervised learning analysis. To ensure reliable and unbiased model training, the dataset was preprocessed and balanced prior to classification. Eight supervised machine learning models, such as ensemble-based (Extra Trees, Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM), distance-based (K-Nearest Neighbors), kernel-based (Support Vector Machine), and neural network-based (Multi-Layer Perceptron) approaches, were experimentally evaluated. Model performance was assessed using multiple metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices, learning curve analysis, and$\mathbf{1 0}$-fold cross-validation to verify robustness and generalization. Among all evaluated models, the Extra Trees classifier demonstrated superior performance, achieving an overall classification accuracy of 98.63%, along with consistently high precision and recall across all tea regions. The findings confirm that the integration of MOS-based E-Nose sensing with ensemble learning techniques provides a reliable, non-destructive, and deployment-ready solution for aroma-based geographical authentication of tea, with strong potential for real-world industrial and regulatory applications.

title: Sovereign Negotiator Network: A Token-Efficient Hierarchical Protocol for Constraint-Aware Multi-Agent Coordination
abstract: Multi-agent systems are evolving from passive tools to autonomous representatives, but current architectures face a critical bottleneck: humans lack the cognitive bandwidth to locate optimal counterparties in large networks, while agents fail to resolve ambiguous constraints without excessive computational overhead. We introduce the Sovereign Negotiator Network (SNN), a hierarchical protocol, intelligent proxies negotiate on behalf of users through two key mechanisms: (1) Federated Society Routing, which organizes agents into specialized clusters, reducing discovery complexity from$O\left(N^{2}\right)$to$O\left(\frac{N}{k}\right)$, and (2) Human-Gated Context Injection, which enables users to inject preference updates only when negotiations reach deadlock, preserving autonomy while maintaining control. Validated on 100-agent networks using a hybrid Llama-3.2:1b (edge) and GPT-4o (cloud) architecture, SNN achieves an 87.6% reduction in token consumption (310 vs. 2,500 tokens) compared to ReAct baselines, where 94% of negotiations are resolved within 4 rounds. SNN provides a practical framework for large-scale agent coordination: proxies handle resource discovery and negotiation autonomously, but humans maintain final authority over high-stakes decisions.

title: Adoption of AI-Based Career Guidance in Sri Lanka: an Analysis of Education, Region, and Age-Based Needs
abstract: The growing use of artificial intelligence in career guidance has changed the way people explore career options, develop skills and make decisions related to employment. In Sri Lanka, however, there is limited empirical evidence on how these tools are actually used across different age groups and regions. This study examines the usage patterns, challenges and user expectations related to AI-based career guidance tools, with particular attention to age-based and regional differences. A survey across multiple districts and provinces yielded 489 responses, of which 481 valid responses were analyzed. The findings show that ChatGPT was the most widely used tool, reported by 71.9% of respondents, followed by Google Gemini (57%), Microsoft Copilot (34.3%), LinkedIn (21.4%) and Coursera (18.1%). Usage was highest among the 18-24 age group, while Coursera showed relatively higher adoption among respondents aged 25-34, reflecting greater interest in structured skill development. The study also identified challenges that affect adoption, including paid feature limitations, language related difficulties, limited internet access and high data costs. Many respondents highlighted the need for stronger support for Sinhala and Tamil languages, emphasizing the importance of inclusive and locally relevant career guidance solutions. Overall, the findings indicate that AI-based career guidance tools are widely used among the surveyed respondents in Sri Lanka, particularly younger users, highlighting exploratory patterns across regions and age groups. The study provides empirical evidence from Sri Lanka, highlighting key user groups, regional disparities, and adoption challenges, while offering one of the survey-based analyses of demographic and regional patterns in AI-based career guidance tool usage.

title: Impact of EEG-Based Emotion Recognition on Video Commercial Effectiveness Optimization: A Comprehensive Literature Analysis
abstract: The growing use of neuromarketing has positioned EEG-based emotion recognition as a powerful approach for understanding and optimizing video commercial effectiveness. This literature analysis examines how EEG-derived emotional indices - Arousal, Valence, and Approach-Withdrawal contribute to measuring consumer responses and improving advertisement performance. Existing studies demonstrate that EEG enables real-time, objective tracking of cognitive and affective reactions, helping identify moments of attention, emotional resonance, and motivational tendencies within video commercials. These insights directly support optimization processes by linking neurophysiological responses with advertising outcomes such as recall, preference formation, and purchase intention. Furthermore, research highlights the value of integrating EEG findings with affective models such as Russell's Circumplex Model and behavioral theories including the Hierarchy of Effects, reinforcing the connection between emotional states and consumer decision-making. Despite these benefits, challenges such as signal noise, device constraints, participant variability, and complexities in interpreting emotional indicators persist. Emerging trends such as multimodal data fusion, machine learning-based classification, and portable EEG systems indicate strong potential for developing predictive, feedback-driven frameworks for video commercial optimization. This review synthesizes current evidence and provides theoretical and methodological insights to support future EEG-based commercial effectiveness measurement and optimization systems.

title: Digital Fatigue and Task Performance in Remote Work: A Multidimensional Analysis in Sri Lanka
abstract: Digital fatigue has become an increasing concern among remote working employees, as it influences attention, engagement, and task performance. Even though the adverse consequences of digital fatigue have been highlighted in global research, there is still limited empirical evidence exist in the context of remote work in Sri Lanka. From an Information Systems (IS) perspective, this study investigates how prolonged interaction with digital interfaces contributes to cognitive, visual, emotional, and physical fatigue and its subsequent impact on task performance. A cross-sectional quantitative survey was conducted with 384 full-time remote workers, capturing demographics, work experience, fatigue dimensions, and task performance indicators. The statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression. The results reveal that all four dimensions of digital fatigue have a significant negative impact on task performance. Among them, physical fatigue shows the strongest negative effect, followed by emotional fatigue, cognitive fatigue, and visual fatigue. The internal consistency of all scales was checked with reliability analysis. Correlation and regression analyses also revealed strong associations between fatigue dimensions and task performance. Overall, the evidence indicates that digital fatigue is a critical variable influencing the effectiveness of remote work and that specific interventions are required. The study offers practical recommendations to IS managers, system designers, and policymakers to develop strategies for minimizing fatigue and sustaining the performance of employees.

title: Hybrid ML/DL Framework for Arthritis Risk and Severity Prediction
abstract: Arthritis is a common chronic disease with significant consequences for the quality of life among older populations. Early diagnosis of arthritis can help in preserving positive health outcomes through mitigating the progression of the disease. In this study, a hybrid predictive framework was introduced that takes individual lifestyle parameters along with the radiographic imaging of the patient as parameters that have not been studied in the Sri Lankan context before. Data were collected from Gampaha Wickramarachchi Ayurveda Hospital, and the data were split into two main data sets:$\mathbf{1 2 0 0}$records of lifestyle factors and clinical manifestations, and 598 diagnostic X-radiography images of knee joints. Supervised Machine Learning algorithms have been applied to the textual dataset, and the best validation accuracy of 96% for the prediction of the likelihood of Arthritis by employing the Random Forest (RF) classifier. Patients at high risk were graded into three groups using deep learning architectures (ResNet-50 and a convolutional neural network). CNN validation accuracy was 95% and 97% for training accuracy. The outcomes of this research have been operationalized through a web application that integrates the two models, enabling arthritis risk prediction based on lifestyle and symptom data, followed by severity classification through X-ray analysis when risk is detected.

title: Sinhala Speech Recognition System for Speech-Based Autism Intervention in Children Using the NAO Robot
abstract: This research focuses on the development of a Sinhala speech recognition engine tailored to identify the language content of conversations with children. The engine leverages machine learning algorithms and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to transcribe and classify speech in Sinhala. Key features include an acoustic model optimized for the nuances of Sinhala phonetics and a language model trained on datasets encompassing texts of child-directed speech. The system evaluates linguistic aspects to assess the appropriateness of content and engagement levels in child-centric dialogues. By addressing challenges such as phoneme variation and informal conversational patterns, the system aims to enhance the understanding and facilitation of Sinhala-based child interactions, promoting effective communication and developmental support.

title: Validating an AI Ethics Awareness Instrument for K-12 Learners: Evidence from Mixed Methods Pilot Study
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in schooling through personalized learning systems, automated assessment, and generative AI tools, raising ethical concerns such as privacy, bias, transparency, accountability, and human oversight. However, empirical evidence on K-12 learners' AI ethics awareness remains limited in developing contexts, including Sri Lanka. This paper reports a mixed-methods pilot study that adapts and evaluates an AI ethics awareness questionnaire for Sri Lankan secondary students (Grades 6-10;$n=75$). The instrument comprised (i) a 13-item Likert scale aligned with autonomy, beneficence, and fairness, (ii) scenario-based multiple-choice ethical dilemmas, and (iii) an open-ended prompt on AI ethics. Quantitative analyses indicated strong internal consistency (Cronbach's$\boldsymbol{\alpha} \boldsymbol{\approx 0. 8 7}$) and supported a preliminary three-factor structure consistent with the intended constructs. Item statistics suggested relatively high perceived awareness of privacy and harm prevention, while autonomy and social-justice related concepts showed lower and more dispersed scores. Scenario responses revealed a notable principles-to-practice gap, where some learners reporting high awareness selected ethically weak options in applied dilemmas. Thematic analysis of 258 open-ended responses (392 coded segments) identified five themes dominated by privacy concerns, learning impacts (overreliance and reduced critical thinking), and academic integrity, highlighting content areas underrepresented in the current scale (e.g., trust/accuracy and misuse in learning). Findings provide initial psychometric evidence for the adapted instrument and motivate refinements and larger-scale validation to inform responsible AI literacy integration in Sri Lankan school curricula.
