title: LSTM-CNN Architecture Enhanced with Semantic Metadata for Efficient Duplicate Bug Report Detection
abstract: Duplication of bug reports poses a significant impact on software development efficiency with$\mathbf{1 2 - 2 5 \%}$of bugs report being duplicated on large projects. Manual identification techniques are both time consuming and prone to error. This study examines whether semantic metadata that encodes content-level similarities together with simplified deep learning architectures can be more effective than relying on complex models. We aim to examine existing practices and determine weaknesses, research and prove semantic content-based metadata to be useful in robust identification, structure and test various deep learning models to define the best methods to use to achieve higher levels of performance. Existing studies reveal that machine learning methods outperform traditional information-retrieval techniques by a significant margin, while deep learning approaches achieve higher accuracy but often suffer from limited feature diversity. We collected 535,477 of quality pairs with a$\mathbf{7 0 \%}-\mathbf{1 0 \%}-\mathbf{2 0 \%}$split for training, validation, and testing. Our feature engineering on DistilBERT yielded a mean correlation of 0.1888, surpassing traditional metadata. We compared 6 architectures, namely, LSTM, CNN, LSTM + Metadata, Hybrid + Attention, Hybrid + Attention with Metadata, and proposed LSTM + CNN + Metadata, evaluated through accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC metrics. The proposed architecture resulted 92.53% F1-score, which is better than complex attention-based models. Contextual processing is proven to be better, as LSTM performs higher than CNN. This paper highlights that the quality of features is more critical for model performance than model complexity, presenting a cost-effective, accurate, and scalable method for automated duplicate bug detection in real-world applications.

title: Generalizable Corn Gray Leaf Spot Classification with Explainability for Resource Constraint Environments
abstract: Accurate detection of plant diseases is critical for ensuring global food security. This becomes a more significant problem for widely cultivated crops such as corn. Gray Leaf Spot, caused by Cercospora species, is one of the most destructive fungal diseases affecting corn. Every year this leads to significant crop losses worldwide if not identified at an early stage. While deep learning approaches have been introduced with high accuracies in plant disease classification, their black box nature limits practical adoption by farmers. This study investigates the explainability of CNN-based models for corn Gray Leaf Spot detection using Gradient weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). Two widely used architectures, ResNet50 and EfficientNet-B0, are trained using a subset of the PlantVillage dataset consisting of healthy corn leaves and Gray Leaf Spot affected leaves. Model performance is evaluated by classification accuracy, while explainability is assessed by analyzing the spatial alignment between Grad-CAM heatmaps and relevant lesion regions on corn leaves. The results show that although both models achieve high classification accuracy, EfficientNet-B0 provides more localized and biologically meaningful visual explanations, highlighting its suitability for trustworthy agricultural decision support systems. Experimental evaluations show that EfficientNet-B0 with random augmentation offers the best balance between accuracy, explainability, and efficiency, achieving 93.7% accuracy on the PlantDoc dataset with low inference time and model size suitable for resource constrained environments.

title: AI-Driven Flutter UI Generation Using Natural Language Commands with Social and Ethical Considerations
abstract: The accelerated pace of development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the emerging opportunities to automate the generation of user interfaces (UI) are explored in this research, especially within the context of cross-platform development tools like the Flutter platform. This research aimed to develop customed and open access LLM models, to create User Interfaces (UI) effectively. Then, the social and ethical implications of AI based UI design creation were assessed through a questionnaire survey. The developed framework was an integration of five free LLM models named Gemini, Groq, Cohere, HuggingFace, and OpenRouter, along with the developed retrieval-based model, which was trained on the 10,000-example dataset of Flutter UI. Then the final framework developed through the FastAPI backend and the Flutter App, along with both typed and vocal input, parallel model processing, and the real-time codes as per the standards of Flutter 3.27.1. The model follows the pragmatic mixed-method research approach, along with accuracy-based metrics to evaluate efficiency, and the perceptions are measured by conducting an extensive survey on 220 IT professionals. The result shows that the developed framework is capable of accurately interpreting natural language commands and then generating valid UI code on the Flutter platform. The custom-trained model scored 87.01% accuracy. The outcome of the survey analysis indicates that AI-generated UI, would be able to pinpoint significant issues. In conclusion, this research makes significant contributions to the technically sound and ethical considerations for AI-driven Flutter UI generation, as well as their professional implications in terms of perceived capabilities and limitations. Some recommendations are proposed to improve accessibility, designs, and practices for future research and more adaptive, context-aware, and inclusive practices for AI-driven UI generation.

title: Script Sensitivity: Benchmarking Language Models on Unicode, Romanized and Mixed-Script Sinhala
abstract: The performance of Language Models (LMs) on low-resource, morphologically rich languages like Sinhala remains largely unexplored, particularly regarding script variation in digital communication. Sinhala exhibits script duality, with Unicode used in formal contexts and Romanized text dominating social media, while mixed-script usage is common in practice. This paper benchmarks 24 open-source LMs on Unicode, Romanized and mixed-script Sinhala using perplexity evaluation across diverse text sources. Results reveal substantial script sensitivity, with median performance degradation exceeding 300 times from Unicode to Romanized text. Critically, model size shows no correlation with script-handling competence, as smaller models often outperform architectures 28 times larger. Unicode performance strongly predicts mixed-script robustness but not Romanized capability, demonstrating that single-script evaluation substantially underestimates real-world deployment challenges. These findings establish baseline LM capabilities for Sinhala and provide practical guidance for model selection in multi-script low-resource environments.

title: Dynamic Pixel Mapping for Adaptive Crowd Displays Using Real-Time Spatial Sampling
abstract: Large-scale crowd displays using wearable light-emitting devices have become a popular medium in concerts, ceremonies, and public events. While some installations rely on infrared (IR) projection systems that externally illuminate participants, this work focuses exclusively on radio-frequency (RF) wearable-based crowd displays without any form of optical projection. Existing wearable systems typically depend on static or section-based control approaches with the assumption of fixed pixel positions. With the motion of the participants, these assumptions fail, resulting in distorted or inconsistent visual patterns. This shortcoming limits the ability to produce detailed images, animations, or visual patterns on crowds. This paper proposes a dynamic pixel mapping framework that enables adaptive visual rendering on moving crowds by treating each participant as a mobile pixel. Rather than mapping visuals to predefined spatial zones, the proposed approach samples a continuously defined visual field at the real-time spatial coordinates of each participant. Two compatible mapping strategies are introduced: coordinate normalization for direct image sampling and continuous field-based mapping for procedural and density robust visual effects. The proposed approach tolerates participant motion, irregular spatial distributions, and localization noise while maintaining global visual coherence. Experimental assessments utilizing simulated and prototype crowd configurations depict that the proposed approaches excel beyond conventional section-based mapping in terms of spatial consistency and temporal stability. Field-based mapping preserves visual structure under sparse and dynamic crowd conditions. This framework presents a foundational model for adaptive crowd displays and human-centric visualization systems, allowing modern applications in smart entertainment venues and large scale Internet of Things light system actuation.

title: Enhancing QoS for Encrypted Traffic Using Flow-Based Traffic Classification in Software-Defined Networks
abstract: With the majority of modern network traffic now encrypted, traditional deep packet inspection techniques are inadequate for application identification and quality of service enforcement. This work proposes a flow-based traffic classification framework that integrates supervised machine learning with software-defined networking to enable intelligent, privacy-preserving quality of service management. Using the VPN-nonVPN 2016 dataset, four machine learning classifiers namely, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost were trained on$\mathbf{1 5}$OpenFlow-extractable flow features to classify encrypted virtual private network traffic into four categories: VoIP, Email, Chat, and Browsing. Among the considered machine learning models, XGBoost achieved the highest accuracy of 92.62% with low inference latency and compact model size, while VoIP traffic attained 98% precision and 99% recall. The trained model was integrated into the Ryu SDN controller in a Mininet environment, enabling the application of real-time quality of service policies based on predicted traffic types. Our empirical test results indicate that machine learning based flow-level classification provides an effective method for managing encrypted traffic and improving Quality of Service without relying on packet payload inspection.

title: Development of an Automated Garment Output Inspection Machine to Identify Color Defects and Oil Stains
abstract: High-end garment manufacturing faces persistent challenges in maintaining product quality, particularly at the final inspection stage, where defects like color variations and oil stains may occur. Manual inspection is prone to human error, fatigue, and inconsistency. This study presents an automated garment inspection system using RGB color sensors, high resolution cameras, and advanced image processing algorithms, including thresholding, edge detection, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), to detect defects in real time. Realtime feedback and integration with production lines reduce manual labor and allow immediate action on defective products, improving speed and quality control. The system is cost-effective and suitable for small and medium enterprises (SMEs). Results demonstrate its potential to transform garment quality control by enhancing detection accuracy, reducing production costs, and increasing operational efficiency. Ongoing optimization can expand its applicability to various fabrics, environmental conditions, and additional defect types. The system achieved higher accuracy (98% vs. 85%) and efficiency (30 minutes vs. 120 minutes per 100 garments) compared to manual inspection. The proposed automated inspection approach offers a practical, scalable solution for meeting the growing demand for highquality garments in international markets while maintaining sustainability in manufacturing.

title: Assessing the Effectiveness of Generative AI in Undergraduate Academic Writing
abstract: Academic writing ability is an essential skill in higher education; however, undergraduates have continued to face challenges in organizing ideas, paraphrasing, and maintaining academic register. However, the rapid development of new tools in the form of Generative Artificial Intelligence, including applications like ChatGPT, has drawn considerable attention regarding their potential in acting as instructional tools for academic writing support. This research explores the effectiveness of Generative AI in developing the academic writing skill of undergraduates in the context of higher education in Sri Lanka. An experimental design was followed for this research, which included 26 information technology and management field students. The writing ability of the students was measured through an analytic rubric that provided an overall score of up to 20. Generative AI support was provided only during the mid-test period, while the pre- and post-tests were done without AI support in order to measure the level of internalization of the subject. The overall scores of the students in the writing task were analyzed through descriptive statistical analysis and gain scores of learning. The outcome of the investigation has shown that Generative AI can be an effective instructional tool for developing academic writing ability in students when provided in an organized and guided manner.

title: A Hybrid LLM-Driven Recommendation System for Selecting Flutter Packages Using Structured Metadata and Stack Overflow Knowledge
abstract: The rapid growth of the Flutter ecosystem has created significant challenges for developers when selecting appropriate third-party packages, particularly in complex categories such as state management. Existing selection approaches typically rely on individual metrics such as popularity or download counts, which fail to capture contextual aspects of developer intent, real-world problem discussions, or semantic alignment between user requirements and package capabilities. To address this limitation, this paper presents a hybrid recommendation system that integrates structured metadata from official Flutter repositories with unstructured community knowledge extracted from Stack Overflow. The system employs large language models (LLMs) to interpret natural-language user queries, extract relevant technical attributes, and compute semantic relevance across multiple data sources. Three LLMs-GPT-4-Turbo, Gemini 1.5 Pro, and DeepSeek-Coder-V2-were comparatively evaluated to assess their effectiveness in technical intent extraction and semantic matching. GPT-4-Turbo was selected as the primary inference engine based on its superior accuracy, consistency, and resistance to hallucinations. The final recommendation model applies a weighted scoring mechanism that integrates popularity, recency, likes, downloads, accepted answers, sentiment signals, and LLM-based semantic relevance to produce ranked package recommendations aligned with developer requirements. This approach ensures that recommendations incorporate both quantitative repository indicators and qualitative developer experiences. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves high precision, recall, and semantic matching accuracy across multiple evaluation scenarios. Expert validation further confirms that the generated recommendations align with real-world development practices and demonstrate the practical value of the system. Although the study focuses on Flutter state-management packages, the proposed methodology can be generalised to other categories within the Flutter ecosystem. The findings highlight the potential of hybrid LLM-assisted frameworks to improve developer decision-making and enhance the efficiency of package selection in modern software engineering environments.

title: Pre-Implementation Readiness for AI in the Success of ERP Implementation: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems is reshaping enterprise operations, yet implementation failure rates remain high due to inadequate pre-implementation readiness. This study conducts a systematic literature review to examine readiness factors influencing the success of AI-enabled ERP implementations. Based on the analysis of 39 peer-reviewed studies published between 2014 and 2025, five dominant readiness dimensions are identified: technological, organizational, environmental, agile-process, and AI-ethical readiness. These dimensions are synthesized into an integrated Technology, Organization, Environment, Agility, AI Readiness (TOE-A2IR) framework, extending traditional ERP readiness models by incorporating adaptability and ethical governance aligned with Industry 5.0 principles. The findings indicate that readiness for AI-enabled ERP is not a static condition, but a dynamic, multidimensional capability shaped by technology, leadership, agility, and ethical awareness. This study contributes by consolidating fragmented literature, advancing readiness theory for intelligent ERP systems, and offering a structured framework to support informed and responsible AI-driven ERP transformations.

title: An Ensemble Learning Approach to Predicting Football Player Positions Based on Skill and Performance Metric
abstract: Proper identification of player positions in football is one of the important tasks in the field of modern sports analytics that helps in decision-making based on data in scouting, tactics, and talent detection. Conventional methods are mostly based on subjective expert ratings, which might lack consistency and scalability to big data. In order to overcome these drawbacks, this paper suggests a machine learning framework that takes advantage of ensemble learning algorithms to categorize player positions in football based on a complex set of skill and performance measurements. Several ensemble models were applied and tested, among which are bagging, boosting, and XGBoost. Further, a stacking ensemble method was formulated that integrated the results of individual models to increase the robustness and generalization in classification. Performance of the model was evaluated by conventional evaluation measures, such as accuracy, precision, recall, and$\mathbf{F 1}$-score, estimated based on the analysis of the confusion matrix, and weighted$\mathbf{F 1}$-score was given emphasis to resolve the problem of class imbalance. The experimental findings prove that boosting models are better than ensemble methods, and XGBoost can be the highest-performing individual production model. The proposed stacking ensemble recorded the best overall accuracy of 79.96% and weighted F1score of 78.23%, which validated the usefulness of ensemble learning in enhancing predictive accuracy. An analysis based on class showed high scores in well-defined roles such as goalkeeper, center back, and striker, whereas there were lower scores in hybrid and underrepresented roles because of shared skill sets. The analysis of the feature importance also determined the importance of attacking, shooting, defending, and heading to be some of the most important attributes affecting position classification. In general, the results indicate the promise of the ensemble learning-based classification models as trustworthy and explainable football analytics tools.

title: AI-Driven Scalable Feature Engineering Framework for Large-Scale Predictive Analytics
abstract: This study introduces an enhanced and scalable Big Data Analytics (BDA) framework designed to predict and explain student academic performance. The framework leverages Apache Spark and employs ensemble machine learning models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM, alongside deep learning techniques and generative AI. Utilizing a realworld dataset comprising demographic, academic, and behavioral features, the study emphasizes the importance of data diversity in educational analytics. The proposed pipeline incorporates distributed preprocessing, multi-model training with 5-fold crossvalidation, and techniques to address class imbalance, specifically through inverse-frequency weighting. Among the evaluated models, LightGBM demonstrated superior performance, achieving an accuracy of 92.4% and a weighted$F 1$score of 92.2%. This performance outstripped both baseline models and traditional deep learning approaches, showcasing the effectiveness of ensemble methods in educational contexts. To further enhance interpretability, the study integrates model-agnostic tools like LIME and model-specific methods such as SHAP. These tools are complemented by Google's Gemini API, which generates personalized performance summaries for students, offering actionable recommendations based on data-driven insights. This comprehensive system amalgamates scalable big data processing, advanced predictive modeling, and explainable artificial intelligence. By doing so, it supports timely interventions and effective monitoring of student performance, thereby contributing to a more nuanced understanding of the factors influencing academic success. The findings underscore the potential of integrated analytics frameworks in facilitating informed decision-making in educational environments.

title: Ensemble Machine Learning Based Clinical Decision Support System for Optimizing Hemodialysis Parameters in End-Stage Renal Disease Patients
abstract: Hemodialysis is a life-sustaining therapy for patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD), but optimizing critical treatment parameters such as dry weight, hemoglobin, and dialysis adequacy remains challenging, especially in resource-limited settings. Conventional management relies heavily on manual interpretation of heterogeneous clinical data and clinician experience, leading to variability, inefficiencies, and increased cognitive burden. While machine learning (ML) has been applied in nephrology, most studies focus on single outcomes and lack validation using longitudinal, real-world dialysis data. This study proposes an AI-driven ensemble learning system for predictive hemodialysis management that enables simultaneous assessment of multiple clinically relevant outcomes using routinely collected data. A retrospective dataset from 45 maintenance hemodialysis patients at the Renal Care Unit, Teaching Hospital Peradeniya, Sri Lanka, included 3,543 dialysis session records for dry weight prediction and 540 monthly investigation records for hemoglobin and dialysis adequacy, modeled as binary classification tasks. Imbalance-aware ensemble techniques, including Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM, were applied and evaluated using metrics suitable for imbalanced clinical data. Results show that ensemble models effectively handle class imbalance, providing stable predictions across outcomes. MacroF1 scores reached 0.51 for dry weight adjustment and 0.67 for hemoglobin risk, with ROC-AUC values of 0.64 and 0.73, respectively. LightGBM achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.69 for dialysis adequacy. Feature importance analysis highlighted arterial pressure, ultrafiltration rate, and interdialytic weight gain as key predictors, supporting physiological plausibility. Overall, the framework demonstrates reliable predictive performance and offers a scalable, low-cost decision support approach for hemodialysis in resource - constrained settings.

title: Type II Diabetes Risk Prediction: A Multifactor Approach Using Laboratory and Lifestyle Features
abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) affects over 500 million people globally, and early detection is critical for prevention. Most machine learning studies use either laboratory tests or lifestyle factors separately, limiting both accuracy and practical guidance. This study develops a T2D prediction model using LightGBM that combines 43 multi-factors, including laboratory and lifestyle features from NHANES data (1988-2018) with ~ 101, 000 participants. First, a multi-algorithm feature selection approach is followed, aggregating importance from six different models to select robust predictors. Using a LightGBM model, missing data is handled naturally without complex preprocessing and imputation, making it practical for real-world use where patient data is often incomplete. The model is trained on balanced data obtained through under-sampling the majority class to improve minority class detection and evaluated on natural disease prevalence. The system achieves 95.27% ROC-AUC, with 88.48% sensitivity and 87.19% specificity, along with high performance in other metrics as well. This integrated approach balances diagnostic accuracy with clinical practicality while addressing common challenges like missing data and class imbalance.

title: Machine Learning Framework for Portfolio Optimization of S&P 500 Companies Using PCA and K-Means Clustering
abstract: The United States of America is the most powerful country in the global economy; hence countries all over the world closely focus on the USA economy. The New York Stock Exchange is a primary indicator of the USA economy, and the S&P 500 index is a specific and widely used benchmark. Many researchers and investors attempt to capture the uncertainty and unpredictability of companies included in this index due to the high volatility of the market. Therefore, the main objective of this research is to identify market patterns and cluster companies according to price, return, and risk, and to define portfolio strategies that are useful for various investors to achieve higher profit with lower risk. Previous studies mainly focused only on portfolio strategies or clustering methods; however, this research combines Principal Component Analysis (PCA), clustering, and portfolio strategies with optimization to deliver a more effective research contribution to the community. After collecting data from the New York Stock Exchange, various features are created and PCA is used to reduce dimensionality. The main three components are then defined as risk, return, and price. After that, clustering, which is an unsupervised machine learning technique, is used to classify companies into three clusters: low, medium, and high. Using weighted values, companies are allocated into five portfolio strategies—aggressive, income, balanced, growth, and value—based on defined percentages. The best portfolios are then obtained through a simulation process. In the final portfolios, all Sharpe ratios are greater than one, indicating that all portfolios are at an acceptable level. This approach is highly interpretable in practical scenarios and is useful for long-term and short-term traders, investors, researchers, and policymakers to maximize their profit while minimizing their risk.

title: AutoGen-TraceKit: A Lightweight Framework for Process-Aware Evaluation of LLM Agents
abstract: Current benchmarks for evaluating large language model (LLM) agents, such as AgentBench, DeepEval, and IBM's Agentic Evaluation Toolkit, primarily emphasize final outcomes, often overlooking the reasoning pathways, efficiency, and robustness of agent behavior. This paper introduces AutoGen-TraceKit, a lightweight framework designed to capture finegrained agent interaction traces and derive process-aware and robustness-oriented metrics. The contribution is methodological rather than algorithmic: the framework evaluates existing agent systems without proposing a new reasoning method. Unlike conventional evaluations that assess what agents achieve, AutoGen-TraceKit evaluates how they achieve it by measuring efficiency, stability, control-flow health, and sensitivity to perturbations. The methodology consists of two stages: baseline establishment, where interaction data is systematically recorded and analyzed, and sensitivity analysis, which explores performance under varying configurations and stochastic conditions. Experiments are conducted on the MATH benchmark using three large language models; DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B via the Groq API, and OpenAI's GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini models ensuring both reproducibility and scalability while enabling cross-model comparison. Results demonstrate that integrating trace logging with structured metrics yields deeper insight into agent strengths, weaknesses, and trade-offs, enabling more transparent and robust evaluations across different model architectures and performance profiles. This approach positions AutoGen-TraceKit as a practical step towards next-generation evaluation frameworks that are reproducible, lightweight, and capable of revealing hidden dynamics in LLM agent reasoning.

title: AI Agent-Based Automated Essay Marking Framework Using Large Language Models
abstract: Manual essay grading is time-consuming, subjective, and difficult to scale. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled Automated Essay Scoring (AES) systems, but a single LLM used in isolation often lacks the domain-specific knowledge, consistency, and transparency required for high-stakes educational assessment. This paper presents an AI Agent-Based Automated Essay Marking Framework that addresses these limitations by orchestrating LLMs within a multi-agent architecture augmented with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). In the design, a team of specialized AI agents (supervisor, retrieval, evaluation, tool, and quality assurance) collaboratively executes a rubric-based grading workflow, retrieving relevant course content and iteratively refining the scoring process to ensure accuracy and fairness. The framework offers a transparent, rubric-aligned, and domain-aware grading process, shifting from a black-box model-centric approach to a process-centric paradigm. Experimental evaluation against human-marked essays demonstrates that the proposed system achieves high alignment with expert graders, with the best configuration (Gemini 2.5 Flash with RAG and multi-agent orchestration) achieving a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.67 (SD =0.60, 95% CI: 0.49-0.85). The inclusion of RAG reduced MAE by 35.7%(p=0.136, trend toward significance) compared to the non-RAG configuration, while the multi-agent architecture improved accuracy by 16.7%(p=0.043, significant) over singleagent baselines. This work contributes a promising architectural framework for next-generation AES, showing that an agent-based approach using LLMs can provide trustworthy automated grading and detailed feedback, effectively augmenting human educators.

title: Evaluating Data Augmentation Techniques on PPG Signals for Hemoglobin Estimation and Anemia Classification using a Small Dataset
abstract: Anemia is the condition of low hemoglobin (Hb) levels, and it has been identified in more than two billion individuals worldwide, especially in low-resource areas. The traditional methods of measuring Hb are invasive and may not be available, which is the reason why non-invasive methods should be considered as alternatives that are affordable. Photoplethysmography (PPG) signals derived from smartphone fingertip videos is a potential solution but small and unbalanced datasets restrict the performance of the models. To fill this research gap, the paper evaluates 12 data augmentation methods on PPG signals to improve hemoglobin estimation and anemia classification. The entire pipeline, including PPG signal extraction, data augmentation, signal preprocessing, feature engineering, and model training, was performed separately with each augmentation methods under same conditions. This paper explores the best data augmentation methods to enhance noninvasive hemoglobin estimation and anemia diagnosis using PPG signals from fingertip videos. The effectiveness was determined using RMSE and$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$for hemoglobin estimation and accuracy and log loss for anemia classification. Amplitude scaling, jittering and signal wandering were chosen as the most effective augmentation methods because they preserve integrity of physiological signals and enhance the model performance and reduce overfitting in the dataset. The final model that utilized these three augmentation methods achieved an RMSE of 0.3896 for hemoglobin estimation and an accuracy of 0.99 for anemia classification outperforming the results of existing studies on this dataset. The results indicate that non-invasive hemoglobin estimation and anemia screening using PPG signals can be substantially enhanced by balancing the dataset through carefully selected noise-free augmentation techniques.

title: EEG Based Classification of Attentive and Distracted States During Video Based Learning
abstract: Monitoring learner attention during video-based learning is important for adaptive educational systems. However, common indicators such as clicks, video completion, and quiz scores do not directly reflect whether learners remain attentive. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a noninvasive and time-sensitive measure of brain activity for attention-state assessment. This study investigates whether interpretable EEG spectral features can classify attentive and distracted states during instructional video viewing. EEG recordings from 30 participants in Experiment 2 of the Brain, Body, and Behavior Dataset (BBBD) were analyzed using the common stimulus stim01 under attentive and distracted conditions. The signals were segmented into 4 s windows with 2 s overlap, producing 5278 windows (2730 attentive, 2548 distracted). For each window, 15 EEG features were extracted from delta, theta, alpha, and beta band powers across frontal, parietal, and occipital regions, together with theta/alpha ratios. Four machine learning models SVM, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost were evaluated using subjectindependent Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation. SVM achieved the best performance, with mean accuracy of 0.6027 and weighted$\mathbf{F 1}$-score of 0.5669. The results show that attentive windows were classified more successfully than distracted windows, suggesting that distraction is harder to detect with the current feature set. These findings provide a stronger benchmark for EEG-based attention classification in video-based learning under subject-independent evaluation.

title: Prophet-LSTM and SARIMAX-GRU: Hybrid Time Series Forecasting for User Engagement in Python Applications
abstract: User engagement in Python-based applications is a key factor in the enhancement of usability, user satisfaction and strategic planning. Despite being considered valuable, Python usage log data such as timestamps, session counts, functional interactions, and download metrics remain largely unexplored for engagement analysis. Nevertheless, the current analytical methods are mainly concentrated on statistical analysis and do not consider temporal dependencies, irregular usage patterns or domain-specific factors such as feature updates and version release. In addition, most researchers have concentrated on platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok while ignoring Python-based applications. The shortcoming in this area is tackled through the development of a time series forecasting framework based on Python application usage logs. The article discusses three forecasting models, namely the traditional statistical models (ARIMA, SARIMA, and Prophet), deep learning models (LSTM and GRU), and the hybrid models (Prophet-LSTM, SARIMAXGRU, and Prophet-ElasticNet). The study evaluates the effectiveness of these models under different conditions, including sparse logs and bursty activity, to measure their robustness as well as their adoptions in Python-based applications. The methodology of study consists of several stages, including preprocessing, feature extraction, model development, and model evaluation with metrics such as MAE, RMSE, and MAPE. A forecasting tool based on Python was developed using Django, React, REST-API, TensorFlow, and other Python libraries. The results indicate that hybrid models are more effective than statistical and deep learning models, particularly in the case of low-density and bursty conditions, with MAPE values of 6.35% and 8.53%. The study signifies the dwindling of the gap in forecasting accuracy by hybrid residual prediction methods, thus playing a major role for Python developers and product teams in providing valuable insights.

title: An Image-Based CNN Ensemble Approach for Pomegranate Freshness Detection with Explainable AI
abstract: Pomegranates are both profitable and healthy, but their freshness is hard to check. The thick skin hides early damage inside. Fruits are often judged only by the outside, so small signs like dull skin or a bent crown are not noticed. This creates challenges for both sellers and buyers who need to maintain high fruit quality. Therefore, the objective of this study is to propose a deep-learning method to assess pomegranate freshness using images. A set of 4,400 fresh and non-fresh fruits was prepared. The images were cleaned and adjusted to show skin color, texture, and defects. Then, five convolutional neural networks (CNNs) were examined in this study: ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B0, InceptionV4, and MobileNetV3, which were trained on 70% and 80% of percentage split and via 5-fold and 10-fold cross-validation. A separate ensemble model was also created by combining these five CNN architectures. Even though this work focuses on binary classification of fresh vs non-fresh pomegranates, the novelty comes from this ensemble-based approach for pomegranates. Based on the results, ensemble approach achieved the highest accuracy of 98.3% than the individual models. Precision, recall, F1-score, mean absolute error (MAE), and root mean square error (RMSE) also better in the ensemble approach. In addition, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods such as GradCAM, LIME and SHAP were used to show which regions of the fruit guided predictions, allowing us to recommend reliable architectures for real post-harvest quality checking, and the findings suggest lightweight and deployable solutions that can be integrated into real-world applications for post-harvest quality inspection. This provides an opportunity to decrease levels of fruit spoilage, as well as assist produce quality assurance after harvesting.

title: CAL-Log: Calibration-Aware Logarithmic Cost Modeling for Active Learning in Low-Resource NLP
abstract: Building robust NLP systems for low-resource languages remains constrained by the high cost of expert annotation rather than model architecture availability. This paper proposes CAL-Log, a cost-calibrated active learning strategy that jointly accounts for (i) human annotation time and (ii) model miscalibration in early rounds, extending our prior framework for costaware active learning [23] to genuinely low-resource multilingual settings. CAL-Log introduces a logarithmic annotation-cost model to avoid the “cost-collapse” behavior of linear utility-pertoken heuristics, coupled with a calibration-aware uncertainty signal. We evaluate on$\mathbf{1 0}$low-resource text classification datasets spanning 8 languages (Sinhala, Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, Yoruba, Amharic, Swahili, Xhosa) over 3 independent random seeds. Results show that CAL-Log achieves an Efficiency Score of 0.281 F1 per 1,000 minutes (mean ± std:$0.432 \pm 0.217$F1 at$1,535 ~{\min}$), maintaining robust performance across all datasets. Multi-seed ablation confirms that removing the cost model raises annotation cost by$\mathbf{3 9 \%}(+597 ~{\min})$and lowers efficiency to 0.180, while removing temperature calibration yields a less stable learning trajectory. Our stability analysis demonstrates that CAL-Log prevents the seed-dependent performance collapse observed in linear cost models (cross-seed std up to$\pm 0.296$on MasakhaNEWS-sw for CAL-Linear) and achieves superior consistency on morphologically complex tasks such as Sinhala Sentiment$(0.547 \pm 0.033$vs.$0.422 \pm 0.061)$. To our knowledge, this is the first active learning framework to jointly formalize annotation cost collapse and integrate model calibration error into the acquisition function under realistic human-time constraints for low-resource multilingual NLP.

title: The Influence of Artificial Intelligence on Knowledge Process Effectiveness in Sri Lankan State-Owned Banks
abstract: The study examines the influence of artificial intelligence (AI) within state-owned banks in Sri Lanka with a particular focus on its impact on organizational knowledge processes. The paper aims to identify the key factors through which AI influences banking operations and to determine how AI affects the effectiveness of knowledge processes among state-owned banks. Appropriate statistical techniques are employed to analyze the data and the findings are interpreted in relation to the research objectives. The results provide insights into the role of AI in shaping knowledge processes and highlight existing strengths and gaps in AI adoption within the state-owned banking sector. The study contributes to a contextual understanding of AI adoption in a highly regulated public banking environment and offers implications for policy and managerial decision-making.

title: Machine Learning-Based Detection and Intervention of Language and Visual Processing Disorders in Primary School Children
abstract: Learning Disabilities (LD) related to language and visual processing can significantly affect the academic achievement and social development of primary school children, especially when early identification and intervention are limited. In Sri Lanka, the absence of culturally appropriate and technology-driven assessment tools for Sinhala-speaking students further delays timely support. This research introduces 'Nena Sawiya', a web-based assessment and intervention system developed for Grades 3-5 to identify Receptive Language Disorder (RLD), Expressive Language Disorder (ELD), Visual Discrimination and Memory difficulties, and Visual Closure deficits. The system combines interactive, curriculum-aligned tasks with machine learning (ML) based analysis, Natural Language Processing (NLP), and speech-to-text technologies to enable automated assessment and personalized intervention. Random Forest classifiers and regression models were employed for skill-level prediction. Experimental evaluation conducted with$\mathbf{1 8 0 - 2 0 0}$Sinhala-speaking primary school students demonstrated strong performance, with classification accuracies of$\mathbf{8 9 \%}$for ELD,$\mathbf{8 7 \%}$for RLD,$\mathbf{9 5 \%}$for visual discrimination, and$\mathbf{9 2 \%}$for visual closure, while Random Forest regression model achieved$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$values of$\mathbf{0. 8 6}$for ELD and Ridge regression model achieved$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$values of$\mathbf{0. 8 8}$RLD respectively. The results indicate that 'Nena Sawiya' provides an effective, scalable, and culturally relevant solution for early detection and targeted intervention, supporting inclusive and equitable primary education in Sri Lanka.

title: Machine learning for data detection in low-resolution quantization-based systems
abstract: In the ever-evolving world of wireless commu¬nication, the demand for faster, more efficient systems has never been greater. As 5G becomes widespread and the world prepares for 6G, new wireless technologies, such as using many anten¬nas together (massive MIMO) and operating at very high frequencies like millimeter-wave and Tera¬hertz, are becoming increasingly important. These innovations promise unprecedented data rates and connectivity, but they come with a significant challenge: power consumption. At the heart of this issue lies the analog-to-digital converter (ADC), a critical component in wireless base stations that converts the received analog signals into digital signals. High-resolution ADCs, while precise, are power-hungry, consuming energy at levels that threaten the sustainability of next-generation net¬works.

title: Temporal Personal Fashion AI System with Multi-Component Integration
abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has reshaped fashion retail but left gaps in personalized sizing, styling, and grooming solutions. This study presents an integrated, AIpowered ecosystem that addresses these challenges through four interoperable, cloud-based modules. First, wardrobe intelligence uses LSTM networks with multi-head attention to track personal style trends over time and recommends sustainable, wardrobe-centric choices, outperforming standard prediction methods. Second, accurate anthropometric measurements are extracted from dual-view images using EfficientNet-B3, enabling privacy-focused and precise body sizing across brands. Third, occasion-based accessory recommendations are generated by combining ResNet-50 for clothing attribute extraction, Transformer-based cultural modeling, and reinforcement learning to adapt to user feedback. Fourth, specialized CNNs offer comprehensive grooming advice—analyzing facial shape, skin, dental, hair, and nail health—validated by expert professionals. The ecosystem leverages large, diverse datasets and federated learning to ensure scalability and user privacy, resulting in notable reductions in return rates, measurable user savings, and high satisfaction across large deployments.

title: An Interactive Learning Platform to Enhance Student Learning of PLCs and Ladder Programming
abstract: Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) are crucial tools in industrial automation, making it essential for electrical and mechanical engineering students to gain both theoretical and practical knowledge of PLCs and their applications. Typically, automation laboratories are equipped with facilities that allow students to gain practical exposure to PLCs and related sensors and actuators. This study is a part of the project that explores the potential of using artificial intelligence-based solutions and other smart solutions to create an intelligent learning facility for students to perform practical PLCs. The interactive learning facility takes the students on a pre-defined learning path, checking the knowledge, enhancing student knowledge up to the essential level, guiding them to perform the practical, and evaluating them. A student is required to know theories related to sensors, actuators, and ladder programming before performing a lab practical; hence, this project focuses on developing an interactive learning platform (ILP) to teach students the essential prior skills to perform a laboratory practical. As developing skills related to PLC programming is essential in the learning path, and yet no such PLC programming interface is developed with the purpose of practicing students, this study focuses on developing an ‘Interactive Ladder Diagram Interface', a similar platform to commercialized ladder programming software used in PLC programming. The developed ‘Interactive Ladder Diagram Interface’ facilitates ladder programming components, allowing users to build ladder diagrams. While the students are developing ladder diagrams, they are evaluated, and students are offered feedback to develop accurate ladder diagrams and guidance to improve their knowledge of ladder diagrams. The student responses regarding the platform were positive, and they agreed that the developed platforms were helpful in their learning process. Hence, this paper discusses the design and development of an interactive learning platform and an interactive ladder diagram interface for students to learn PLCs

title: Cross-Cultural Emotion-Aware Bilingual Hashtag Generation Using Vision-Language Transformers
abstract: Social media hashtag generation systems face critical limitations in serving multilingual populations, lacking emotion-awareness for affective content matching and training predominantly on Western-centric datasets that introduce demographic bias for underrepresented South Asian users. Existing vision-language models achieve competitive image captioning performance but cannot generate bilingual hashtags conditioned on facial emotions, while hashtag recommendation systems rely on retrieval-based ranking rather than generative synthesis and exhibit cross-lingual contamination in multilingual contexts. This research presents a vision-language transformer integrating ResNet152 visual encoding, four-layer hierarchical cross-attention for multi-scale vision-language fusion, twelve-layer transformer decoder with self-attention and auxiliary emotion and language classifiers within a unified multi-task learning framework. The architecture generates emotion-matched hashtags in English and Sinhala through language embedding injection and explicit auxiliary discrimination, trained on 12,124 facial expression images comprising 40.2 percent South Asian and 59.8 percent global samples across six basic emotions grounded in Paul Ekman's universal emotion theory. The model achieved 75.66 percent token-level accuracy for hashtag generation with perfect emotion classification and complete language separation achieving zero cross-lingual contamination, representing the first model with absolute bilingual disentanglement in multilingual text generation. Multi-task learning analysis revealed a 2.46 percentage point improvement over single-task baselines, confirming synergistic effects from complementary emotion conditioning and language discrimination. The model achieves efficient deployment with 1.25 gigabytes in half-precision format and 0.15 -second inference time. These results demonstrate that emotion-aware bilingual hashtag generation advances cross-cultural artificial intelligence fairness while enabling affective computing applications for underrepresented multilingual populations in global social media contexts.

title: A Systematic Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models for EEG-based Epileptic Seizure Prediction with Clinical Deployment Guidelines
abstract: Epilepsy affects approximately 70 million people worldwide, with unpredictable seizures significantly impacting quality of life. This study presents a systematic comparative evaluation of 20 machine learning and deep learning models for epileptic seizure prediction using the CHB-MIT Scalp EEG Database, with a focus on clinical applicability and computational efficiency across deployment scenarios. Authors evaluated models across five categories: traditional machine learning, deep learning, hybrid architecture, domain adaptation, and optimized models. The dataset comprised 24 patients with 3,500,696 analysis windows, including 1,179 seizure windows and 3,499,517 normal windows, representing extreme class imbalance of 0.034% seizure rate. Our evaluation employed clinical and computational metrics including sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, F1-score, AUC-ROC, false alarm rate per hour, Matthews Correlation Coefficient, training time, and parameter count. Results demonstrate that Support Vector Machine achieved highest accuracy of 97.22% (95% CI: 96.1-98.3%) with perfect sensitivity and only 10 false alarms per hour. Temporal Convolutional Network showed optimal balanced performance with 94.44% across all metrics and 50 false alarms per hour. Our novel Quantized-Tiny model demonstrated exceptional computational efficiency with only 3,937 parameters and 6.3-second training time while maintaining 94.44% accuracy. Statistical validation through 5- fold cross-validation and McNemar's tests confirmed result robustness$(\mathbf{p}<0.001)$. This study provides practical clinical deployment guidelines for cloud-based systems, edge computing, and wearable applications, demonstrating that traditional machine learning can outperform complex deep learning architectures on limited medical datasets.

title: Evaluation of the performance of network-based protein function prediction algorithms on protein-protein interaction networks in plants
abstract: Protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks are used to elucidate functional information of proteins in the absence of experimental data. Many network-based algorithms have been developed for this purpose leveraging the guilt-by-association principle. However, these methods have not been evaluated on plant networks to date. Plant PPI networks differ from those of other organisms due to plant-specific functions such as photosynthesis and root development, etc. Therefore, a systematic evaluation was conducted on six network-based protein function prediction algorithms (majority voting (mv), hishigaki (hm), markov random fields (mrf), random walk (rw), random walk with restart (rwr), and page rank (ppr)) over three plant PPI networks (Arabidopsis thaliana, Oryza sativa japonica, and Zea mays). High-confidence plant PPI networks were obtained from the STRING database, and Gene Ontology (GO) annotations with experimental evidence were sourced from AMIGO. The algorithms were implemented in Python and R, and evaluated using ten-fold cross-validation. Performance was measured on the following metrics: area under the receiver operator curve (AUROC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPR), Fmax, and the average precision (AP). While AUROC scores were generally high (0.6–0.9), AUPR and AP values were lower (0.07–0.5). These values highlighted the challenge posed by class imbalance. Fmaxindicated a more balanced performance (0.1-0.6) since it captures the trade-off between precision and recall. Interestingly, Z. mays excelled in precision–recall based metrics and balanced performance, whereas A. thaliana achieved the highest AUROC scores. Among algorithms, ppr and rwr consistently delivered the best results though simpler methods such as mv and hm occasionally performed competitively, likely due to dataset-specific characteristics. This evaluation highlights the effectiveness of propagation-based algorithms such as ppr and rwr for function prediction in plant PPI networks. Nonetheless, evaluating multiple algorithms remains important, as performance varies across species and network structures.

title: QuanNetDetect: A Quantum Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Encrypted TLS Malicious Traffic Detection
abstract: Transport Layer Security encryption protects over 95% of internet communications but creates detection challenges when malicious actors exploit encrypted channels. Classical machine learning methods struggle with the high-dimensional feature spaces characteristic of TLS metadata, achieving limited accuracy on realworld encrypted traffic. This paper presents QuanNetDetect, the first quantum hybrid deep learning framework specifically designed for detecting malicious patterns in encrypted TLS network traffic. The system integrates quantum neural networks with classical preprocessing through amplitude embedding and strongly entangling layers to process TLS handshake metadata. We implement three model architectures: a quantum neural network for multiclass classification of distributed denial-of-service attacks, a quantum neural network for binary detection of malicious VPN and Tor traffic, and a novel quantum-enhanced gated recurrent unit model for temporal pattern recognition. Evaluation on industrystandard datasets demonstrates 82.83% accuracy for multiclass DDoS classification on CIC-DDoS-2019 and 99.95% accuracy for binary malicious traffic detection on CIC-Darknet-2020, substantially exceeding previous quantum approaches to network security. The framework processes actual packet captures, performs automated feature extraction from encrypted flows, and generates detection reports suitable for security operations. Results provide empirical evidence of quantum computing advantages for analyzing complex encrypted network metadata without payload decryption

title: Understanding Uncertain Spatial Terms for Manipulating Objects on Irregular Plane Surfaces
abstract: Understanding and interpreting spatial geometric terms in relation to human cognition remain a challenging and intriguing area of research. It is difficult to comprehend theway humans generate definitions. Although current state-of-the-art vision-language models can associate terms with text inputs, identifying spatial regions according to human preferences remains challenging. Nevertheless, this multimodal understanding is crucial for making robots more autonomous and reducing the cognitive load on users. Initially, a preliminary human study was conducted to explore human preferences for grounding spatial terms “Left/Right” and “Center”. Insights from this study helped develop a framework with two main branches to ground these terms. Three key features Circular level, Symmetrical level, and Edge Linearity level were identified to define the “Left/Right” regions relative to a given spatial area. By combining these features, fuzzy activations were created to accurately determine the borderline orientation for the left and right regions. All memberships were carefully tuned based on insights from the preliminary study, and the entire grounding process was evaluated through a human subject-based assessment, which ensured alignment with human preferences throughout the framework. Simultaneously, to ground the term “Center”, a fuzzy-based attention map was introduced, along with an evaluation process involving human subjects to verify the accuracy of the proposed framework. The evaluations revealed an overall accuracy of 91.67% for defining “Left/Right” and 65.52% for “Center”. Moreover, grounding these uncertain spatial terms effectively supports human-like decision-making in task execution with open vocabulary inputs, ultimately enhancing the robot’s intelligence and precision.

title: Generative AI adoption and employee empowerment in tourism: ChatGPT use for text-based customer communication and its effects on workplace power dynamics
abstract: This study investigates tourism and hospitality employees' behavioral intentions to adopt ChatGPT for text-based customer communication and examines how generative AI use shapes psychological empowerment and internal power dynamics within service teams. Drawing on a mixed-methods design that integrates survey data from 322 employees in Sri Lanka's tourism sector with qualitative thematic analysis, the study applies an integrated framework combining the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). PLS-SEM results indicate that perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use positively influence employee attitude toward ChatGPT, while attitude, subjective norm, and perceived behavioral control together account for 64.3% of the variance in intention to use. The integrated model demonstrates strong explanatory power, with attitude emerging as the dominant predictor of adoption intention. Qualitative findings reveal that ChatGPT use enhances psychological empowerment across four dimensions: meaning, self-determination, competence, and impact. Critically, increased employee autonomy in communication tasks is accompanied by a redistribution of communicative authority within teams, shifting control from supervisory gatekeepers toward frontline and back-office staff. These results establish that generative AI functions not merely as a productivity instrument but as a structural force reshaping work roles, decision-making authority, and organizational power relations in tourism settings. The study contributes novel empirical evidence at the intersection of AI adoption theory, empowerment theory, and power-agency perspectives in the context of an emerging economy's tourism sector.

title: How energy-efficient UAVs are transforming pesticide spraying
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV), often called “drones”, is one of the modern technologies widely used in different fields such as real-time monitoring, remote sensing, disaster relief operations, delivery of goods, security and surveillance, precision agriculture, and civil infrastructure inspection. Due to global population growth, global food demand increases therefore UAVs are becoming important tools in precision agriculture [1]. UAVs are integrated in farming operations and support a range of tasks including crop monitoring, pesticide and fertilizer spraying, seed sowing and growth evaluation. Equipped with high-resolution cameras and cutting-edge sensors, UAVs can gather real-time data on pest infestations, soil condition, and crop health. From those data about where and when apply inputs such as fertilizers or pesticides, and water ensuring better resource efficiency.

title: Classification of pre-harvest avocado maturity using machine learning assisted polarization-based multispectral imaging
abstract: Avocado (Persea americana) is a climacteric fruit with significant commercial value. This study reports the development of a multispectral imaging system ased on the degree of linear polarization (MSI DoLP) to estimate the physiological maturity level of avocados in situ. The MSI-DoLP employs three light-emitting diodes with center emission wavelengths at 450 nm, 520 nm, and 630 nm. A mobile phone camera served as the imaging device, and two linear polarizers were used to capture DoLP images. A rotating sample holder facilitated imaging of multiple locations of the fruit. The objective was to detect the pre-harvest maturity of an avocado. A cross-sectional study design was used for the experiment. MSI-DoLP was performed on both mature and immature avocados during plucking. amples were obtained from several locations of the central province of Sri Lanka consisting of more than 600 DoLP multispectral measurements on 100 different avocado samples. Partial Least Square Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA), Random Forests, and Support Vector Machines (SVM) were used for the classification. The 630 nm spectral window showed the best sensitivity and selectivity for correctly identifying a mature fruit at the time of harvesting. SVM-based classification recorded the overall best accuracy (82%).

title: Shaping the future of surgical assistance with IoT Robotics: Bot Nurse 1.0
abstract: New Dawn in Surgical Treatment Surgical procedures are essential to healthcare and require high levels of precision, concentra¬tion, and stamina from medical personnel. Extended operations may result in fatigue and raise the risk of human error. The need for dependable assistive technologies is further highlighted by the global shortage of skilled surgical personnel. One crucial technological advancement intended to counteract these challenges is robotic assistance in surgical settings. Despite their advantages, contemporary robotic solutions can occasionally increase the cognitive load on surgeons by requiring them to use modified surgical instruments or remember specific gestures. Tackling these pivotal challenges holistically, Bot Nurse 1.0 unveils a novel methodol-ogy that fuses cutting-edge robotics, Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, speech recognition, and computer vision. This system markedly elevates surgeon-robot engagement by employing instinctive voice commands and accurate palm recognition, seeking to diminish operational intri-cacy, boost surgical efficiency, and reinforce safety outcomes, thus establishing a fresh standard in assistive surgical innovation.

title: Non-Linear Modeling of Ocean-Atmosphere Heat and Energy Fluxes in the Western Indian Ocean: A Machine Learning Approach
abstract: This research leverages 23 years of NASA’s MERRA-2 reanalysis data (August 2002 to May 2025) to model the non-linear diagnostic relationships between latent heat, sensible heat, and kinetic energy fluxes in the Western Indian Ocean. By evaluating multiple machine learning algorithms, the study establishes that Random Forest regression significantly outperforms Gradient Boosting and Neural Network architectures, achieving an R2 of 0.557. The findings reveal that cyclical seasonal patterns driven by monsoonal forcing are the primary predictors of flux variability, accounting for 64.5% of model importance, while also identifying a significant long-term declining trend in sensible heat flux. Ultimately, the work demonstrates that ensemble tree-based methods provide a robust framework for capturing complex air-sea interactions in climatically sensitive regions, offering critical insights for regional marine resource management.

title: Decoding Parkinsonian tremor: An explainable framework integrating spatial and spectral dynamics of multi-revolution spiral drawings
abstract: Parkinson’s disease manifests with motor impairments that are detectable through digitized spiral drawings. This study introduces an explainable framework for Parkinson’s disease screening using a novel radial-sampling feature fusion approach. We transform two-dimensional spiral images into one-dimensional revolution signals via a systematic ray-sampling technique to extract three distinct revolutions. We integrate spatial metrics, such as inter-revolution spacing variability and root mean square radial derivatives, with spectral descriptors derived from fast Fourier transform analysis across low-, mid-, and high-harmonic bands. A total of 20 features were utilized to train state-of-the-art machine learning models, including support vector machines, random forests, and light gradient boosting machines. Among these, the random-forest classifier demonstrated superior performance. Subsequent five-fold cross-validation stability analysis, along with feature importance analysis, identified the root mean square radial derivative of the outer revolution (r3_derive_rms) as the most critical biomarker. Stratified cross-validation demonstrates that combining spatial and frequency features significantly enhances detection accuracy compared to single-domain methods, facilitating effective clinical deployment even in data-scarce environments. This interpretable pipeline provides a robust, low-cost “white-box” screening tool, offering a practical alternative to opaque deep-learning models for early clinical intervention.

title: Boundary Conditions of Cost-Aware Active Learning: A Multi-Dataset Taxonomy of Calibration and Length-Variance Failure Modes
abstract: Active Learning (AL) strategies that incorporate annotation cost, such as the recently proposed CAL-Log heuristic, have demonstrated significant efficiency gains in verbose, document-heavy Data Mining and Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks. However, the stability of cost-aware selection remains poorly understood across the diverse spectrum of linguistic regimes. This paper presents a systematic diagnostic study of CAL-Log's performance boundaries across ten diverse text classification benchmarks, ranging from short-form social media tweets to long-form cinematic reviews. Our analysis reveals that the utility of cost-normalization is governed by a “Variance Law”: substantial gains are realized only when document length variance ($\sigma_{L}$) exceeds a critical threshold ($\sigma_{L} \approx 15$), below which the acquisition engine undergoes “Selection Collapse” and introduces stochastic noise. Furthermore, we identify a “Calibration Trap”—a phenomenon where high Expected Calibration Error (ECE) in high-cardinality tasks causes the learner to prioritize “cheaply wrong” samples, actively undermining the cost-utility tradeoff. We provide a comprehensive taxonomy of these failure modes and introduce a metadata-driven practitioner's decision framework for selecting optimal acquisition strategies. Our findings establish the first empirical boundary conditions for deploying cost-aware active learning in production NLP pipelines.

title: Analysis of loan delinquency prediction based on multinomial logistic regression and random forest
abstract: The banking sector plays a critical role in fostering economic growth by extending credit to individuals and businesses; however, effective loan portfolio management remains a persistent challenge due to the risks associated with Non-Performing Assets (NPAs). Rising NPAs, often driven by economic downturns, inadequate risk assessment, and external shocks, pose a significant threat to financial stability. To address these challenges, this study explores predictive modeling approaches for loan delinquency classification by employing the Multinomial Logistic Regression Model and the Random Forest model applied to 43,644 loan records from a Sri Lankan bank. The analysis categorizes loan performance into four levels, ranging from A0 (performing loans) to D0 (severely delinquent loans), using several financial and demographic variables. Multinomial logistic regression shows that interest rate and loan age are the most influential predictors. The model indicates that a 1% rise in interest rate increases the risk of delinquency by 5.7 21.1%, while each additional month of loan age amplifies the likelihood by 27 76%. Delays in recovery also significantly elevate risk for severely delinquent loans, with each additional day of delay associated with a 1.2% increase in default probability. The model demonstrates excellent discriminatory power at the performance extremes (AUC: 0.987 for A0 and 0.996 for D0). The Random Forest model considers the loan status as a binary (current vs. delinquent) variable. An 80:20 training-testing split was used for data analysis. The performance of the model was evaluated using a confusion matrix, AUC-ROC curves, and accuracy metrics on a testing set. The Random Forest model pidenterforms better in overall predictive accuracy, with a low 1.55% out-of-bag error rate. It achieves 99.4% accuracy in classifying current loans and 96.6% for delinquent loans. Variable importance analysis confirms loan age, recovery date, and interest rate as dominant predictors. Our study is cross-sectional, with predictor variables measured at a defined observation point for each loan. Class imbalance is a limitation; to address this, we plan to apply class weighting and evaluate model performance using accuracy metrics in future work. Collectively, the models underscore the predictive strength of time-dependent variables (loan age and recovery delays) and financial indicators (interest rates, outstanding amounts). While multinomial logistic regression offers nuanced insight into risk progression across multiple categories, Random Forest delivers robust binary classification performance.

title: A comparative analysis of time series models for predicting the S&P SL 20 index of the Colombo stock exchange (CSE)
abstract: The performance of stock markets is influenced by various factors, and understanding these dynamics is crucial for investors and policymakers. This research centers on Sri Lanka's capital market, with particular attention to the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE), and analyzes the influence of the Standard & Poor's Sri Lanka 20 (S&P SL 20) index, which represents the top 20 leading companies listed on the CSE. Specifically, the primary objective of this research is to compare the effectiveness of traditional time series models with machine learning and deep learning models in predicting the S&P SL 20 index. These models, developed using computerized programs, are evaluated based on their predictive performance within the context of the CSE. The study will use daily S&P SL 20 stock index data obtained from the CSE data library enclosing the period 2010 to 2018. This methodology compares Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), which is a traditional time series model and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), which is a recurrent neural network model. In this research, the Python language will be employed for analysis. The ARIMA and LSTM models are evaluated using three performance metrics: MAE, MAPE, and RMSE. ARIMA slightly outperforms LSTM in MAE (233.96 vs. 249.37) and RMSE (269.57 vs. 269.86), which essentially indicates better overall accuracy in absolute and squared error terms. However, LSTM achieves a marginally lower MAPE (6.96% vs. 7.04%), showing fewer relative percentage errors. All in all, both models offer similar performances, with minor differences depending on the metric. Both ARIMA and LSTM show strengths in predicting the S&P SL 20 Index. ARIMA excels in minimizing absolute errors (MAE), ideal for linear trends. LSTM’s lower MAPE highlights its ability to capture nonlinear patterns. With similar RMSE values, both handle overall errors well. ARIMA’s constant predictions in some periods reveal its limitations with limited or weak trend data. The choice depends on the forecasting goal: ARIMA for linear trends and LSTM for complex patterns.

title: AI-Driven Post-Disaster Communication: A Review of ML, NLP, and GIS for Crisis Triage and Dispatch Support
abstract: Post-disaster communication remains a critical challenge in emergency response, as traditional reporting channels are often fragmented, overloaded, and slow, causing delays in situational awareness, triage, and coordination. This paper presents a structured review of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven post-disaster communication research from 2020 to 2025, focusing on machine learning, natural language processing, and geospatial information system approaches for crisis message classification, urgency detection, geolocation extraction, and priority-aware routing. The review analyses limitations of traditional systems, compares AI-based techniques, and synthesizes commonly used datasets and benchmarking practices. Key outcomes indicate that machine learning classifiers achieve F1-scores above 0.92 for relevant message detection, transformer-based natural language processing models provide robust contextual understanding with F1 greater than 0.95 for urgent message classification, and GIS-enabled platforms enhance situational awareness and prioritization in real-time mapping of people in need. Despite these advances, challenges remain, including noisy short-text data, class imbalance, limited multilingual support, weak cross-event generalization, and insufficient operational validation. This review consolidates fragmented literature, highlights current research gaps, and outlines future directions for developing scalable, inclusive, and deployment-ready post-disaster communication systems.

title: A Unified Framework for Joint Feature Selection and Hyperparameter Optimization in LSTM Networks using a Multi-Objective Modified Firefly Algorithm
abstract: The performance of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks in financial time series forecasting is heavily dependent on two interdependent factors: the selection of input features and the configuration of network hyperparameters. Existing methodologies treat these as isolated sequential problems, optimizing one while holding the other fixed, which guarantees a suboptimal convergence. This paper introduces a Multi-Objective Modified Firefly Algorithm (MOMFA) that executes joint feature selection and hyperparameter optimization as a single unified search. Candidate solutions are encoded as 30-dimensional vectors combining a discrete binary feature mask with continuous hyperparameter spaces. The standard Firefly Algorithm is modified via Lévy flight exploration and a sigmoid transfer function to bridge the continuous and discrete search spaces. Optimizing for both forecast accuracy (RMSE) and model complexity, the framework generates a Pareto-optimal set of network configurations.

title: IEMS: An AI-Framework Fusing IoT, Deep Learning, and LLMs for Multi-Domain Urban Environmental Monitoring and Actionable Sustainability Insights
abstract: Rapid urbanization presents significant environmental challenges including air pollution, diminished green spaces, noise, and CO2 emissions, demanding integrated monitoring. This paper introduces the Intelligent EcoUrban Monitoring System (IEMS), an AI-driven framework designed for comprehensive urban environmental assessment. The research contribution is an integrated platform that synergistically combines diverse AI techniques with multi-source data to overcome limitations of siloed monitoring and provide actionable intelligence for urban sustainability. IEMS employs four specialized components: EcoSensor AI (IoT-based air/CO2 analysis), GreenVision AI (satellite imagebased green space assessment), NoiseGuard AI (urban noise classification/forecasting), and EcoGo AI (vehicle CO2 estimation/LLMdriven mitigation advice), all interconnected via a central data fusion pipeline. This architecture enables cross-domain analysis and enhanced predictive capabilities. Evaluation demonstrated robust performance: air quality forecasting achieved R2 > 0.89, green space segmentation yielded an F1-score of 96.60%, and multi-label noise classification showed >91% accuracy, enabling informed decision-making for urban planners and policymakers. IEMS offers a significant step towards data-driven sustainable urban development, with future work focusing on edge deployment and enhanced multi-modal data fusion.

title: A Unified Framework for Joint Feature Selection and Hyperparameter Optimization in LSTM Networks using a Multi-Objective Modified Firefly Algorithm
abstract: The performance of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks in financial time series forecasting is heavily dependent on two interdependent factors: the selection of input features and the configuration of network hyperparameters. Existing methodologies treat these as isolated sequential problems, optimizing one while holding the other fixed, which guarantees a suboptimal convergence. This paper introduces a Multi-Objective Modified Firefly Algorithm (MOMFA) that executes joint feature selection and hyperparameter optimization as a single unified search. Candidate solutions are encoded as 30-dimensional vectors combining a discrete binary feature mask with continuous hyperparameter spaces. The standard Firefly Algorithm is modified via Lévy flight exploration and a sigmoid transfer function to bridge the continuous and discrete search spaces. Optimizing for both forecast accuracy (RMSE) and model complexity, the framework generates a Pareto-optimal set of network configurations.
