title: An Ensemble Machine Learning Framework for Real-Time Procrastination Pattern Detection in Academic Desktop Environments
abstract: Academic procrastination affects 75–95% of university students worldwide, yet automated detection systems remain limited to binary classifications derived from coarse metrics, failing to distinguish clinically relevant procrastination archetypes or adapt to individual behavioral baselines. This paper presents the Procrastination Pattern Detection Intelligence System (PPDIS) an ensemble machine learning pipeline that passively classifies daily student behavior into five procrastination archetypes grounded in established psychological theories including Temporal Motivation Theory (TMT), Delay Discounting, and Attention Control Theory (ACT). The pipeline integrates a pre-initialized Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM), an XGBoost multi-class classifier, and an Isolation Forest into a unified 0-10 procrastination score, supplemented by an LSTM next-day predictor and per-user adaptive retraining. A study involving 14 undergraduate students over 21 days produced 280 real behavioral samples. SMOTE augmentation yielded a 355sample balanced training set. Five-fold stratified cross-validation achieved weighted accuracy of 88.1% (95% CI:$84.4 \%-91.8 \%$), weighted$\mathrm{F} 1=0.876$, and macro$\mathrm{F} 1=0.848$. A Wilcoxon signedrank test confirms statistically significant improvement over a naive majority-class baseline ($p=0.031$, Cohen's$d=2.41$). A prospective power analysis determines$N=47$participants for definitive evaluation at 80% power.

title: AI-Based Accident Detection and Severity Classification System with Passenger Awareness
abstract: Vehicular accidents and their severity level, including the number of passengers, need to be quickly and accurately identified for prompt action. Current solutions provide location information about accidents, but do not give information about the severity of the crash or the number of passengers. Therefore, this paper introduces a comprehensive IoT-based Accident Detection and Severity Classification System, where machine learning and computer vision techniques are integrated. An MPU6050 accelerometer/gyroscope installed in a vehicle identifies vehicular crashes, and a Random Forest classifier is used to classify the severity of crashes, including Low, Medium, and High, based on G-forces and crash duration. At the same time, a camera installed in the vehicle utilizes YOLOv5 to count the number of passengers within the vehicle. As soon as a crash is identified, a message is sent to emergency services with information about the location, severity, and number of passengers. Experiments conducted by crashing a vehicle in various locations demonstrate that the system can quickly detect crashes and accurately classify their severity levels, similar to previous works.

title: Akura: Dyslexia Aware Sinhala Essay Grading System
abstract: Automated Essay Scoring (AES) improves assessment scalability, but most systems are optimized for rater agreement rather than equitable outcomes for neurodiverse learners. This challenge is more pronounced in low-resource languages such as Sinhala, where orthographic complexity and surface-form variation can lead to unfair penalization of dyslexic writing. This paper presents Akura, a dyslexia-aware Sinhala AES framework that integrates dyslexic writing-pattern classification, context-aware sentence reconstruction, biasaware semantic scoring, and multimodal feedback generation. The framework combines human-in-the-loop reconstruction with XLM-RoBERTa-based rubric-aligned scoring and fairness monitoring using Statistical Parity Difference (SPD) and Disparate Impact Ratio (DIR). By unifying detection, controlled normalization, fairness-aware scoring, and accessible feedback, Akura provides a practical approach for inclusive essay assessment in low-resource educational settings.

title: An Agentic AI-Driven Adaptive Intelligent Tutoring System using Reinforcement Learning, Emotionaware Vision, and RAG-Based Content Generation
abstract: Current intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) primarily rely on performance-based metrics and rule-based strategies, limiting their ability to adapt in real time to changes in learner engagement and behavior. This paper proposes an Adaptive Intelligent Tutoring System (AITS) that integrates four key components: (i) a computer vision-based student engagement detection module, (ii) a reinforcement learning (RL)-based decision engine, (iii) an agentic AI core for multi-step, goaloriented instructional planning, and (iv) a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based content generation layer. The system continuously monitors learner states using visual and contextual signals, enabling dynamic representation of attention, confusion, and boredom. A Deep Q-Network (DQN)based RL model selects optimal pedagogical actions. The agentic AI core then refines these actions into structured instructional strategies through multi-step planning and context-aware reasoning. A hybrid intervention trigger mechanism, based on engagement thresholds and time-on-task, is introduced to prevent unnecessary interruptions and maintain learner autonomy. Personalized instructional content is generated using Gemini Flash 3.0 within a RAG framework to ensure contextual relevance and accuracy. The system was evaluated using both simulated learner environments and a real-user study involving 15 participants. The proposed AITS achieved an Engagement Stability Index of 0.81, a Modality Adaptation Speed of 32 seconds representing a 57% reduction compared to rule-based approaches, an Intervention Success Rate of 0.76 exceeding the target threshold of 0.70, and a learning gain of +24.2 percentage points compared to$\boldsymbol{+} \mathbf{1 4. 3}$for rule-based and$\boldsymbol{+} \mathbf{8. 2}$for non-adaptive systems. These results demonstrate that integrating reinforcement learning, engagement-aware perception, agentic planning, and adaptive content generation provides a scalable and effective framework for real-time intelligent tutoring.

title: Topology-Aware Predictive Autoscaling for Kubernetes Microservices Using Deep Learning
abstract: Cloud-native applications widely use microservice architectures deployed on platforms such as Kubernetes. However, the commonly used Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) works using a reactive scaling method. It increases or decreases resources only after system metrics like CPU usage reach a threshold. Because of this reactive behavior, scaling often happens with a delay when workloads suddenly increase. This delay can cause performance problems, service bottlenecks, and violations of Service Level Objectives (SLOs), especially in microservice systems where services depend on each other. In addition, traditional autoscaling methods mainly rely on resource metrics such as CPU and memory, which do not capture the relationships between services. To solve this problem, this research proposes a topology-aware predictive autoscaling framework called the Smart Auto Scaler. The system analyzes service dependency graphs and combines topology features with resource metrics to predict future resource needs using deep learning models. This approach enables proactive autoscaling, helping improve system reliability and resource efficiency in Kubernetes-based microservice environments. The proposed approach improves prediction accuracy and reduces under- and over-provisioning, enabling proactive autoscaling that enhances system reliability and resource efficiency in Kubernetes microservice environments.

title: LankaLens: A Mobile-Based Heritage Exploration System for Artifact Reconstruction and Location Tracking
abstract: Digital technologies are increasingly used to enhance visitor engagement and interpretation at archaeological heritage sites. However, many locations still lack integrated mobile systems that combine immersive visualization with structured on-site exploration. The main objective of this research is to develop a mobile-based heritage exploration system that integrates mixed reality reconstruction with real-time location-aware navigation. This study presents LankaLens, an Android-based application that supports two key components: mixed reality artifact visualization using QR-triggered reconstruction and a real-time user location tracking and exploration map system. The system integrates geolocation services, QR-based verification, and cloudsupported exploration tracking to improve visitor interaction with heritage environments. Sigiriya, Sri Lanka, is used as the primary implementation environment. The results demonstrate that the system achieved GPS accuracy between 6.5 m and 8.6 m with geofence detection delays ranging from 1.3 s to 2.1 s, while maintaining 100 % successful QR-based visit verification. These findings confirm the effectiveness of integrating mixed reality visualization with real-time location-aware navigation in heritage environments.

title: Huruwa: an AI-IoT Robotic System for Adaptive Speech Therapy and Parental Support for Sinhala-Speaking Children with Speech Sound Disorders
abstract: Early phonological intervention for Sinhalaspeaking children with speech sound disorders requires scalable, engaging tools that bridge clinical expertise and home practice; however, low-resource language constraints limit available solutions. This paper introduces Huruwa, an AI-IoT robotic platform designed to support speech therapy for Sinhala-speaking children. The system integrates LLM-guided conversational interaction, phoneme-adaptive exercises (80-90% task suitability), and SVM-RBF-based phoneme error detection achieving 78% accuracy. It further employs knowledge-graph-driven therapy generation and a RAG-based parent guidance system to deliver grounded, hallucination-controlled support. Evaluations confirm real-time feasibility across components, offering a deployable model for Sinhala child speech therapy in resource-limited settings like Sri Lanka.

title: AI-Enabled Lost and Found System With Adaptive Retrieval and Intelligent Security Monitoring
abstract: The existing lost and found systems in public environment remain due to manual reporting, keyword-based search and lack of intelligent quality control and security monitoring. This work presents an AI powered lost and found platform designed as a unified modular system integrated with four components as Uncertainty-Aware Cascaded Retrieval (UACR), proactive multimodal input validation, real-time suspicious behavior detection and device behavior anomaly detection with predictive risk analytics. The UACR module incorporates Monte Carlo Dropout-based entropy estimation to measure classification uncertainty and dynamically adapt retrieval strategies between category restricted Facebook AI Similarity Search (FAISS) search and Contrastive Language Image Pre-training (CLIP) based semantic re-ranking. The multimodal validation module evaluates image quality, text, coherence, voice clarity and cross-model consistency, achieving 94% accuracy on 500 submissions (${p}<0.001$). The surveillance module combines YOLO11 detection, multi-object tracking, and spatio-temporal rules to detect unattended objects and abnormal behaviors in real time. Device behavior modeling using Isolation Forest achieved an AUC of 0.937, while XGBoost-based risk prediction reached a ROC-AUC of 0.924 with online improvement over time. By integrating uncertainty modeling, multimodal validation, temporal reasoning, and predictive analytics within a single architecture, the proposed system moves beyond reactive matching toward a more proactive framework.

title: ALTRUS - Adaptive Life-Support and Therapeutic Robotic Unit System
abstract: Assistive mobile robots are becoming increasingly important for supporting independent living and continuous healthcare monitoring in domestic environments. However, existing approaches remain largely fragmented, with navigation, human-robot interaction (HRI), sensor integration, and system reliability often engineered as isolated subsystems, thereby increasing overall complexity, limiting reproducibility, and reducing operational robustness. This paper presents ALTRUS, a unified modular assistive robotic architecture implemented on Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2), built upon four reusable, developer-oriented frameworks designed to enable rapid robot construction across diverse hardware configurations: (i) an adaptive navigation framework combining hybrid simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM)-based localization with multimodal voice and gesture command fusion; (ii) a configurable firmware generation framework enabling IoT-based health monitoring through template-driven ESP32 code synthesis; (iii) a multimodal emotion-aware interaction framework incorporating facial and vocal affect recognition with context-aware empathetic response generation; and (iv) a fault-tolerant middleware backbone supporting deterministic intent arbitration, proactive subsystem recovery, and blockchain-backed immutable runtime logging. Together, these frameworks establish a layered architecture that bridges perception, cognition, interaction, and safety management within a single deployable platform. A declarative configuration model further enables rapid customization across diverse robot morphologies while preserving modularity and reusability. Experimental validation demonstrates reliable navigation, real-time multimodal interaction, continuous health data streaming, and resilient operation under induced fault conditions, providing a scalable foundation for next-generation assistive robotic development.

title: A Hybrid Multi-Modal AI Framework for Insider Threat Detection in Hybrid Work Environments
abstract: Hybrid work environments have significantly expanded organizational attack surfaces, increasing the risk of insider threats such as data exfiltration, privilege abuse, and anomalous behavioral patterns across distributed systems. Traditional security solutions, including rule-based intrusion detection and Data Loss Prevention (DLP) systems, are limited in their ability to adapt to dynamic user behavior and often suffer from high false-positive rates and lack of contextual awareness. This research proposes a unified AI-driven insider threat detection framework that integrates multi-modal anomaly detection techniques with platform-aware monitoring and integrity assurance mechanisms. The proposed system combines two key components: a Data Exfiltration Monitoring Framework (DEMF), which focuses on detecting anomalies in GitHub and Microsoft 365 (M365) environments using Autoencoders and OneClass Support Vector Machines, and a Behavioral and Communication Anomaly Analysis System (BCAAS), which leverages Transformer-based temporal modeling, Graph Neural Networks for relational analysis, and XGBoost classification enhanced with Evidential Deep Learning for uncertainty quantification. To further enhance reliability and trust, the framework incorporates a blockchain-based module for tamper-proof logging of high-confidence alerts, ensuring integrity and non-repudiation of forensic evidence. The system is evaluated using real-world datasets, including CERT Insider Threat datasets, LANL authentication logs, and platform-specific audit logs, enabling comprehensive detection of both known and previously unseen threats. Experimental results demonstrate improvements in accuracy, F1-score, and reduction of false positives compared to traditional systems. The proposed framework contributes a scalable, privacypreserving, and explainable solution for insider threat detection, addressing the challenges of modern hybrid work environments.

title: AI-Powered VR Platform for Interactive Learning and Immersive Exploration of Historical Events
abstract: Sri Lanka possesses a rich cultural heritage spanning more than two millennia. However, access to accurate, engaging, and context-aware historical knowledge remains limited for many learners and visitors. Conventional heritage interpretation methods such as guidebooks, static displays, and generic digital content often fail to provide spatial accuracy, temporal relevance, or personalized engagement. To address these limitations, this paper presents an Artificial Intelligence (AI) powered Virtual Reality (VR) platform for interactive learning and immersive exploration of historical events. The core contribution of this work is a tightly integrated architecture that combines geo-temporal personalization using GPS based location detection and era-based temporal filtering, a hybrid conversational AI system combining Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with LoRA fine tuning of the Mistral-7B language model on a$\mathbf{2, 0 4 6}$event Sri Lankan heritage dataset a spatially synchronized dual era VR environment enabling seamless transitions between modern and historical scenes, and an emotionally intelligent character framework that synchronizes AI-generated speech with procedurally generated gestures (Language of Motion, SMPL-X). Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed hybrid RAG and LoRA system outperforms all baseline configurations, achieving a BERTScore of 0.924 and cultural accuracy of 88.5%, while the K-Means clustering module attains a silhouette score of$\mathbf{0. 5 7 1 9}$. The platform is optimized for deployment on mid-range mobile VR hardware through multi-resolution asset streaming, level of detail management, and additive scene loading. Results confirm the feasibility of delivering personalized, immersive, and scalable cultural heritage experiences on mobile platforms

title: Real-Time Vehicle Fault Detection Using Acoustic Analysis and Machine Learning
abstract: Early detection of vehicle engine faults is important for preventing mechanical failures and reducing maintenance costs. Conventional diagnostic systems often require specialised hardware, trained technicians, and time-consuming inspection procedures. This paper presents an automated vehicle fault detection system based on acoustic signal analysis and machine learning, designed for practical, low-cost deployment. The proposed system follows a two-stage classification architecture. In the first stage, a pretrained audio classification model, YAMNet, verifies whether the input audio contains vehicle-related sounds. In the second stage, Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), delta, and delta-delta features are extracted to form a 150-dimensional feature vector, which is subsequently classified by an XGBoost model to identify the fault category. The system targets three fault classes: engine knocking, engine misfire, and belt squeal. Evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation on a dataset of 418 samples derived from 72 original recordings through augmentation, the system achieves a mean classification accuracy of 93.54%$(\pm \text{2. 3 1 \%})$with a mean inference latency of approximately$\text{2 - 3}$seconds per sample. While the proposed contribution is primarily incremental and the dataset remains limited in scale, the results demonstrate that combining pretrained audio verification with handcrafted acoustic features and gradient boosting provides a practical baseline for accessible, mobile-assisted vehicle diagnostics. Limitations regarding dataset diversity, generalisability, and absence of large-scale benchmarking are acknowledged and discussed.

title: PulseTrack AI: A Predictive Multi-Layer Decision Framework for Edge-Based Boundary Intrusion Verification Under Uncertainty
abstract: Reliable boundary intrusion verification in rural edge environments is difficult because sensing is imperfect, communication is intermittent, and false positives rapidly erode operator trust. Existing intrusion monitoring systems often rely on reactive triggers, vision-heavy analytics, or generic multisensor fusion pipelines that do not explicitly model uncertainty or exploit predictive context. This paper presents PulseTrack AI, a predictive multi-layer decision framework for edge-based boundary intrusion verification under uncertainty. PulseTrack AI operates as a dedicated boundary verification layer that confirms whether an approaching entity has physically crossed a protected zone. The framework combines ETA-guided activation, sequential radar tripwire reasoning, range-gated spatial confirmation, piezoelectric impact evidence, confidence-weighted semantic decision states, fault-aware degradation, temporal stability control, and a fail-safe autonomous sentinel mode. The paper contributes a deployment-grounded architectural formulation for predictive verification using low-cost sensors, positions the framework against prior work in reactive sensing and conventional sensor fusion, and presents evaluation using real event timelines, controlled component-level field trials, and simulation under noise and sensor failure. Controlled trials achieved 88.3% overall verification accuracy, while simulation indicated lower false positive exposure and improved decision stability compared with reactive and single-sensor baselines. The work argues that reliable intrusion verification can be achieved at the edge not by assuming trustworthy sensors, but by explicitly structuring how uncertain evidence is activated, interpreted, and constrained.

title: AI-Driven Fabric Defect Detection & Monitoring System for the Appeal Industry in Sri Lanka
abstract: This paper introduces FabricVision, an AIdriven quality monitoring system designed to enhance fabric inspection processes in Sri Lanka's apparel industry. By automating the traditional manual and inconsistent inspection of fabric rolls, the system supports pre-seam fabric quality assessment through the integration of high-resolution imaging, motion-aware frame selection, edge-level fog processing and advanced deep learning models. Intelligent fabric capture combined with anomaly pre-screening and lightweight quality analytics ensures that only reliable and meaningful fabric data is processed, improving inspection efficiency. An edge-level fog processing layer further supports this pipeline by performing adaptive image enhancement based on fabric appearance characteristics, improving visual consistency before defect analysis. You Only Look Once is employed for real-time detection and localization of defects such as holes, stains and fabric irregularities, enabling meter-level mapping of flaws on fabric rolls. Beyond defect detection, the system improves inspection consistency, reduce latency, and support proactive quality control through predictive and prescriptive analytics that integrate detection results with temporal trend analysis. In doing so, the system delivers a practical and scalable solution for fabric quality monitoring in resource-constrained apparel manufacturers.

title: Sinhala Learn: AI-Based Education Assistant for Sinhala Resources
abstract: This paper presents an AI-powered educational assistant built specifically for Sinhala medium education in Sri Lanka. The system brings together four main components: document processing with semantic embedding, text-based question answering and summarization, voice interaction, and automated answer evaluation. The document processing module uses YOLOv8 for layout analysis alongside hybrid OCR, Tesseract for printed text and TrOCR for handwriting followed by embedding generation via Gemini. For question answering and summarization, a RAG pipeline combines BM25 keyword matching with semantic embeddings, plus grade-level adaptive summarization that adjusts vocabulary complexity and includes safety checks afterward. The voice module fine-tunes Whisper for Sri Lankan accents, adding a Southern dialect normalization layer and converting conversational Sinhala to written form. Answer evaluation runs through a controlled grading engine that scores based on semantic similarity, concept relevance, and coverage using deterministic scoring rather than generative model outputs to keep things explainable. All components sit on a unified backend with PostgreSQL and pgvector, supporting both online and limited offline use. Evaluated using OCR metrics, semantic similarity, and retrieval accuracy, the system tackles challenges in Sinhala edtech like OCR noise, accent variation, hallucination prevention, and transparent grading offering a foundation for AI-driven education in low-resource language settings.

title: Agri-Sense: Autonomous Tomato Farming Robotic Vehicle
abstract: The precision greenhouse cultivation of tomatoes is often hindered by the expensive labor costs, the easy spread of diseases, and the unavailability of robust digital technologies. This paper proposes Agri-Sense, a comprehensive autonomous robotic system that covers the entire scope of greenhouse management. The system includes a robotic platform that allows the crops to be traversed autonomously without the need for human input. The ripeness and leaf disease detection are done using advanced YOLO-based computer vision techniques. The robotic arm has 4 degrees of freedom, which includes a modular gripper and a precise sprayer system for disease treatment. This reduces the usage of chemicals and protects the healthy crops from disease. To solve the problem of connectivity in rural greenhouse environments, the system includes a sensor mesh using LoRa sensors and a Software-Defined Networking controller. This controller uses Quality of Service and VPN tunnels to provide robust communication services even in the presence of unreliable connectivity. Experimental results showed that the proposed system bridges the gap between passive monitoring and autonomous greenhouse management. The system is robust and efficient in greenhouse management.

title: Phoneme-Based Accent-Adaptive Speech Recognition for Accurate and Mispronunciation Feedback
abstract: The increasing use of online meeting platforms has intensified the need for clear spoken communication, particularly among non-native English speakers. While modern Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems provide accurate transcription, they offer limited support for pronunciation assessment in spontaneous multi-speaker environments. This paper presents a hybrid accent-adaptive pronunciation detection framework for post-meeting analysis of South Asian English speech. The proposed system integrates commercial ASR transcription with a fine-tuned Whisper model to improve accent robustness, and combines word-level confidence scoring with phoneme-level alignment using the Montreal Forced Aligner and the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary. A hybrid decision mechanism incorporating confidence thresholds and phoneme deviation analysis is further enhanced with an accent-aware filtering strategy to reduce false positives. Experimental evaluation on multi-speaker meeting recordings demonstrates a significant reduction in false positive rate and improved pronunciation detection accuracy. The framework maintains computational efficiency suitable for post-meeting deployment while providing interpretable, sound-level diagnostic feedback. The results confirm that hybrid confidence-phoneme integration offers a practical and scalable solution for automated post-meeting pronunciation feedback in multi-speaker online meeting environments.

title: Hemora: Multi-Modal Deep Learning Approach for Automated Hematological Disease Detection
abstract: Hematological diseases, including Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL), Beta-Thalassemia (Minor), Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA), and Sickle Cell Disease (SCD), raise significant health challenges in Sri Lanka due to diagnostic delays and limited specialist access. This research introduces “Hemora,” an integrated deep learning framework designed to automate the identification of these disorders by combining microscopic blood smear image analysis with Complete Blood Count (CBC) data. Using a multi-modal approach with hybrid architectures such as CNN, YOLO, and EfficientNet the system was developed to detect critical morphological abnormalities: lymphoblasts in ALL, target cells and hypochromia in BetaThalassemia, microcytosis and pencil-shaped cells in IDA, and sickle-shaped red blood cells in SCD. Trained on local datasets to reflect Sri Lankan patient populations, the web-based solution facilitates rapid processing and real-time output, significantly reducing the diagnostic timeline from several days to a rapid result. The system achieved classification accuracies of$96.9 \%(\text{mAP})$and 75% for ALL detection and classification respectively, 94% for Beta-Thalassemia, 75% for SCD, and$\mathbf{9 3 \%}$for IDA. Preliminary results confirm the system's potential to minimize human error and provide essential diagnostic support in low-resource clinical settings.

title: An Integrated Machine Learning and Clinical Analysis System for Kidney Disease Prediction and Management
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is an increasing public health issue in Sri Lanka, where late identification and disjointed clinical practices often contribute to unsatisfactory patient outcomes. This research introduces a comprehensive artificial intelligence-driven decision support system designed for the early detection, continuous monitoring, and effective management of CKD. The proposed framework brings together four core components: urine dipstick test analysis, clinical kidney image analysis, prediction of disease progression based on lifestyle factors, and intelligent donor-recipient matching. Advanced deep learning approaches are used for image-based tasks, including YOLOv8 segmentation paired with a dualchannel Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for interpreting urine dipstick results, along with a U-Net CNN for segmenting kidney ultrasound images and assessing structural features. In addition, machine learning models such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression, and Gradient Boosting are employed for lifestyle risk assessment and donor-recipient compatibility prediction. The lifestyle prediction model achieved an accuracy of 89.5%, urine dipstick analysis recorded an accuracy of 88.12% across eight parameters, donor-recipient matching reached$\mathbf{8 9. 2 \%}$accuracy, and ultrasound-based CKD severity classification achieved 91.27% accuracy. By bringing together clinical, imaging, lifestyle, and transplant-related information into a single platform, the proposed system enables thorough risk assessment, tailored clinical interventions, and reliable decisionmaking. This integrated approach offers a scalable and costeffective solution for enhancing the management of CKD, particularly in a healthcare setting where resources are limited, as effective and affordable solutions are greatly required for patient care.

title: Smart Solar Advisor: AI-Driven IoT-Based System for Location-Aware Monthly Energy Forecasting
abstract: Recent advances in Internet of Things technologies and machine learning, including real-time monitoring of environmental conditions, have greatly improved the accuracy of renewable energy forecasting via data-supported predictions. This paper introduces the Smart Solar Advisor, an IoT and site-specific based assessment framework for estimating the expected monthly energy production of solar photovoltaic systems developed prior to their installation. A sensor-based module collects environmental measurements at the site level via the Internet to a central server. The server processes input data to perform validation, normalization of data and anomaly detection to achieve consistent and reliable input data. These processed input data are then supplied to a trained regression model using the XGBoost algorithm deployed as a serialized artefact, which outputs an accurate estimation of the expected monthly energy generation of the solar photovoltaic system. Furthermore, the use of nearby site similarities enables more reliable predictions in areas that do not have enough historical data by referencing locations with similar geography. The framework serves as a practical, accurate decision-support tool to assist users in assessing solar potential, supporting sustainable energy use while making informed decisions on where to invest.

title: AloeGreen: Smart IOT-Based System for Aloe Vera
abstract: Agriculture plays a vital role in food security, yet Aloe vera cultivation remains vulnerable to environmental variability, nutrient imbalance, disease occurrence, and unstable market conditions. This study presented AloeGreen, a crop-specific AI–IoT smart agriculture framework designed to support Aloe vera cultivation through integrated sensing, forecasting, and decision-support modules. The system combined real-time IoT-based field monitoring with machine learning models for yield prediction, environmental forecasting, disease detection, fertilizer recommendation, and price forecasting. A key contribution of the study was a forecast-informed yield prediction strategy in which short-term environmental forecasts were incorporated into the yield estimation pipeline to support future-aware decision-making. In addition, domain-specific agronomic features, including water stress and heat stress indices, were introduced to better represent Aloe vera growth conditions. For the yield prediction module, the cleaned hourly cultivation dataset contained 1,048,330 observations after removing missing critical fields and duplicates. Experimental results showed that XGBoost achieved the best yield prediction performance with an RMSE of$\mathbf{1 0. 0 2}$and an$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$of$\mathbf{0. 8 9 2}$, while the environmental forecasting module achieved strong performance for temperature and humidity prediction, although rainfall prediction remained comparatively weaker. The disease detection module achieved balanced classification performance of approximately 77% accuracy, and Random Forest performed best in both price forecasting and fertilizer recommendation tasks. Overall, the findings showed that integrating IoT sensing with intelligent analytics in a unified Aloe vera cultivation platform can improve decision support, reduce uncertainty, and contribute to more sustainable smart agriculture practices.

title: Aquanext: Intelligent Aquaculture Based on IoT and AI for Sustainable Shrimp Farming in Sri Lanka
abstract: Shrimp aquaculture is economically significant in Sri Lanka, yet smallholder farms frequently experience production losses due to limited continuous water-quality monitoring, inefficient feeding strategies, delayed disease-risk detection, and fragmented decision-making processes. This study proposes an integrated Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT)-based framework designed to support sustainable and cost-effective shrimp farming under resourceconstrained conditions. The system consists of four coordinated modules: (1) water-quality prediction and automated control, (2) acoustic-based feeding optimization, (3) multimodal stress and disease-risk screening, and (4) AI-driven decision support. The water-quality module was evaluated using operational-style datasets under time-aware validation protocols, achieving a 6 hour dissolved oxygen forecasting performance of ${R}^{{2}} \boldsymbol{=} {0. 9 4}$ (MAE $=0.31 \text{mg} / \mathrm{L})$ , while ammonia-risk classification reached 91.3 % accuracy with an average lead time of 14.2 hours. The feeding module, validated using a leakage-aware experimental setup across multiple pond environments, achieved $95.2 \% \pm 1.3 \%$ classification accuracy. Extended pilot deployments conducted over 90-120 culture days across 8-12 ponds were associated with a measurable reduction in feed waste under comparable operational conditions. While the evaluation was not conducted under a fully controlled experimental design, the observed improvements were consistent across multiple ponds and production cycles; however, further controlled large-scale validation is required to quantify causal impact. The diseaserisk module integrates environmental and visual indicators through a composite stress index, providing early warning signals aligned with retrospective outbreak patterns. The decision-support system demonstrated strong alignment with Best Management Practice (BMP)-based recommendations under controlled evaluation scenarios. While results demonstrate technical feasibility and system integration capability, the findings are derived from a combination of controlled experiments, pilot deployments, and scenario-calibrated datasets. Therefore, large-scale multi-site validation is required to confirm generalizability, reproducibility, and long-term economic impact.

title: Interactive Sign Language Learning System with Multimodal Emotion and Interaction Recognition Analysis
abstract: Child-centric intelligent applications increasingly require adaptive mechanisms to understand emotional engagement and provide inclusive learning experiences. However, existing systems often rely on single-modal emotion recognition or non-interactive learning approaches, limiting reliability and accessibility. This paper presents a twocomponent intelligent framework that addresses these challenges through a multimodal emotion and interaction analysis module that fuses facial emotion recognition and hand movement intensity, and a gamified sign language learning and progress-tracking module designed for deaf and mute children. The first component employs an EfficientNet-B0-based facial emotion recognition model trained on FER2013 and fine-tuned using CK+, achieving 96.9% validation accuracy, combined with motion-based hand interaction analysis to generate stable session-level engagement insights. The second component introduces a camera-assisted, game-based sign language learning environment with a landmark-based DNN gesture validation model achieving 97% validation accuracy, along with a parent-oriented progress dashboard. Experimental results demonstrate improved robustness in engagement detection and effective learning support through gamification. The proposed system highlights the novelty of integrating multimodal behavioral analysis with accessible, child-friendly learning mechanisms suitable for real-time environments.

title: CardioRAG: Toward Trustworthy Medical Question Answering Through Hypothetical Document and Instruction-Aware Embedding
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves the factual grounding of large language models (LLMs) by combining retrieval with generation, but applying it in specialized medical domains introduces real friction. Domain-specific terminology, scarce supervised relevance labels, embedding-space mismatch across heterogeneous models, and hallucination risk all create problems that general-purpose RAG pipelines weren't designed to solve. CardioRAG is a domain-aware hybrid retrieval framework for cardiology question answering. It combines instruction-aware query encoding, hypothetical document generation, projection-based embedding alignment, and dense retrieval. The framework builds two complementary query representations. The first encodes the user query with INBEDDER to capture semantic intent, then projects it into the document embedding space of an INSTRUCTOR-indexed cardiology knowledge base — bridging the mismatch between heterogeneous embedding models. The second uses a fine-tuned SciFive generator to produce hypothetical cardiology answers under the Hypothetical Document Embeddings (HyDE) paradigm; these generated texts are embedded and aggregated into a retrieval-oriented representation. Both vectors are fused through weighted combination and used for FAISS-based dense retrieval. A pre-retrieval domain gate filters out-of-scope queries before retrieval and answer generation, which limits hallucination exposure on off-domain inputs. Experiments on a cardiology-focused subset of the MIRIAD dataset show that CardioRAG outperforms a standard dense-retrieval RAG baseline on faithfulness, completeness, and hallucination resistance. Gains in answer correctness are modest, but the results indicate that hybrid query representation and domain-aware filtering can meaningfully improve groundedness in specialized medical QA.

title: Smart Agri-Suite: A Globally Deployable Machine Learning Platform for Satellite-Driven Idle Land Mobilization and Smallholder Agricultural Decision Support
abstract: Across the tropics, 500 million smallholder farmers drive global food security. However, they face three connected, systemic failures. First, fertile land often remains undetected and idle. Second, market transactions lack legal or technical safeguards. Third, farmers make critical pricing, inventory, and labor decisions without reliable data. These challenges are not isolated inefficiencies. Instead, they act as planetary-scale barriers to agricultural prosperity. This study introduces the Smart Agri-Suite. It is a modular, mobile-first platform designed to address these exact barriers. The system integrates satellite intelligence, machine learning, and digital governance. Together, these form a comprehensive, field-ready solution. The platform processes Sentinel-2 Level-2A imagery using an XGBoost classifier. This enables precise, parcel-level land mapping and crop suitability analysis. Consequently, the system identifies previously undetected arable land with 80% accuracy. The platform features a compliance-driven marketplace. The marketplace strictly enforces spatial and legal verification for every transaction. Data-driven pricing and forecasting components incorporate demand signals, transportation costs and Net Present Value. These algorithms support financially sound decision-making. Furthermore, quantile regressionbased inventory management provides probabilistic demand forecasts. It also generates automated stock alerts. The system features a crop-agnostic and language-neutral architecture. This design demonstrates direct transferability to other smallholder systems. It can easily adapt to Sub-Saharan Africa, South and Southeast Asia, and Latin America. These findings highlight the power of targeted technological integration. It can transform persistent agricultural inefficiencies into measurable prosperity. Ultimately, this creates equitable growth for farming communities worldwide.

title: AI for Digital Literacy and Educational Programs in Public Libraries: A Case Study of Colombo District
abstract: This research aims to explore the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) in educational and digital literacy programs at public libraries in the Colombo District of Sri Lanka. Public libraries serve as essential digital gateways, assisting underserved communities in acquiring fundamental technological skills. Public libraries have expanded digital literacy programs to support community learning; however, many initiatives remain limited by one-size-fits-all instruction, low learner engagement, and limited scalability. This study addresses these gaps by developing and evaluating a personalized, technology-enabled digital literacy framework designed to enhance engagement, adaptability, and measurable learning outcomes across diverse community learners. AI technologies can help solve this problem through AI assessment systems and adaptive learning platforms, which deliver customized learning experiences that boost program effectiveness. The research examines the extent to which AI can be a primary reason for enhancing digital literacy at public libraries in the Colombo District of Sri Lanka. The study examines current digital literacy initiatives and assesses AI tool deployment benefits, while identifying deployment barriers and developing a strategic plan for sustainable AI implementation in digital literacy and library educational programs.

title: Sim-to-Real Transfer of Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments Using an Ackermann-Steered Mobile Robot
abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) enables robots to navigate through environments using natural language instructions, making human-robot interaction intuitive. Traditional VLN models often rely on navigation graphs, 360-degree views, and perfect localization which pose significant challenges when adapting these models to real-world settings. This work addresses these limitations by performing a simulation-to-real domain shift of a VLN approach that operates in continuous environments without requiring navigation graphs or panoramic views. The proposed system integrates vision-language models that align visual inputs and linguistic instructions within a shared embedding space, facilitating natural language-driven navigation. We employ a Cross-Modal Attention (CMA) based architecture trained on an existing dataset in a simulated environment and fine-tune it using real-world data collected from a custom-built Ackermann-steered robot equipped with a camera and a LiDAR sensor. By utilising linear photometric adjustments and fine-tuning on a limited number of episodes, our model successfully adapts to real-world environments, achieving effective navigation while running offline on dedicated hardware. Experimental results, evaluated using Success weighted by Path Length (SPL) and Normalized Dynamic Time Warping (nDTW) metrics, demonstrate the robustness and adaptability of our approach.

title: ColdFusionX: Multi-Modal Fusion via Aligned Latent Manifolds and Stochastic Masking for Zero-Shot CTR
abstract: Click-Through Rate (CTR) prediction is a foundational pillar of modern recommender systems. While collaborative ID-based embeddings excel at modeling warm-item interactions, they catastrophically fail in zero-shot, cold-start scenarios. Existing multi-modal approaches attempt to fuse textual and visual content to bridge this gap, but routinely suffer from two structural flaws: gradient starvation, where dominant ID embeddings inhibit the learning of content networks, and disjoint latent manifolds, where collaborative and semantic features reside in fundamentally incompatible vector spaces. In this paper, we propose ColdFusionX, a novel multi-modal CTR architecture engineered to explicitly solve these representational bottlenecks. First, we introduce Stop-Gradient Cosine Alignment, which forces content-based meta-embeddings to map into the established collaborative space without corrupting the mature ID representations. Second, we implement Stochastic Alpha Masking (SAM), a targeted modality dropout mechanism that randomly severs the ID-embedding dependency during training, forcing the downstream network to become highly robust to zero-shot inference. Finally, we propose a Residual Temporal FiLM module to model item temporal drift as an additive residual dynamic. Evaluated on the large-scale AntM2C dataset, ColdFusionX establishes a new state-of-the-art for cold-start CTR prediction. By systematically outperforming modern generative and meta-learning baselines, it achieves a Cold AUC of 0.8543 and an Overall AUC of 0.9255. Latent space visualizations further confirm that our alignment strategy successfully fuses previously disjoint modalities into a single, cohesive topological manifold.

title: Experts against automation? Comparing artificial intelligence and human identifications of multi-cell cereal husk phytoliths
abstract: This study compares the efficacy of a deep learning-based computer vision model against manual expert identification of multi-cell husk phytoliths from wheat (Triticum boeticum/dicoccoides), barley (Hordeum spontaneum), and oats (Avena sativa). Conducted via an online survey in 2024 with twelve respondents (92% completion rate, one respondent did not finish), the survey presented 18 phytolith images selected based on: 1) deep learning performance, 2) manual diagnostic clarity, and 3) random control. The deep learning model achieved 100% classification accuracy, while manual experts averaged 44%, with Avena proving the most challenging (26.39% accuracy) compared to Hordeum (54.17%) and Triticum (48.61%). Statistical analysis confirmed significant accuracy variations (p = 0.0016), highlighting Avena’s genus identification difficulty. Experience level influenced performance, with less than five years post-PhD researchers scoring highest (72%), though completion time did not correlate with accuracy. The algorithm’s superior performance, employing and appropriately weighting features like wave pattern and papillae, underscores the potential of artificial intelligence to transform paleoethnobotany by generating reliable, large-scale datasets. This research advocates for the integration of machine learning tools within manual studies in the short-term, to enhance accuracy and efficiency in phytolith analysis, paving the way for broader applications in environmental archaeology in the long-term.

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Animated Dance Creation: A Study of Audience Engagement and Creative Transformation
abstract: As a result of advancements in technology and software, the artificial intelligence (AI) has integrated into creative industries. AI has introduced novel approaches to various aspects of dance production, including costume design, choreographic composition, and animated dance creation. As a result, dance has extended beyond the boundaries of live stage performance and has increasingly become integrated into virtual and digital platforms. The creation of dance animation is a complex and multi-layered process that involves the anthropomorphizing of non-living or virtual characters into lifelike forms. It requires the integration of full-body movement, expressive gestures, costume design, in to rhythmic cultural and traditional way to achieve a coherent and believable performance. The primary problem of this research is to determine whether human-created or AI-generated animated dance is more effective and realistic from the audience’s perspective. In addition, the study seeks to investigate the extent to which artificial intelligence influences dance animation in terms of visual quality, emotional expression, and conceptualization. This study adopts a mixed-method research design to examine audience perceptions of AI-generated and human-created animated dance. A purposive sample of fifty participants with prior knowledge of dance and media will be selected. Quantitative data collected through questionnaires and qualitative data collected from audience observation and discussions. The findings of this research AI-generated dance content enhance visual appeal and accessibility, particularly in digital and social media contexts and it may lack the depth of emotional expression typically associated with human performance. The study concludes that AI does not replace traditional dance practices but rather expands the possibilities of dance as a hybrid digital art form.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Academic Integrity in UK Higher Education: A Rapid Literature Review of Emerging Challenges, Institutional Policy Responses, and Future Research Directions
abstract: Background: Academic integrity has been challenged in a radically different way in the UK higher education sector by the rapid growth of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools, underscored by the widespread use of large language models, including ChatGPT. Just three years after ChatGPT was released in the UK in the end of 2022, adoption by students has jumped from about 53% to 88%, presenting new systemic challenges, for which the current institutional frameworks were not planned and are not well-suited to deal with. The method used in carrying out this study is a rapid literature review (RLR) with a literature reporting approach based on PRISMA 2020. Four academic databases (Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC and the British Education Index) were searched as well as policy databases in the UK such as the British Education Index's (BEI) Higher Education publications archive, and Jisc's National Centre on AI (NCAI) database. The Quality Assurance Agency (QAA) was also used as a source for policy documents related to artificial intelligence for education. A total of 38 sources were identified for consideration after systematic screening and included two institutional policy analyses, six official sector documents, and 29 peer-reviewed journal articles. The synthesis highlighted four key thematic areas: (1) the unprecedented scale and definitional complexity of academic misconduct involving AI; (2) the technical and ethical limitations of academic integrity detection systems for AI; (3) the different nature and weak cohesion of policy responses to academic misconduct across the UK sector; and (4) the general consensus on redesigning and authentic assessment and enhancing AI literacy as the educationally soundest strategic directions. As reviewed above, the scholarly literature at hand questions the conceptual soundness of current academic integrity frameworks, which are developed within a pre-AI world that relies on individual authorship and empirical evidence assessable through the traceability of student work. Along with this, the paper reveals four areas of research that require immediate attention: Longitudinal effectiveness studies; UK specific empirical studies based on student and staff perspectives; Comparative institutional policy analysis; Theoretical research in the creation of new academic integrity frameworks that are sufficient to the AI era. The subject aims to embed a deeper understanding of generative AI within the framework of academic integrity and the concept of academic misconduct. The aims of the topic are to build a more robust understanding of generative AI in the context of academic integrity and academic misconduct.

title: When the Next Step Is Not One Step: Distribution-Aware Execution Modeling for Concurrent Go Programs
abstract: Training a model to predict the next step in a concurrent program is harder than it looks: two runs of the same program from the same trace prefix can produce different next events, both valid, because the scheduler is nondeterministic. A model trained against a single label is learning to guess one outcome of a random process. We turn this around and use the nondeterminism as a training signal. We run each program many times, aggregate the observed next events into an empirical distribution, and fine-tune a 7B model to match that distribution with a KL objective. On 798 held-out predictions drawn from real production Go bugs (CockroachDB, Kubernetes, gRPC, etcd), fine-tuning on fewer than a thousand traces reaches 36.2% accuracy, ahead of a strong proprietary model used zero-shot (34.8%) and the same model zero-shot (28.6%). Distribution training matches cross-entropy on accuracy (35.8% vs. 36.2%) while reducing Expected Calibration Error from 0.205 to 0.169. We also derive a formal goroutine-leak signature for a class of select-blocked goroutines where P (GoUnblock) = 0 holds by scheduler semantics, not by learning. We release the dataset, trained adapters, and all tooling.

title: Predicting compressive strength of fly ash blended sandcrete using machine learning models
abstract: Cement-based materials, particularly sandcrete, play a crucial role in the construction industry, where demand for sustainable and high-performance materials is increasing. Fly ash, a byproduct of coal combustion, has gained attention as a supplementary cementitious material (SCM) to improve the sustainability of these materials. However, predicting the compressive strength of fly ash-blended mortars, which is essential for ensuring the structural integrity and durability of construction materials, remains a challenge. This study aims to address this gap by leveraging advanced machine learning techniques to predict the compressive strength of fly ash blended sandcrete, using key input variables such as aggregate-to-binder ratio (Agg/B), fly ash-to-binder ratio (FA/B), water-to-binder ratio (W/B), and curing time. While previous research has focused on conventional cement mortars, few studies have integrated these key variables using machine learning models. The goal of this research is to develop a reliable and accurate predictive model for compressive strength, filling a gap in existing literature regarding the influence of multiple input variables on mortar performance. The study employs four machine learning models - Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) - to evaluate their performance in predicting compressive strength. The results show that XGB outperforms other models, achieving an R² of 0.84 for training data and 0.74 for testing data, along with the lowest prediction errors. These findings demonstrate the potential of machine learning models, particularly XGB, in optimizing mix designs and improving sustainability in construction, offering valuable insights for future material innovations.

title: Integrating News Topics and Sentiment Signals into Tourism Demand Forecasting: Evidence from Sri Lanka
abstract: Tourism is a critical economic sector in many developing countries, making accurate demand forecasting essential for effective planning, resource allocation, and destination management. However, tourism demand is influenced not only by historical trends and seasonality but also by social disruptions and changes in destination perception that are often reflected in news media. This study investigates whether news-derived semantic topics and sentiment signals can enhance tourism demand forecasting in Sri Lanka. Tourism-related news articles were transformed into structured explanatory variables using Sentence-BERT embeddings, K-Means-based semantic clustering-based topic discovery, and Valence Aware Dictionary and sEntiment Reasoner (VADER) sentiment analysis. Monthly distributions of discovered topics, sentiment categories, and seasonal indicators were then integrated into forecasting models. The predictive performance of a traditional time-series model, Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA), was compared with machine learning and deep learning approaches, including Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), Feed Forward Neural Networks (FNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Univariate models were trained using historical tourist arrivals only, whereas multivariate models incorporated both time-based and news-derived features. To assess the incremental value of additional information sources, forecasting performance was evaluated across historical-only, seasonality-enhanced, and news-augmented feature configurations. The results show that machine learning and deep learning models consistently outperform SARIMA, while the inclusion of seasonal and news-derived variables further improves forecasting accuracy. The best-performing standalone model was an FNN trained on a three-month lag structure with time-based and news-derived features, achieving an RMSE of 8,842.66, MAE of 6,824.43, MAPE of 3.63%, and R² of 0.9567. A hybrid FNN–XGB model produced a marginal improvement (RMSE = 8,658.84; R² = 0.9585), although the Diebold–Mariano test indicated no statistically significant difference. Overall, the findings demonstrate that news topics and sentiment signals provide complementary information beyond historical arrivals and seasonality, supporting more robust tourism demand forecasting and evidence-based tourism policy development.

title: Sinhala Similarity and Semantic Plagiarism Detection Using Modern Embedding Models
abstract: Abstract While plagiarism detection has developed to some degree in English and in some high-resource languages, it has not yet been fully developed in Sinhala language. Plagiarism detection is now well developed in English, and in some high resource languages, but there is little practical support for Sinhala language. This situation is worse in learning environments with presence of manual or tool-based checking of Sinhala submissions that doesn't identify semantic rewriting and translated copying. Current Sinhala research demonstrates success in direct matching and sentence similarity measures, yet these are applied on a limited scale between small corpora and/or rely on very basic similarity measurements or on a sentence level model that cannot be scaled to a full detection pipeline. In this paper, a research design that will tackle 2 related tasks in a single system for plagiarism detection system is presented for Sinhala plagiarism. The first one searches for similarity plagiarism within the Sinhala language, and is able to highlight copied and paraphrased content on a sentence level. It is written in English and then translated into Sinhala and is used without a reference. Semantic plagiarism is where English source material is translated and then used without a source. The proposed solution includes the use of a corpus to build the system, annotating the corpus, generating contextual embeddings, using a Siamese neural network, creating bilingual sentence representations, conducting a focused web crawl, and deploying the system as a service. A common framework enables the ingestion of documents, splitting them into sentences, comparing them, ranking them by ‘thresholder' and generating the report. The paper also dissects the data plan, workflow for implementation, progression of the prototypes and the evaluation plan for both components. The research integrates same language detection and cross language detection technologies within a single framework to improve the natural language processing for Sinhala language and at the same time simultaneously support academia in the low resource scenario by using it as a tool on academic integrity.

title: Real-Time Sri Lankan Static Sign Language System using EfficientNet-B0
abstract: Sign Language serves as an important medium of communication for the deaf and hard of hearing community. However, there is a lack of understanding among the public regarding the various signs used. Although around 300,000 Sinhala-speaking individuals are either deaf or hard of hearing, dedicated applications for Sri Lankan Sign Language detection are quite limited. In contrast, various sign language detection systems for other popular sign languages, such as American Sign Language (ASL) and British Sign Language (BSL), exist in abundance. This study aims to design and develop a lightweight mobile application, backed by the Efficient-B0 model, for Sri Lankan Static Sign Language detection. This application can detect five popular words using nine static signs and can be scaled up in the future. The developed application was found to be lightweight, efficient, and usable among the target users, achieving an accuracy of over 90% for real-time sign detection.

title: Identification and characterization of inference bottlenecks and class imbalance in Transformer-based Smart Contract Auditors
abstract: This research investigates critical challenges in Transformer-based smart contract auditing systems, with a specific focus on inference instability and class imbalance in CodeBERT-based binary vulnerability classification. Layer-2 blockchain networks introduce highly complex architectures that increase the risk of smart contract exploits, where traditional static analysis tools such as Slither often produce large volumes of noisy, rule-based alerts. Recent advancements in pre-trained Transformer models, particularly CodeBERT, have demonstrated strong capabilities in semantic code understanding and vulnerability detection. However, during deployment of a fine-tuned CodeBERT-base model, we observe significant performance and stability issues. Initial inference experiments show a 100% false-positive rate, primarily attributed to severe class imbalance in the slither-audited-smart-contracts dataset and model sensitivity to specific smart contract patterns such as raw Ether transfer functions. In addition, system-level execution profiling reveals a silent segmentation fault during model initialization. Further investigation using Windows OS logs identifies dependency conflicts between PyTorch and PyArrow (via Hugging Face Datasets), particularly related to C++ DLL load-order issues. Experimental analysis demonstrates that modifying dependency import order, prioritizing PyArrow initialization, and enforcing strict model.eval() state management significantly improves inference stability. These findings highlight important architectural and deployment considerations for Transformer-based blockchain security systems and provide practical insights for improving the robustness of automated smart contract auditing pipelines in Layer-2 Web3 ecosystems.

title: Identifying Employee Emotions Based on Facial Expression Analysis in IT Sector using Ensemble Learning Techniques: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Facial expression analysis is an important tool for determining employee emotions, especially in the IT sector, where knowing emotional states can have significant effects on productivity and well-being. Traditional techniques for emotion detection are frequently limited by their dependence on simple recognition models that may not fully represent the complexities of human emotions. However, recent research has investigated the possibilities of ensemble learning techniques to improve the accuracy and dependability of these systems. This systematic literature review examines the various approaches used in emotion recognition from 2011 to 2023, with a focus on how ensemble learning might increase the efficiency of facial expression analysis. An initial selection of 33 studies was taken from six internet databases, with 7 eventually being included in the final review. The findings show that integrating several analytical methodologies into models produces promising results, leading the path for more robust emotion identification systems in the workplace.

title: Smart Detection of Elephant Intrusions Using LoRaWAN Enabled IoT Sensors
abstract: Abstract Despite recent progress in mitigating human elephant conflict across Sri Lanka, it continues to pose severe threats to human lives, security and elephant conservation, not only in Sri Lanka but also in other parts of Asia and Africa. Limited coverage, unreliable sensors, on-site maintenance, and lack of a communications infrastructure in remote areas are all limitations of current available mitigation technology (e.g., fences, manual guarding, single sensor alarms). In this paper, a smart intrusion detection system is designed for elephants which integrates both seismic and passive infrared sensors, locally processes the data, uses a machine learning algorithm to classify the event, communicates via LoRaWAN, sends the alerts to the cloud and includes a non-lethal deterrent counter measure. The proposed system has four coordinated layers: multi sensor field nodes, a hybrid LoRaWAN communication backbone to connect to the WiFi and LTE networks as a failover option, a machine learning engine to discriminate between elephants and non-elephants, and last but not least, a dashboard and notification layer for farmers and wildlife officers. The architecture has been developed with these features – low power, self-healing communication, offline buffering, delivery of warning in real time. The paper also implies the design on the backdrop of the latest literature from the open sources for human elephant conflict, seismic elephant detection and LoRaWAN for wildlife monitoring. In a recent geophone interface study done in Sri Lanka, up to 155.6 m distance was achieved for seismic detection and an accuracy of 99.5% was achieved which provides strong support to the sensing basis of this project. The system being proposed further builds on that as a full farm platform for deployment in the rural environment.

title: A Modified Firefly Algorithm Adaptive to the Single-Stage Fixed Charge Transportation Problem
abstract: The transportation problem is primarily concerned with the ways in which resources can be transported from supply centers to final customers with minimum total transportation costs. In addition to variable transportation costs, the single-stage fixed charge transportation problem (FCTP) has become a more challenging and complex optimization problem due to the inclusion of fixed route activation costs. Therefore, since it is difficult to obtain optimal solutions for these problems in a reasonable time, heuristic algorithms are used to obtain more qualitative and accurate solutions. This study proposes a modified firefly optimization algorithm to efficiently obtain high-quality near-optimal solutions. The enhanced algorithm improves convergence behavior and robustness and is implemented in Python for computational efficiency. The performance is observed and evaluated on numerical experiments across different problem scales. Here, the solutions of the proposed algorithm are compared with other existing heuristic algorithms through numerical experiment analysis. The numerical experiments conducted across different problem scales show that the proposed method performs competitively with existing heuristics and provides superior results for large-scale cases.

title: smear-microscopy-autofocus-benchmark
abstract: This record provides version 1.0.0 of the software and reproducibility outputs supporting the study “Weakly Supervised Cross-Dataset Benchmarking and Interpretable Symbolic Fusion of Focus Measures for Smear Microscopy Autofocus.”The archive implements a weakly supervised cross-dataset autofocus benchmark across five smear-microscopy datasets: WBC, TBI, PBS, BMA, and TBF. It includes 32 implemented handcrafted focus measures, ten autofocus evaluation metrics, leave-one-dataset-out genetic programming with ten seeds per held-out dataset, a ten-seed final all-dataset refit, and evaluation of fourteen retained composite focus measures.Included materials comprise the complete Python source code, experiment configuration, source/surrogate/leave-one-out label arrays, raw and normalized focus curves, timing measurements, single-measure results, 50 LODO GP seed runs, 10 final-refit runs, composite evaluations, statistical analyses, publication tables and figures, and reviewer-response sensitivity computations.Raw microscopy images and the approximately 46 GB reconstructed stack cache are not redistributed because their access, licensing, privacy, and storage requirements must be handled separately. Authorized users can rebuild the stack cache using the supplied pipeline and dataset configuration instructions.Surrogate labels are consensus labels and must not be interpreted as optical ground truth. The internal “Curvelet Transform Sharpness Index” name maps to Wavelet Detail Energy (db1). title: Inference-Time ROI Policy for Domain-Robust Deep Autofocus in Smear Microscopy: Code, Models, Results, and Supplementary Evidence
abstract: This record contains source code, frozen model checkpoints, calibration metadata, support indices, fixed-model predictions, policy-level metrics, statistical analyses, tables, figures, the main manuscript draft, and comprehensive supplementary evidence for a study of inference-time region-of-interest selection in smear-microscopy autofocus. Seventeen ROI policies were evaluated across white blood cell (WBC), peripheral blood smear (PBS), and bone marrow aspirate (BMA) domains while model weights, preprocessing, sign-confidence thresholds, test support, and FOV-level aggregation were held constant. Adaptive hybrid ROI selection reduced domain-gap MAE by 29.39% relative to center-top1 while weighted pooled MAE remained nearly unchanged under WBC-dominated support. Raw microscopy images and the approximately 198 GB Phase 3 tensor cache are not included; manifests, indices, frozen predictions, checkpoints, and calibration metadata are provided.

title: Deep Learning-Based Plant Identification in Sri Lanka
abstract: Sri Lanka has a lot of types of plants. Many of these plants are really important for farming and keeping the environment healthy. Usually people use ways to figure out what kind of plant something is. These old ways can take a time and are often wrong especially when the leaves of the plants look very similar. This article is about using computers to help identify plants that're from Sri Lanka. It talks about a way to use computers to recognize plants automatically which is based on deep learning and focuses on plants, from Sri Lanka. MobileNetV2 and other models like YOLOv8 and EfficientNetB0 were used in this study. A custom CNN was also used. These are all complicated image classification models. The team gathered a lot of pictures of leaves. They then did some things to these pictures to make them better for training the models. This included making the pictures bigger or smaller and changing the colors a bit. MobileNetV2 was really good at recognizing the leaves. It got 99 percent of the training pictures right. 93 Percent of the test pictures right. This was better than the models they tried. The results show that MobileNetV2 is really good at telling the difference between leaves that look pretty similar. MobileNetV2 reliably distinguishes similar leaf types, even those with nearly identical appearances. Our work not only highlights deep learning's strengths in accurate, large-scale plant identification but also paves the way for real-world uses in farming studies, classroom teaching, and biodiversity conservation. We propose expanding the dataset and enhancing preprocessing steps to overcome challenges like data scarcity and classification errors. Looking ahead, we plan to incorporate drone-based image capture and build a mobile app for on-the-spot species recognition

title: VAGNet: Vision-Based Accident Anticipation With Global Features
abstract: Traffic accidents are a leading cause of fatalities and injuries across the globe. Therefore, the ability to anticipate hazardous situations in advance is essential. Automated accident anticipation enables timely intervention through driver alerts and collision avoidance maneuvers, forming a key component of advanced driver assistance systems. In autonomous driving, such predictive capabilities support proactive safety behaviors, such as initiating defensive driving and human takeover when required. Using dash-cam video as input offers a cost-effective solution, but it is challenging due to the complexity of real-world driving scenes. Accident anticipation systems need to operate in real-time. However, current methods involve extracting features from each detected object, which is computationally intensive. We propose VAGNet, a deep neural network that learns to predict accidents from dash-cam video using global features of traffic scenes without requiring explicit object-level features. The network consists of transformer and graph modules, and we use the vision foundation model VideoMAE-V2 for global feature extraction. Experiments on four benchmark datasets (DAD, DoTA, DADA, and Nexar) show that our method anticipates accidents with higher average precision while being computationally more efficient compared to existing methods. It also achieves higher mean time-to-accident scores in most cases, while being competitive in others.

title: AI-Based Irrigation Demand Forecasting for Climate-Adaptive Crop Water Management in Irrigated Agriculture
abstract: Accurate and timely forecasting of crop irrigation demand is a critical agrometeorological challenge, particularly in regions experiencing intensifying climate variability, water scarcity, and growing food insecurity. Weather conditions, including temperature extremes, precipitation deficits, and elevated evaporative demand, directly drive crop water requirements and can significantly reduce yields when irrigation scheduling is poorly timed. Existing studies on crop water demand have employed machine learning (ML) for actual evapotranspiration (ETa) prediction, incorporating feature selection to reduce data dimensionality and mitigate multicollinearity, thereby improving model performance. However, existing ETa models have limited spatial continuity and restricted applicability under changing climate conditions.This study addresses these limitations by developing a machine learning-based Irrigation Demand Forecasting Model (AI-IDFM) that integrates multi-sensor satellite data, spectral indices, and various climatic variables to determine crop water requirements under changing climate conditions. The actual crop evapotranspiration (ETact), a key agrometeorological variable linking atmospheric demand and crop water use is estimated through a surface energy balance framework using Landsat satellite data with 30 m spatial resolution, complemented by high-resolution (3 m) land cover information, capturing fine-scale microclimatic variability relevant for field-level irrigation decision-making. The key variables, including NDVI, SAVI, LST, and net radiation (Rn), along with climatic variables such as precipitation, temperature, and humidity, are incorporated into the model. Deep learning and machine learning approaches, including Convolutional Neural Network–Multilayer Perceptron (CNN-MLP), Random Forest (RF), and Gradient Boosting (GB), were used for training and validation. The CNN-MLP model performed best, achieving an R² of 0.90, followed by RF and GB with R² values of 0.87 and 0.80, respectively. From this study, the short-range irrigation advisories are generated by coupling AI-IDFM with daily meteorological outputs from the ICON ensemble model, providing 7-day forecasts of key atmospheric drivers, including temperature, total precipitation, and relative humidity. Forecasted inputs for April 2025 indicated temperatures ranging from 36.2-42.8°C, average humidity between 18.5-43.7%, reflecting intense thermal stress during the pre-Kharif transition period that directly amplify crop water demand.Model performance showed that CNN predictions closely matched observed ETact for rice (6.798 vs. 6.99 mm/day) and wheat (2.041 vs. 1.86 mm/day), validated against eddy covariance flux tower observations across Kharif and Rabi cropping seasons in Okara district, Punjab. The model consistently outperformed ensemble methods across diverse crop types. During the Rabi wheat growth phase, CNN forecasted ET at 29.87 mm/day compared to a flux tower measurement of 33 mm/day, with the lowest deviation recorded in December (6.99 vs. 6.89 mm/day). The results demonstrate that AI-IDFM provides a robust, weather-informed irrigation advisory framework capable of supporting farm-level decision-making across diverse cropping systems. The approach links weather data to actionable irrigation decisions, enabling scalable management from field to regional levels, improving water use efficiency and supporting climate-resilient agriculture in data-scarce systems.
