title: Ethical and Transparent AI in Cyber Defense: An Explainable AI Plugin for Network Intrusion Detection Using SHAP, LIME, and ELI5
abstract: Abstract Security Operations Centers (SOCs) increasingly rely on machine learning-based intrusion detection systems to identify malicious network activity in high-volume environments. However, strong classifiers such as Random Forest and XGBoost often operate as black boxes, limiting analyst trust and increasing investigation effort during alert triage. This paper presents an explainable intrusion detection framework that integrates binary IDS predictions with human-interpretable explanations generated using SHAP, LIME, and ELI5. The framework is evaluated on the CICIDS2017 dataset using repeated experimental runs and a structured quantitative evaluation of explanation stability, fidelity, runtime efficiency, and cross-method agreement. In addition to offline evaluation, the study implements a Streamlit-based dashboard prototype that visualizes model predictions, confidence levels, feature attributions, model agreement, and analyst-oriented summaries. The results show that both Random Forest and XGBoost achieve high detection performance, while explanation methods provide complementary forms of local and global interpretability. The study demonstrates that explainability can be treated as a measurable and operationally deployable component of IDS design rather than as a visualization add-on.

title: A data driven framework for forecasting post-retrofit HVAC and lighting energy consumption
abstract: Buildings account for a substantial share of global energy consumption, yet significant uncertainty persists in predicting energy savings following retrofit interventions, contributing to the widely reported energy performance gap. Existing prediction approaches primarily rely on physics-based simulation or short-term operational forecasting, with limited research addressing cross-building prediction of post-retrofit energy performance. This study develops a data-driven cross-building machine learning framework to forecast post-retrofit heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) and lighting energy consumption using pre-retrofit building characteristics and operational variables. A Random Forest regression model was trained on a large-scale dataset comprising energy and operational records from 9450 commercial buildings, incorporating building characteristics, occupancy patterns, system specifications, and climatic variables. The model was validated using two independent commercial office buildings excluded from training to evaluate predictive generalization under realistic deployment conditions. Model performance was assessed using mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), root mean squared error (RMSE), coefficient of variation of RMSE (CVRMSE), and coefficient of determination. The proposed framework achieved strong predictive accuracy, with MAPE values below 7% and CVRMSE below 10% across validation cases, outperforming commonly reported benchmarks in building energy forecasting. Results demonstrate that cross-building learning captures transferable relationships between pre-retrofit conditions and post-retrofit energy performance without requiring building-specific calibration. Feature importance analysis identified baseline HVAC consumption, occupancy-related variables, building size, and climatic factors as dominant drivers of post-retrofit energy demand. This study contributes a scalable and reliable predictive approach for retrofit performance forecasting, reducing uncertainty in energy savings estimation and supporting evidence-based investment and measurement and verification processes. The findings highlight the potential of data-driven cross-building models to enhance the credibility and effectiveness of large-scale building energy retrofit programs.

title: Application of Machine Learning for Waste Classification Using Electrical Conductivity, Thermal Conductivity, and Thermal Imaging
abstract: Efficient waste segregation is a critical step towards achieving sustainable environmental management and circular economy goals. This research presents the development and implementation of an intelligent web-based application designed to identify and classify various types of waste materials, such as plastic, glass, aluminium, paper, and steel, using a multi-modal approach that combines electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and thermal imaging data. The system employs machine learning and a YOLOv8-based object detection model to analyze thermal images of waste items and accurately detect their type (i.e. glass etc.). Simultaneously, a rule-based algorithm interprets the measured electrical and thermal conductivity values to enhance prediction reliability. The platform was developed using Python, with a Flask back end and a user-friendly HTML/CSS/JavaScript front end. The application enables users to upload thermal images and input conductivity data, returning real-time classification results. Extensive testing with a dataset of common household and industrial waste materials showed a high degree of classification accuracy. title: Application of Machine Learning for Waste Classification Using Electrical Conductivity, Thermal Conductivity, and Thermal Imaging
abstract: Efficient waste segregation is a critical step towards achieving sustainable environmental management and circular economy goals. This research presents the development and implementation of an intelligent web-based application designed to identify and classify various types of waste materials, such as plastic, glass, aluminium, paper, and steel, using a multi-modal approach that combines electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and thermal imaging data. The system employs machine learning and a YOLOv8-based object detection model to analyze thermal images of waste items and accurately detect their type (i.e. glass etc.). Simultaneously, a rule-based algorithm interprets the measured electrical and thermal conductivity values to enhance prediction reliability. The platform was developed using Python, with a Flask back end and a user-friendly HTML/CSS/JavaScript front end. The application enables users to upload thermal images and input conductivity data, returning real-time classification results. Extensive testing with a dataset of common household and industrial waste materials showed a high degree of classification accuracy. The integration of image-based detection and physical property analysis significantly improves the reliability of waste identification. This tool is particularly valuable for use in smart recycling stations, waste sorting facilities, and educational settings, where real-time material classification is essential.

title: Ethical, Empathic, Psychological and Social Implications of Artificial Intelligence in Counselling Practice: A Theory-Informed Systematic Review and Critical Thematic Synthesis
abstract: Abstract The rising integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in counselling and psychotherapy is outpacing the development of ethical, empathic and regulatory frameworks governing its use. Despite strong potential of AI-assisted tools in enhancing accessibility and efficiency, concerns involving safeguarding, accountability, psychological influence over vulnerable users’ behavior and the erosion of empathic care repeatedly emerge. Such challenges are particularly salient within the Sri Lankan context, where mental health infrastructure, regulatory oversight and AI literacy remain constrained. This study examines qualitative literature addressing the ethical, social, empathic and psychological implications of AI implementation in counselling, with specific emphasis on ethical standardization requirements and the need for continued research. A qualitative systematic literature review was conducted using the READ method and reflexive thematic analysis informed by Naeem et al.’s (2023) framework, to identify recurring ethical risks, social tensions and practice-level implications. The analysis revealed 5 themes comprising (1) data privacy and psychological vulnerability; (2) professional competence, accountability and ethical responsibility; (3) integrity of empathy and the therapeutic alliance; (4) social inequality, access and marginalization; and (5) systemic gaps in ethical standardization and governance, alongside cross-cutting tensions comprising accessibility vs psychological safety, and efficiency vs empathic integrity. The interpretive findings indicate heightened risks in vulnerable populations such as minors, rural residents, sensory impaired users and individuals with limited digital literacy or complex mental health needs. They also highlight increased susceptibility to psychological and cognitive influence, cultural misalignment, limitations in crisis management, professional deskilling and over-reliance on AI-mediated guidance. They further suggest that while AI systems may simulate therapeutic interaction and improve accessibility and efficiency, limitations in contextual reasoning, empathic reciprocity, interpretative capacity of non- normative expression and emotionally nuanced communication, plus cognitive variation and mechanistic processes of AI may compromise therapeutic depth, relational authenticity and psychological safety. Additionally, they emphasize the need for improved quality and competence of AI-based software, and conceptualize AI as a conditional, ethically governed adjunct to traditional therapy as opposed to a therapeutic substitute. The study outlines implications for professional standards, governance frameworks, culturally sensitive implementation, human-in-the-loop safeguards and future directions for ongoing research in the field. title: Early Detection of Dyscalculia in Children: A Sri Lankan Perspective Using Ensemble Machine Learning
abstract: A specific learning disability called Dyscalculia that affect numerical and mathematical cognition and approximately 3–6% of school-age children in worldwide estimated to be impact by this specific learning disability. In Sri Lanka, culturally validated, automated screening tools for dyscalculia are limited and it results in widespread underdiagnoses especially in rural educational settings. So this paper aims to present a mobile application-integrated machine learning system that helps to early detection of dyscalculia severity and its common comorbidities named attention deficits and memory impairments among primary school children (ages 7–8) in Sri Lanka. Nearly 2,000 child activity records were collected from Mihintale Primary School using mobile application and consulting educational psychologist is the one who assigned ground truth labels to the dataset. Firstly child have to play numerical recognition, addition, subtraction, division, mathematical symbol identification, word questioners and using that activity records detect dyscalculia severity classification (No Risk, Mild Risk, and High Risk) using a stacked ensemble combining MLP(Adam), Random Forest and XGBoost with Random Forest as meta-learner and it achieved 98.80% testing accuracy. If child identified as Mild or High Risk then attention and memory detection activities triggered and using those activity records trained an attention impairment detection machine learning model using Support Vector Machine and it achieved 97% testing accuracy while memory impairment detection machine learning model using Random Forest achieved 98% testing accuracy. Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) was used only to the training dataset for class imbalance handling, GridSearchCV for hyperparametes tuning and 5-fold stratified cross-validation technique was applied across all machine learning models. The proposed mobile application provide an accessible, low-cost and culturally contextualized early screening tool for Sri Lankan primary education setting.

title: Risk Detection in Financial Markets: A Sentiment-Aware Hybrid Deep Learning Approach for Crisis Forecasting
abstract: Financial forecasting has always been a significant challenge; however, the predictive accuracy of traditional models such as ARIMA and standard machine learning classifiers greatly reduces when faced with changes in the economy. Market volatility driven by exogenous shocks, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, frequently renders these conventional methods ineffective. This research introduces a novel multi-modal hybrid machine learning approach that integrates technical market data with unstructured sentiment signals to enhance forecasting precision and risk identification during crisis periods. The proposed architecture utilises a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) to capture temporal dependencies in financial time series, complemented by a dense Artificial Neural Network (ANN) that processes static context vectors derived from macroeconomic indicators (eg. VIX, inflation) and global news sentiment (via GDELT). A cross-attention mechanism is employed to weigh the influence of diverse data inputs dynamically. The model was empirically evaluated using S&P 500 data specifically covering the COVID-19 crisis period (2019–2021). The proposed Hybrid GRU-ANN with Cross-Attention was evaluated on its ability to detect the market crash associated with COVID-19 (February to April 2020, 62 trading days, 53% downward-class balance). On this crisis window, the Random Forest baseline (AUC 0.455) and a standalone GRU ablation (AUC 0.393) both fall to or below random performance, exhibiting opposite manifestations of the same pathology. Specifically, the Random Forest model takes advantage of long-term uptrends, while the GRU model collapses to predicting downtrends. The proposed Hybrid GRU-ANN with Cross-Attention is the only architecture with discriminative power above chance, achieving an AUC-ROC of 0.598 and the highest precision (0.667) when predicting downturns. These findings establish that sentiment aware cross-attention provides genuine crisis detection capability rather than the false confidence of base rate driven baselines.

title: AI and critical thinking: cognitive partner or cognitive substitute
abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping higher education faster than pedagogy can respond. AI tools can personalise feedback, scaffold metacognition, and deepen collaborative inquiry, yet without structured guidance, they equally risk creating cognitive dependency, distorted self-assessment, and superficial thinking. Educators urgently need a coherent framework to navigate this tension. This paper draws on a systematic review of 63 peer-reviewed studies (January 2023 April 2025, PRISMA 2020) to pursue three objectives: synthesising evidence on AI's dual impact on critical thinking; examining ethical challenges including academic integrity, algorithmic bias, and privacy; and proposing the AI-Enhanced Critical Thinking (AI-CTE) Framework. Unlike existing AI literacy models, the AI-CTE framework explicitly positions critical thinking preservation rather than AI proficiency as the central pedagogical objective. The evidence reveals that AI functions as either a cognitive partner or a cognitive substitute the difference lies entirely in pedagogical intentionality. The AI-CTE Framework addresses this through four progressive dimensions: AI Literacy and Foundational Understanding, Guided Application and Critical Engagement, Evaluation Synthesis and Creative Construction, and Ethical Reflection and Responsible Practice, united by a feedback loop that keeps the learner as active cognitive agent. Empirical validation across diverse educational contexts remains a priority

title: An Interpretable Machine Learning Framework for Diabetes Risk Prediction
abstract: The current trend of diabetes escalating to global levels necessitates that the risk be identified early through non-invasive lifestyle and food information. However, the dimensionality of lifestyle surveys is very high and most machine learning models lack transparency which severely constrains their clinical usability. Here, (N=189), we suggest an interpretable predictive framework that is focused on clinical transparency and less overfitting. Boruta algorithm was applied to filter 58 lifestyle features with high rigor and a highly significant predictive subset were obtained with BMI, age, and sleep quality. Individual algorithms (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost) and homemade ensemble structures were evaluated involving 5-fold stratified cross-validation. Using an ablation study of ensemble estimators, it was revealed that the most powerful pairwise ensemble, which was purely tree-based, was a combination of Random Forest and XGBoost, and this combination had an accuracy of 89.47% and the F1-score of 0.83. These finding evidences that when variance-reducing (bagging) and bias-reducing (boosting) models are separated and integrated, the ensemble resists the structural collision between mixed linear probabilities, and effectively captures non-linear lifestyle trends. Moreover, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) served to ensure the transparency of diagnosis by quantifying the directional influence of any one lifestyle decision on the final risk prediction outcome. Finally, the framework demonstrates that rigorous feature selection plus explainable and high performing ensemble modeling is a more reliable and suitable tool in the individualized diabetes risk assessment.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Smart Traffic Signal Optimization: A Comparative Analysis of Efficiency and Robustness
abstract: Traffic congestion in urban areas is one of the major issues in contemporary transport systems, especially when the traffic demand is considerably volatile and unpredictable. When the traffic flows are normal, fixed-time traffic signal controllers can work effectively, but they tend to work poorly when there is a sudden shift in the traffic. Although Deep Reinforcement Learning has become a promising solution in adaptive traffic signal control, typical controllers which are based on standard Deep Q-Network models are not resistant to unstable or noisy environments because they require instantaneous observation of their states. This paper presents a hybrid traffic signal control framework that combines Long Short-Term Memory based traffic prediction with a Deep Q-Network controller. The proposed framework follows a dual-stream architecture. A LSTM model is trained using actual traffic data to discover short-time temporal dynamics, whereas a DQN controller is trained in a SUMO simulation environment to discover adaptive signal phase control. The predicted near-future traffic flow was then architecturally integrated into the state representation in such a way that it can be applied to the agent to be able to make decisions based on present and near-future traffic. Through the experiments, the LSTM was found to have attained a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0855, improving prediction performance by 15% over a persistence baseline. In controller evaluation, a Genetic Algorithm optimized static controller performed best under predictable heavy traffic, but the proposed hybrid controller was more robust under extreme traffic conditions. In the most volatile scenario, the hybrid controller maintained a queue measure of about 38,801, compared with 42,418 for the static controller and about 85,000 for the pure DQN model. These results suggest that incorporating temporal prediction into reinforcement learning can improve robustness in unstable traffic environments.

title: OptiROP: A Multi-Architecture Deep Learning Framework with Hybrid Dual-Backbone Fusion and Imbalance-Aware Training for Binary Retinopathy of Prematurity Classification
abstract: Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP) is a leading cause of childhood blindness, yet current deep learning (DL) screening systems suffer from three critical limitations: exclusive reliance on single-timepoint retinal images, absence of calibrated uncertainty quantification, and poor performance under severe class imbalance where Plus disease cases constitute fewer than 10% of training data. This paper presents OptiROP, a systematic five-model comparative framework evaluating ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B3, MobileNetV3-Large, and a novel HybridFusionModel on 6,386 retinal fundus images with strict patient-aware data splits. A comprehensive imbalance-aware training regime combines 4× Plus-class oversampling, Focal Loss (γ=2.5), Generalised Mean Pooling concatenated with Global Max Pooling, two-phase frozen-then-unfrozen backbone training, and MixUp augmentation (α=0.35). The HybridFusionModel— fusing ResNet50 structural features with EfficientNet-B3 texture representations via a learned gating mechanism—achieves the best overall performance: 76.44% validation accuracy, 78.28% test accuracy, Plus recall of 0.79, and macro F1 of 0.77. ResNet50 achieves the highest Plus recall at 0.89. Grad-CAM and Grad-CAM++ visualisations confirm clinically coherent activation in vascular and optic disc regions. All results are reported on patient-level held-out test sets to prevent data leakage.

title: Interpretable Multi-Label Classification of YouTube Videos Using Explainable AI on Title and Description Text
abstract: The rapid growth of user-generated content on different platforms such as YouTube has created a critical demand for efficient and automated video classification systems. This study addresses the limitations of traditional single-label models by proposing an interpretable multi-label classification model using textual metadata, including video titles and descriptions. An existing dataset was extended and relabeled manually to support multi-label classification and improve the quality of the dataset. The traditional machine learning models, such as Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost, were evaluated using a comparative analysis to assess their effectiveness in multi-label classification. In addition, transformer-based model, Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), was also evaluated, and the results show clear performance improvement over the assessed traditional models. Conventional machine learning models performed moderately, the XGBoost achieved the highest macro F1-score of 0.77. title: EndoPro: A Secure, Edge-Optimized Heuristic-Augmented Deep Learning System for Real-Time Gastrointestinal Anomaly Detection
abstract: Although deep learning has demonstrated remarkable theoretical accuracy in gastrointestinal diagnostics, cloud-infrastructure dependencies, expensive GPU requirements, and neural networks’ vulnerability to Out-of-Distribution (OOD) environmental noise significantly impede real-world clinical deployment. EndoPro, a completely localised, offline-first edge AI system for real-time endoscopic analysis on commodity CPU hardware, is presented in this study. The intelligence layer was trained using an EfficientNetV2-Large architecture on a mathematically trimmed, 16-class subset of the Hyper-Kvasir dataset (10,478 pictures) employing sophisticated spatial augmentations in order to create a maximum-accuracy diagnostic baseline. This method produced an unseen test accuracy of 89.58% and a peak validation accuracy of 94.91%. The real-time deployment step uses edge-optimized cross-compilation using the Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) runtime in conjunction with a novel RGB-dominance heuristic pre-filter to address the significant computational limitations present in large deep learning designs. By successfully separating tensor processing from the primary application thread, this architectural technique achieves continuous inference speeds of more than 30 frames per second (FPS). EndoPro bridges the crucial gap between resource-constrained clinical viability and high-performance diagnostic AI by integrating hardware-level USB encrypted authentication for absolute data sovereignty.

title: An AI-Driven Predictive Analytics Framework for Forecasting Undergraduate Student Dropout Rates
abstract: Student dropout in higher education is a serious problem because of the academic, social and economic implications to the students and institutions. Conventional ways of identifying are based on delayed indicators of academic performance, and this restricts early intervention. This paper suggests an anticipatory analytics system that is trained on an artificial intelligence platform to predict the likelihood of student dropout among the undergraduate students using the UCI Student Dropout Dataset (4424 student records, 37 attributes). The framework combines the techniques of baseline, advanced, ensemble, and explainable machine learning. The dataset was preprocessed and converted to a binary classification problem. Random Forest and XGBoost were the models applied as the advanced models in comparison to Logistic Regression and Decision Tree as the baseline models. A soft voting ensemble was created to integrate the strengths of models. The findings indicate that the ensemble model achieved the highest accuracy (85.31%), and best overall performance as indicated by an F1-score of 78%. SHAP-based explainability analysis demonstrated that academic performance during the first semester, as well as financial stability, are the most significant predictors of dropout. The study demonstrates that explainable machine learning can be used to assist in early warning and student retention strategies.

title: Real-Time Multimodal Disaster Detection Using Social Media
abstract: Social media platforms have become valuable sources of real-time information during disaster events; however, accurately identifying relevant content remains challenging due to noise, misinformation, and the limitations of unimodal analysis. This study proposes a real-time multimodal disaster detection framework that integrates textual and visual information within a two-stage pipeline, where posts are first classified as informative and then categorized by disaster type. The system incorporates a real-time data ingestion module that continuously collects social media posts via API-based streaming and processes them through a hybrid TF-IDF-based text model enhanced with domain-specific keywords and location-aware features, alongside a deep learning-based image classification model. To improve reliability, both unimodal and multimodal approaches are evaluated using late fusion and a stacking-based Random Forest meta-classifier. Experimental results show that the stacking fusion model outperforms unimodal methods, achieving an accuracy of 81.86% and an F1-score of 84.20%, demonstrating a clear improvement over text-only and image-only models. In addition, the system performs location extraction using named entity recognition and geocoding, enabling real-time visualization through an interactive geospatial dashboard. The results confirm that multimodal fusion significantly enhances disaster detection performance and provides a practical solution for real-time situational awareness and decision support.

title: OptiROP: A Multi-Architecture Deep Learning Framework with Hybrid Dual-Backbone Fusion and Imbalance-Aware Training for Binary Retinopathy of Prematurity Classification
abstract: Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP) is a leading cause of childhood blindness, yet current deep learning (DL) screening systems suffer from three critical limitations: exclusive reliance on single-timepoint retinal images, absence of calibrated uncertainty quantification, and poor performance under severe class imbalance where Plus disease cases constitute fewer than 10% of training data. This paper presents OptiROP, a systematic five-model comparative framework evaluating ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B3, MobileNetV3-Large, and a novel HybridFusionModel on 6,386 retinal fundus images with strict patient-aware data splits. A comprehensive imbalance-aware training regime combines 4× Plus-class oversampling, Focal Loss (γ=2.5), Generalised Mean Pooling concatenated with Global Max Pooling, two-phase frozen-then-unfrozen backbone training, and MixUp augmentation (α=0.35). The HybridFusionModel— fusing ResNet50 structural features with EfficientNet-B3 texture representations via a learned gating mechanism—achieves the best overall performance: 76.44% validation accuracy, 78.28% test accuracy, Plus recall of 0.79, and macro F1 of 0.77. ResNet50 achieves the highest Plus recall at 0.89. Grad-CAM and Grad-CAM++ visualisations confirm clinically coherent activation in vascular and optic disc regions. All results are reported on patient-level held-out test sets to prevent data leakage.

title: EdgeFusion-Seg: Lightweight Edge-Guided Segmentation and Metric Depth for Single- Frame Markerless AR
abstract: Markerless augmented reality (AR) on consumer phones must answer two questions from a single ordinary photograph: what surfaces and objects occupy the scene, and how far each lies from the camera. This paper addresses that gap with a single-frame pipeline that converts one RGB image of an indoor living space into a structurally segmented, metrically scaled, three-dimensional layout suitable for markerless AR object placement. At its core is EdgeFusion-Seg, a compact multi-task network that segments the frame into five structural classes chosen for their relevance to placement. EdgeFusion-Seg delivers the best boundary fidelity and the smallest model with accurate BoundaryF and mIoU while perceiving low parameters.

title: FreqFusion: A Frequency-Domain Hybrid Network for Cross-Tissue Generalisation in Histopathology Deepfake Detection
abstract: Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence have made it feasible to produce highly realistic synthetic histopathology images. Although such images are useful for data augmentation, education, and model development, they pose significant risks of scientific fraud, data contamination, medical fraud, and erosion of trust in digital pathology workflows. This paper examines whether frequency-domain features can enhance cross-tissue deepfake detection without access to target-domain training data. We propose FreqFusion, a hybrid model that combines a MobileNetV3Small spatial branch with a compact FFT-based convolutional neural network branch. FreqFusion is trained on breast histopathology images using real BreCaHAD patches and synthetic SNOW StyleGAN2 data, and evaluated on unseen lymph node histopathology images containing GAN-generated and U-Net-generated fakes. FreqFusion128 achieves an AUC of 0.6521 on cross-tissue GAN fake detection, representing a 24.9 percent relative improvement over the MobileNetV3Small baseline. The 128-dimensional frequency embedding provides the strongest overall balance among the proposed MobileNetV3-based variants. U-Net-generated fakes remain substantially more difficult to detect across all models, representing a critical limitation of cross-generator transfer. These findings indicate that frequency-domain features provide partial improvement in histopathology deepfake detection without access to target-domain training data, though the achieved performance remains below the threshold required for practical clinical or forensic deployment.

title: An Interpretable Machine Learning Framework for Diabetes Risk Prediction
abstract: The current trend of diabetes escalating to global levels necessitates that the risk be identified early through non-invasive lifestyle and food information. However, the dimensionality of lifestyle surveys is very high and most machine learning models lack transparency which severely constrains their clinical usability. Here, (N=189), we suggest an interpretable predictive framework that is focused on clinical transparency and less overfitting. Boruta algorithm was applied to filter 58 lifestyle features with high rigor and a highly significant predictive subset were obtained with BMI, age, and sleep quality. Individual algorithms (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost) and homemade ensemble structures were evaluated involving 5-fold stratified cross-validation. Using an ablation study of ensemble estimators, it was revealed that the most powerful pairwise ensemble, which was purely tree-based, was a combination of Random Forest and XGBoost, and this combination had an accuracy of 89.47% and the F1-score of 0.83. These finding evidences that when variance-reducing (bagging) and bias-reducing (boosting) models are separated and integrated, the ensemble resists the structural collision between mixed linear probabilities, and effectively captures non-linear lifestyle trends. Moreover, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) served to ensure the transparency of diagnosis by quantifying the directional influence of any one lifestyle decision on the final risk prediction outcome. Finally, the framework demonstrates that rigorous feature selection plus explainable and high performing ensemble modeling is a more reliable and suitable tool in the individualized diabetes risk assessment.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Smart Traffic Signal Optimization: A Comparative Analysis of Efficiency and Robustness
abstract: Traffic congestion in urban areas is one of the major issues in contemporary transport systems, especially when the traffic demand is considerably volatile and unpredictable. When the traffic flows are normal, fixed-time traffic signal controllers can work effectively, but they tend to work poorly when there is a sudden shift in the traffic. Although Deep Reinforcement Learning has become a promising solution in adaptive traffic signal control, typical controllers which are based on standard Deep Q-Network models are not resistant to unstable or noisy environments because they require instantaneous observation of their states. This paper presents a hybrid traffic signal control framework that combines Long Short-Term Memory based traffic prediction with a Deep Q-Network controller. The proposed framework follows a dual-stream architecture. A LSTM model is trained using actual traffic data to discover short-time temporal dynamics, whereas a DQN controller is trained in a SUMO simulation environment to discover adaptive signal phase control. The predicted near-future traffic flow was then architecturally integrated into the state representation in such a way that it can be applied to the agent to be able to make decisions based on present and near-future traffic. Through the experiments, the LSTM was found to have attained a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0855, improving prediction performance by 15% over a persistence baseline. In controller evaluation, a Genetic Algorithm optimized static controller performed best under predictable heavy traffic, but the proposed hybrid controller was more robust under extreme traffic conditions. In the most volatile scenario, the hybrid controller maintained a queue measure of about 38,801, compared with 42,418 for the static controller and about 85,000 for the pure DQN model. These results suggest that incorporating temporal prediction into reinforcement learning can improve robustness in unstable traffic environments.

title: FreqFusion: A Frequency-Domain Hybrid Network for Cross-Tissue Generalisation in Histopathology Deepfake Detection
abstract: Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence have made it feasible to produce highly realistic synthetic histopathology images. Although such images are useful for data augmentation, education, and model development, they pose significant risks of scientific fraud, data contamination, medical fraud, and erosion of trust in digital pathology workflows. This paper examines whether frequency-domain features can enhance cross-tissue deepfake detection without access to target-domain training data. We propose FreqFusion, a hybrid model that combines a MobileNetV3Small spatial branch with a compact FFT-based convolutional neural network branch. FreqFusion is trained on breast histopathology images using real BreCaHAD patches and synthetic SNOW StyleGAN2 data, and evaluated on unseen lymph node histopathology images containing GAN-generated and U-Net-generated fakes. FreqFusion128 achieves an AUC of 0.6521 on cross-tissue GAN fake detection, representing a 24.9 percent relative improvement over the MobileNetV3Small baseline. The 128-dimensional frequency embedding provides the strongest overall balance among the proposed MobileNetV3-based variants. U-Net-generated fakes remain substantially more difficult to detect across all models, representing a critical limitation of cross-generator transfer. These findings indicate that frequency-domain features provide partial improvement in histopathology deepfake detection without access to target-domain training data, though the achieved performance remains below the threshold required for practical clinical or forensic deployment.

title: Enhancing lung segmentation in chest X-rays via SAM with anatomical priors and boundary-aware loss
abstract: Accurate lung segmentation in chest X-rays is a foundational step for computer-aided diagnosis of respiratory diseases such as pneumonia, tuberculosis, and lung cancer. While the Segment Anything Model (SAM) has demonstrated remarkable zero-shot segmentation capabilities on natural images, its direct application to medical imaging remains limited due to domain shift, low contrast, and ambiguous anatomical boundaries. To address these challenges, we propose a lightweight yet effective adaptation of SAM that integrates (i) a Mask Autoencoder (MAE) as an anatomical prior to enforce global shape consistency, and (ii) a composite loss function combining Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE), Dice, and Boundary losses to jointly optimize pixel-level accuracy, region overlap, and edge fidelity. Our parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy trains only 0.3% of SAM's parameters, specifically the mask decoder, while freezing the image and prompt encoders. Evaluated on the MedSeg Chest X-ray Lung Dataset, our method achieves a Dice score of 87.3%, outperforming both full fine-tuning (MedSAM: 81.2%) and recent parameter-efficient variants (S-SAM: 84.6%, SAM-PARSER: 85.1%). Moreover, our model demonstrates exceptional robustness across the test set, with median Dice and Specificity exceeding 0.90, and runs at 78 ms per image, the fastest among compared methods. Qualitative results confirm precise delineation of lung fields even under challenging conditions such as rib overlap and cardiac silhouette interference. By combining anatomical constraints with boundary-aware supervision, our framework improves prompt-conditioned lung segmentation performance and provides a lightweight segmentation component that can be integrated into larger clinical decision-support pipelines.

title: A Feature-Fusion Ensemble Approach for Tamil Hate Speech Detection
abstract: Detecting online toxicity in morphologically rich, low-resource languages like Tamil remains a major computational challenge.Standard transformer models often struggle with sub-word fragmentation, which can dilute the semantic intensity of regional insults and out-of-vocabulary slang.To mitigate this limitation, we train a multi-layer hybrid framework that fuses the deep contextual representations of L3Cube-TamilBERT with the character-level robustness of FastText embeddings.Our architecture leverages Last-4 Layers averaging and a dual pooling strategy (Mean + Max) to capture both global sentence intent and extract high-activation spikes of offensive cues typically lost in single layer representations.Experiments show that this hybrid model achieves a Macro-F1 of 0.7883, notably enhancing Hate Recall (0.7503) for detection of offensive content.Additionally, as reported by other studies, stacking ensemble achieves peak hate precision (0.9296), providing a high accuracy alternative for moderation scenarios requiring minimal false positives.By combining deep contextual hidden states with FastText embeddings, the proposed feature-fusion ensemble approach with multi-layer hybrid framework approach establishes a new benchmark for hate speech detection for Tamil.

title: Ethical Dimensions of AI Development: Africa’s Role and Challenges
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a cornerstone of technological innovation, transforming industries such as healthcare, education, and finance ("AI: History and Evolution," 2023; "AI Development in Emerging Markets," 2023). Despite its global advancements, AI development in Africa raises significant ethical concerns, particularly in the context of data labeling tasks. Workers often face challenges such as low wages, insecure job conditions, and exposure to harmful content, which take a toll on their mental health and economic stability. These systemic issues are further exacerbated by weak regulatory frameworks and limited access to mental health resources in many African countries ("AI Ethics and Governance," 2023). The lack of strong labor protections and minimal oversight allows exploitation to persist, highlighting the need for immediate intervention to ensure fair treatment and sustainable practices. This article explores these challenges and presents actionable solutions, including implementing fair labor practices, providing mental health support, and enforcing stronger regulations. It advocates for fostering inclusivity in AI development and leveraging synthetic data to reduce reliance on harmful content. Addressing these concerns is crucial for building an equitable and sustainable AI ecosystem ("Ethical AI Development," 2024; "Labor Economics in AI," 2024).

title: MedGore: An Approach and a Dataset for Identification of Sensitive Medical Images
abstract: Medical images are invaluable in illustrating health issues for the patients.While biomedical publications are a good source of such images, some of the images are not appropriate for the patient viewing without a warning.To enable development of automated tools for selection of patient-safe images and generation of warnings, we created a dataset MedGore of over 78,000 sensitive medical images and 183,000 non-sensitive images published in the biomedical literature.The sensitive content includes gore, severe disease, nudity, surgical openings, internal organs, and other medical images of this nature.The set of the manually identified seed 300 images was expanded using a combination of human curation and a nearest neighbor clustering algorithm.The quality of the automatically labeled images was evaluated manually, yielding a total of more than 4,000 doubly-manually annotated images.The automatically labeled images proved to approach the utility of the manually labeled images for training the models in our experiments that validated the dataset in the task of labeling unseen images using the image features, the figure captions or both.

title: Explainable Intelligent Recommendation System for Optimal Destination Sequencing
abstract: Tourism has emerged as a critical driver of national economic development in Sri Lanka, contributing approximately 4.9% to national GDP and supporting over 402,000 employment positions. Despite rapid growth in domestic travel post-pandemic, most existing travel recommendation platforms continue to surface only the most popular destinations, suffering from systemic popularity bias, opaque decision-making, and a complete absence of route optimization. This paper presents RouteMaster, an Explainable Intelligent Recommendation System for Optimal Destination Sequencing that addresses all three limitations simultaneously. The proposed system integrates a Causal-Aware Hybrid Filtering pipeline combining Propensity Score Matching (PSM) and Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW) for bias mitigation, an ensemble of XGBoost, LightGBM, and Random Forest classifiers for engagement probability prediction, a Nearest Neighbor Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) heuristic for geographic route sequencing, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for transparent recommendation justification. Deployed as a full-stack React–FastAPI–MySQL web application and evaluated on 10,000 synthetic tourist profiles across 28 Sri Lankan destinations, the Gradient Boosting ensemble achieves 96.50% accuracy, F1-score of 0.8563, and ROC-AUC of 0.8725, outperforming all baseline approaches. IPW based causal debiasing improved recommendation diversity by 31%. All 24 functional requirements achieved 100% acceptance in external validation testing, confirming the system’s production readiness.

title: Machine Learning-Driven Personalised Learning Pathway Recommendation for Transferable Skill Enhancement in Undergraduate Academic Performance
abstract: This study developed and evaluated a machine learning-driven personalised learning pathway recommendation system to support transferable skill development and academic performance among undergraduate students. The study used secondary data from the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset, comprising 24,998 student records after preprocessing and integration. Eighteen features were selected from the available dataset based on educational relevance and correlation analysis. K-means clustering was applied to identify four learner profiles, and the resulting cluster labels were incorporated into subsequent model development. Five classification models were trained and compared: Decision Tree, Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbours, Random Forest and XGBoost. A Stacking Hybrid model combining XGBoost, Random Forest and K-Nearest Neighbours as base learners, with Logistic Regression as the meta-learner, was then evaluated for multi-class prediction of student performance categories. The final model was tested on 5,000 student records and achieved an accuracy of 85.00%, weighted precision of 85.10%, weighted recall of 85.00% and weighted F1-score of 84.79%. Ten-fold stratified cross-validation produced a mean accuracy of 84.28%, with a standard deviation of 0.009. The recommendation component assessed nine transferable skill areas and generated personalised learning pathways using 30 curated resources across three difficulty levels. The Stacking Hybrid model correctly identified 2,150 at-risk students out of 2,405 in the 5,000-student test set, achieving an 89.40% detection rate and identifying 1,013 additional students beyond the generic baseline. The recommendation engine was separately evaluated on 500 student records and attained 92.20% accuracy based on category-to-resource matching criteria, indicating the system's effectiveness in delivering targeted transferable skill interventions. These findings indicate that machine learning-based personalisation can support more targeted academic interventions, although further validation with broader institutional datasets and longitudinal outcome measures is required.

title: CAL-Log: Cost-Aware Active Learning with Logarithmic Cognitive Effort Modeling and Online Adaptation to Human Annotation Behavior
abstract: Active learning (AL) reduces labeled data requirements in NLP, yet most methods optimize label efficiency while ignoring annotation cost.Standard uncertainty sampling assumes uniform effort, leading to suboptimal resource allocation when documents vary in length.Supasan and Athuraliya (2026) introduced CAL-Log, a cost-aware AL variant using logarithmic cost modeling C(x)=α+β log(1+L(x)), where C(x) is the predicted annotation time for document x and L(x) is its token length, grounded in information foraging theory (Pirolli and Card, 1999) and psycholinguistic studies of human skimming (Rayner, 1998).While prior work introduced preliminary cost-aware mechanisms, this paper is the first to formalize, operationalize, and extensively validate CAL-Log as a standalone framework, extending it with two new contributions: temperature-scaled calibrated entropy and online per-annotator cost adaptation, which together resolve the coldstart calibration bottleneck identified in the prior work.Experiments on ten text classification benchmarks demonstrate a 3.3× speedup over BADGE (Batch Active learning by Diverse Gradient Embeddings; Ash et al., 2020) and 3.9× over Entropy sampling to reach F1 = 0.80, with large effect sizes (Cohen's d>0.8).A live annotation deployment with preliminary user evaluation (N =42) suggests that the online cost model produces readingspeed classifications consistent with annotator self-reports, and that a transparency interface successfully communicates the scoring rationale to non-expert users.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Code Review Comments to Understand Reviewer Emotions and Their Impact on Software Project Quality
abstract: Code review comments contain emotional expressions that may influence collaboration quality and software development outcomes. Although previous studies have explored sentiment analysis in software engineering, limited research has quantitatively examined the relationship between reviewer sentiment and measurable software quality attributes. This study proposes a hybrid RoBERTa+VADER sentiment analysis framework combined with a Weighted Overall Sentiment Score (OSS) to account for comment length and engagement level when analyzing reviewer emotions in GitHub code review comments. A dataset of 3,720 review comments collected from 20 open-source GitHub repositories was manually labeled into Satisfied, Neutral, and Unsatisfied categories. Multiple sentiment classification approaches including VADER, Naive Bayes, SVM, LSTM, BERT, and RoBERTa were evaluated. The proposed hybrid model achieved the best performance with 73.2% accuracy and an F1-score of 0.731. The study further investigated the relationship between project-level sentiment and SonarQube quality metrics using Pearson correlation analysis. Results indicate that reviewer sentiment demonstrates a moderate correlation with reliabilityrelated metrics, suggesting that sentiment may reflect the broader collaborative atmosphere of active software projects. Weaker relationships were observed for maintainability, security, and code duplication metrics. The findings highlight the importance of developer communication and provide evidence for integrating sentiment-aware monitoring into collaborative software development environments.

Multiple sentiment classification approaches including VADER, Naive Bayes, SVM, LSTM, BERT, and RoBERTa were evaluated. The proposed hybrid model achieved the best performance with 73.2% accuracy and an F1-score of 0.731. The study further investigated the relationship between project-level sentiment and SonarQube quality metrics using Pearson correlation analysis. Results indicate that reviewer sentiment demonstrates a moderate correlation with reliabilityrelated metrics, suggesting that sentiment may reflect the broader collaborative atmosphere of active software projects. Weaker relationships were observed for maintainability, security, and code duplication metrics. The findings highlight the importance of developer communication and provide evidence for integrating sentiment-aware monitoring into collaborative software development environments.

title: Benchmarking Deepfake Detection Robustness Using a Hybrid CNN and Content Provenance Framework
abstract: Deepfake detection remains a critical task in digital media forensics because synthetic facial images can undermine the reliability of visual evidence and public communication. This study develops and evaluates a hybrid deepfake detection framework that combines convolutional neural network-based visual artefact analysis with content provenance verification. The primary experiments used the Deepfake vs Real 60K dataset, which contained 57,071 facial images divided into real and fake classes. Images were resized to 224 × 224 pixels, normalised and augmented during training. The classification component used an EfficientNetB0-based convolutional neural network with a Squeeze-and-Excitation attention mechanism. The provenance component extracted deep feature embeddings and compared input images with real and fake reference databases using cosine similarity. The CNN probability and provenance probability were combined using weighted score fusion to generate the final prediction. The CNN with attention achieved 93.5% accuracy and a ROC-AUC of 0.9937. The provenance module achieved 98.8% accuracy and a ROC-AUC of 0.9996 under controlled within-distribution evaluation. The hybrid framework achieved 94.3% accuracy, precision of 0.95, recall of 0.94, F1-score of 0.94 and ROC-AUC of 0.9969. Provenance score analysis showed clearer separation between real and fake images than perceptual hashing. Cross-dataset evaluation indicated variable generalisation performance, with accuracy ranging from 52.30% to 99.32% across external datasets. The findings suggest that provenance-based similarity analysis can complement CNN-based detection and improve interpretability. However, performance depends on dataset distribution and reference database coverage, and further validation with independent datasets is required before operational use in digital forensic workflows.

title: A Machine Learning Approach for Predicting Developer Burnout Risk from Behavioral Patterns in Open-Source GitHub Activities
abstract: Burnout is a psychiatric condition caused by emotional exhaustion, persistent cognitive strain, and diminished personal accomplishment. It frequently arises from continuous workload pressures, irregular work schedules, and ongoing workload demands. In today’s highly competitive information technology industry, burnout has emerged as a significant and growing concern. Reactive burnout-detection methods, such as traditional surveys and HR evaluations, are often inadequate in digital work environments. This research uses behavioral data derived from open-source GitHub activity to address the gap in proactive, developer-focused burnout prediction models. The main objective is to develop a reliable machine learning model that detects subtle changes in developers' Git activity patterns to estimate the likelihood of burnout. The research questions guided the project's implementation, from identifying behavioral patterns in GitHub activities associated with burnout to determining the data extraction approach and selecting the best machine learning predictive model. The GitHub Application Programming Interface was used to retrieve behavioral data from several open-source projects, including Apache Airflow, Facebook/React, home-assistant/core, TensorFlow, and Ansible. The extracted data includes commit messages, commit history, pull request review comments, files changed, review response time, and lines added and deleted. Labelling the dataset was challenging because direct indicators of burnout are not available in GitHub behavioral data. Therefore, heuristic-based proxy labels were developed to classify developers as high-risk or low-risk. After preprocessing the dataset by lowercasing, removing stop words, lemmatizing, and tokenizing, it is converted into a machine-trainable format. The feature vector was used to train two phases of experiments. In the first phase, independent models such as Random Forest, Logistic Regression, XGBoost, and LightGBM were trained and optimized through the Optuna library. In the second phase, advanced ensemble models such as Stacking and Weighted Voting were applied. The Weighted Voting Ensemble model achieved the best predictive effectiveness, with an Accuracy of 91%. This study concludes that burnout is a personalized, cumulative phenomenon and that a context-aware ensemble model can effectively serve as an early warning system for burnout-risk estimation among developers.

title: The Role of Perceived Fairness of Algorithms on Shaping Psychological Well-Being: Propositions and Future Research Agenda
abstract: With the growth of technology, there is a growing demand for decision-making through algorithmic platforms. However, such decisions would create negative individual outcomes such as perceived unfairness and lower psychological well-being. The purpose of this study is to fill an existing research gap by proposing a new model to examine the impact of perceived fairness of algorithms on psychological well-being, with the moderating role of technology transparency. The current study was conducted by reviewing 26 articles related to psychological well-being, perceived fairness of algorithms and technology transparency. Based on the review, a conceptual model is proposed with two propositions that future researchers can empirically validate. Accordingly, this study provides two theoretical implications. Firstly, it reviews the existing literature on algorithmic decision-making and psychological well-being. Secondly, it contributes to the Theory of Cognitive Appraisal by defining the ways of deriving perceptions among individuals. The paper shows directions of future research and emphasises the need for empirical testing within the given model. The analysis helps to shed light on the ethical adoption of artificial intelligence in business practices.

title: Resilient Intelligence in Biomimetic Design of Coastal Green Infrastructure: Evaluating Habitat Complexity in Econcrete Modules for Adaptive Reef Patches
abstract: Coastal ecosystems face escalating threats from climate change and urbanisation, necessitating green infrastructure that balances structural resilience with ecological biomimetic design. This study investigates the habitat complexity of seven ECOncrete® coastal protection modules designed as building units for reef patches to evaluate their potential to enhance biodiversity and coastal resilience. A semi-quantitative framework integrated visual scoring by a multidisciplinary expert panel with quantitative volumetric analysis across six ecological features: surface topology, edge complexity, internal void architecture, vertical complexity, shelter provision, and organic form factor. Habitat potential ratios (void-to-solid volume) were calculated as geometric proxies for niche availability. Classic Tidal Pools and Bio Active Pocket emerged as top performers with visual scores of 89.0 and 71.7 and habitat ratios of 0.760 and 1.540, while Sea Wall Panels and Bio Active Standard scored lowest. Resilient intelligence — defined as the integration of expert perceptual judgement with exploratory computational sensitivity analysis — was incorporated through Random Forest modelling, identifying Surface Topology and Edge Complexity as dominant design attributes. Ranking mismatches highlight the complementary nature of perceptual and geometric metrics. The study underscores the potential of void-rich, nature-inspired modules to support marine biodiversity, with field validation recommended as a necessary next step.

title: A Machine Learning Based Early Warning Framework for CKDu Risk Prediction Using Water Quality Data
abstract: This paper proposes and tests an environmental water-quality screening proof-of-concept based on machine learning and routine physicochemical measurements. Although the framework is described as CKDu risk prediction, it should be interpreted strictly as an environmental proxy water-potability feature-screening tool and not as a clinical patient-modelling system. The study employed an open-source dataset of 3,276 water samples with nine variables: pH, hardness, total dissolved solids, chloramines, sulfate, conductivity, organic carbon, trihalomethanes and turbidity. Missing values were imputed using median values, and feature scaling was applied where required. A stratified 80:20 train-test split was performed using the original class distribution and a random seed of 42. Accuracy, balanced accuracy, macro F1-score, ROC-AUC and confusion-matrix analysis were used to evaluate five supervised machine-learning models. Random Forest achieved the highest test performance, with an accuracy of 0.659, balanced accuracy of 0.641, macro F1-score of 0.636 and ROC-AUC of 0.695. The selected model was embedded in a prototype interface that translates non-potability probabilities into Low, Moderate and High screening bands and provides input validation and user-friendly follow-up messages. The results indicate the technical feasibility of multivariate machine learning for water-potability classification and sample prioritisation. The dataset does not include CKDu patient records, clinical outcomes, patient exposure histories, geographic exposure information or locally collected samples from CKDu-endemic communities. Therefore, the framework should be regarded only as a proof-of-concept environmental water-screening tool, not as a validated CKDu prediction, clinical diagnostic or regulatory decision-making system.

title: Developing a Persuasive Social Robot as a Learning Companion
abstract: This study presents the design and evaluation of a persuasive social robot, Roboto, developed as a learning companion to support early second language (L2) acquisition in children aged 4–8. While prior research in robot-assisted learning has largely emphasized interaction design and short-term engagement, limited attention has been given to integrating pedagogically grounded frameworks such as constructivist learning and Problem-Based Learning (PBL) within child–robot interaction. To address this gap, Roboto employs a question-driven conversational model that facilitates active learning through guided inquiry and incremental feedback. The system incorporates multimodal interaction, including speech, visual cues, and emotion-aware responses, to enhance engagement and adaptability. An experimental study was conducted with 18 participants across three interaction scenarios: conversational learning, storytelling, and repeated longitudinal sessions. Data were collected using questionnaire-based evaluations and observational measures, and analyzed using nonparametric statistical methods, including Chi-square and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. The results indicate high levels of user engagement and acceptance, with all participant sexpressing willingness to interact with the system. Statistical findings show that the PBL-driven questioning model significantly enhances perceived learning support. Furthermore, longitudinal analysis reveals a significant increase in positive emotional engagement and improved task efficiency over repeated sessions, suggesting the development of interaction familiarity. Despite these promising findings, the study is limited by a small sample size and the absence of a control group. Overall, this work demonstrates that integrating constructivist pedagogy with persuasive and emotionally adaptive interaction design can effectively support learner engagement and perceived learning support, providing a foundation for future research in educational social robotics. title: PACE-KG: An Automated Pipeline for Educational Knowledge Graph Construction from Lecture PDF Slides
abstract: The rapid growth of digital learning materials, especially lecture PDFs, makes it challenging for students to identify and connect key concepts. Existing educational knowledge graph systems often produce untyped or binary relations, lack source grounding, and rely on external knowledge bases, introducing noise. This paper presents PACE-KG, an automated pipeline for constructing typed Educational Knowledge Graphs directly from lecture slides without domain-specific retraining. PACE-KG integrates layout-aware PDF parsing with OCR fallback, zero-shot keyphrase extraction via GLiNER, and LLM-based triple extraction constrained by an eight-relation pedagogical ontology. A three-layer validation mechanism comprising keyphrase anchoring, SBERT evidence verification, and semantic post-validation ensures accuracy. Concepts are SBERT-weighted, expanded via a closed corpus, stored in Neo4j AuraDB, and visualised through a React interface. Evaluation on 356 exhaustively annotated triples achieved a macro-average Simple Random Sampling (SRS) score µs = 0.610 (σ = 0.124 across documents; 95% CI ±0.051), a 14-point improvement over the optimised baseline. Evidence validity reached 87.1% and concept relevance 82.2%, while relation accuracy at 62.1% indicates room for future improvement. User surveys confirmed full relevance and ease of use across all participants. Generalisation to disciplines beyond the evaluated Java course remains future work.

title: A Hybrid Convolutional Neural Network Approach for Context-aware Fashion Recommendation
abstract: This study aimed to develop a fashion recommendation system that classifies clothing items and recommends complementary outfit pieces based on user-selected style preferences, addressing the limitation of existing systems that rely solely on visual similarity without incorporating style-based personalisation. The study was carried out at the Department of Information and Communication Technology, Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, University of Sri Jayewardenepura, Sri Lanka, between 25th July 2025 and 2nd June 2026, and followed a quantitative experimental approach involving the design, development, and performance evaluation of a two-stage deep learning-based classification and recommendation system. The proposed system consists of two stages: classification and recommendation. In the first stage, the system classifies the query item using a hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN) model combining ResNet-50 and EfficientNetB0. In the second stage, Fashion CLIP and CLIP ViT-B/32 models retrieve complementary items, which are then filtered and re-ranked based on the user-selected style from four categories: Casual, Formal, Party, and Streetwear. The classification model achieved 94% accuracy on the main dataset and 89.17% on external validation, while the recommendation pipeline achieved a mean Precision@5 of 84.2% and Accuracy@5 of 94.4%. The proposed system achieved 100% style consistency compared with 56.2% for the baseline model. The proposed two-stage system combines item classification with style-aware recommendation and has practical potential for integration into fashion e-commerce platforms to enhance user experience and support cross-category sales.

title: Effectiveness and students’ perception of tutor-guided AI navigation in undergraduate medical education in Sri Lanka: a quasi-experimental study
abstract: Abstract Background The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, into undergraduate medical education offers new opportunities for personalized learning. However, concerns remain regarding content accuracy, possible over-reliance and limited critical engagement when AI tools are used without guidance. Tutor-guided AI navigation has been proposed as a structured approach combining AI accessibility with educator oversight. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and perception of tutor-guided AI navigation among medical undergraduates. Methods The study was conducted among 87 final-year medical students at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Kelaniya, Sri Lanka. A quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test design compared knowledge gains following tutor-guided versus self-directed ChatGPT-assisted learning. A cross-sectional survey assessing three domains-Perception of Learning Experience, AI Usability and Confidence, Satisfaction and Overall Impression- was administered immediately after the session. Responses were measured using a five-point Likert scale. Internal consistency was evaluated with Cronbach’s alpha and descriptive statistics were analysed using SPSS. Results Baseline pre-test scores were comparable between groups (W = 670.5, p = 0.153). Both groups improved significantly from pre- to post-test (p 0.86). Students rated ease of use (4.19 ± 1.07), tutor-guided AI experience (4.03 ± 1.13), satisfaction (3.91 ± 0.94) and willingness to recommend (4.01 ± 0.97) favourably, while trust in AI accuracy was moderate (3.27 ± 0.91). Conclusion Tutor-guided AI-assisted learning was well accepted by students and provided a positive, structured learning experience. Although it did not produce a statistically significant advantage in immediate knowledge gain over self-directed AI use, it was associated with favourable perceptions of usability, satisfaction and recommendation. These findings support the structured integration of tutor-guided AI into undergraduate medical education while maintaining educator oversight and critical appraisal of AI-generated content.

title: Generative AI and IoT security: opportunities and challenges
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is one of the frameworks that help to make safe and rational decisions and analyze complex information to foresee risky behaviors. Now the internet of things (IoT) has spread all over the world, and cyberattacks are used to ensure real-time integration of huge amounts of data. But coordinating with threats and attacks, as well as dealing with hackers and using networks, is an important challenge for the security of the classic IoT. Some of them include rule-based detection, rule-based intrusion detection, and signature-based intrusion detection. There are countless possibilities for generative AI (Gen AI), such as advanced anomaly detection, realistic attack simulation, production of artificially generated data to facilitate the prediction of writers, and automated incident management. Besides, there are a few challenges with Gen AI integration to IoT applications. Problems with competitive management, the computing and technological constraints of IoT devices, ethics issues, and numerous ways for hackers to extract false information from sensors using Gen AI are major challenges. In addition, it could be held responsible for publicizing sensitive information from fake datasets and could have problems with the privacy of sensitive data being trained with Gen AI. The main objective of this research work is to do a detailed analysis of IoT security Gen AI technology. The information, in this report for the 2018–2025 periods, was obtained from the current literature. The paper discusses and addresses some key concepts, and based on that, there are opportunities, challenges, and innovative approaches that are crucial for Gen AI utilization. The next generation thinks that Gen AI will be one of the most important technologies that will affect the next generation of IoT cybersecurity solutions. It is important for them to thoroughly analyze the advantages and disadvantages of this technology.

title: A Unified Multimodal Edge AI Smart Assistive Stick for Visually Impaired Users
abstract: Smart assistive sticks are widely studied as mobility aids for blind and visually impaired users, yet many existing systems remain limited to obstacle warning and do not integrate user state awareness, environmental context understanding, and emergency audio perception into one embedded assistive platform. This paper presents a unified multimodal edge AI smart assistive stick that combines three complementary intelligence layers: behavioral stress detection using grip pressure and motion sensing, acoustic emergency sound recognition using an on-device audio classifier, and contextaware navigation through vision-based landmark recognition and ultrasonic obstacle sensing. The behavioral module applies sliding window averaging and debounce-based confirmation to classify user state into Normal, Stressed, and Panic categories. The navigation module identifies landmarks such as crosswalks and traffic lights while enforcing a safety-first obstacle alert policy. The audio module detects emergency sound events to increase situational awareness. A caregiver-facing dashboard provides live monitoring, environmental sensor visualization, event history, and analytics as a remote supervision layer. Experimental evaluation on the embedded prototype yields approximately 91% validation accuracy for landmark recognition, 87.5% accuracy for behavioral stress detection (F1scores 0.80 and 0.91 per class), and 75% overall validation accuracy for acoustic emergency sound recognition, with a 96% true positive rate for distress events. The ultrasonic subsystem reliably detects obstacles within 80 cm. The proposed system demonstrates the feasibility of a low-cost, edge-native, multimodal assistive framework that meaningfully improves mobility safety and contextual awareness for visually impaired users.

title: A Proof-of-Concept AI Framework for Vanilla Crop Monitoring and Quality Measurement
abstract: Vanilla planifolia cultivation is critically bottlenecked by a highly time-sensitive pollination window and susceptibility to rapid-onset pathologies, challenges that current smart farming systems fail to adequately address. This research introduces a comprehensive edge-computing and IoT framework specifically engineered to automate the vanilla crop lifecycle. The architecture strictly prioritizes autonomous mobile field scouting to capture fleeting blooming events for immediate manual pollination, followed closely by the real-time, edge-based detection of early-stage plant diseases. Extending this primary field workflow, the system incorporates a non-destructive post-harvest quality measurement module for objective pre-curing pod grading. Finally, a supplementary stationary IoT network provides foundational support by dynamically automating greenhouse fertigation and environmental regulation. Evaluated through a controlled proof-of-concept utilizing curated datasets and simulated baselines, the framework demonstrates strong architectural feasibility and baseline edge-inference performance. Having established viability in simulated environments, our next phase targets rigorous real-world validation in active greenhouses to assess the system's operational robustness under dynamic agricultural conditions.

title: Intelligent Gem Cutting Robotic Arm: A Semi-Autonomous Robotic System for Multimodal Gemstone Identification, Defect-Aware Evaluation, and 3D Cut Planning
abstract: Gemstone cutting is a highly skilled and laborintensive process that significantly influences the final value and optical performance of gemstones. In Sri Lanka, where the gem industry plays a vital economic and cultural role, traditional cutting methods rely heavily on expert craftsmanship, leading to inconsistencies, material loss, and limited scalability. This research proposes a semi-autonomous intelligent gem cutting robotic arm that integrates robotics, embedded systems, machine learning, and 3D modeling to automate and optimize the gemstone cutting workflow. The system performs gemstone identification, defect-aware evaluation, value estimation, cut type recommendation, and precise robotic execution using a ROS 2-based control architecture. Machine learning models are employed for gemstone identification, defect detection, and cut planning, while a 5-DOF robotic arm executes optimized cutting trajectories. The proposed prototype demonstrates a multimodal data-fusion approach to bridge the gap between gemological analysis and robotic execution and robotic control to gemstone cutting in an academic and research-oriented context, highlighting potential pathways toward scalable, intelligent gem manufacturing systems.

title: AI-Powered Intelligent Home Planning & Optimization System
abstract: Modern house planning is complex due to limited land, space constraints, and cultural requirements, often requiring costly expert input. This research proposes an AI-powered home planning system integrating land utilization, automated 2D plan generation, interior and exterior optimization, and Vastu compliance evaluation. It uses YOLOv8 and CNN models for room detection, alongside rule- and constraint-based optimization for layouts and furniture placement. Operating on structured JSON data, the system ensures modular integration and efficient processing. Experiments show it provides a cost- and timeefficient solution, offering intelligent decision support without expert intervention.

title: Smart Monitoring and Identification System for Leopards Using Thermal, Acoustic, and Spatial Analysis
abstract: The study in this paper focuses on conservation efforts for the Sri Lankan leopard (Panthera pardus Kothiya). It tackles ecological and technological challenges related to rising human-wildlife conflict and the limitations of current monitoring methods. The research suggests a combined system that incorporates three advanced technologies in computing. One technology uses deep learning with MobileNetV2 and transfer learning for visual monitoring. Another uses infrared for thermal analysis, converting temperature data and segmenting anatomy to detect physiological issues and injuries based on bilateral symmetry. The third employs eco acoustics with spectrogrambased neural networks and Hidden Markov Models. This setup enables real-time, nonintrusive monitoring of leopard populations through roar detection and mapping of spatial density hotspots.

title: Intelligent Traffic Management Using Fuzzy Logic and Machine Learning
abstract: Increasing traffic congestion and road accidents present major challenges in urban environments due to unsafe driving behavior, traffic violations, and inefficient signal con-trol. Conventional traffic management systems rely on manual monitoring and fixed signal timings, making them ineffective in handling dynamic real-time traffic conditions. This research proposes an Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS) that integrates real-time traffic monitoring, adaptive signal control, traffic violation detection, and accident risk prediction through a unified analytical dashboard. The system is designed for an IoT-based four-way junction where sensors and cameras detect vehicle density and dynamically prioritize lanes with higher traffic volume. Using video-based vehicle detection, the system measures vehicle speed in real time and identi-fies violations such as over-speeding, red-light violations, and illegal parking. Drivers receive notifications through a mobile application where they can check violation details and pay fines calculated based on predefined traffic rules. Additionally, a dynamic accident risk scoring mechanism combines real-time vehicle speed data with historical violation records to identify high-risk driving behavior. Analytical dashboards visualize traffic density, violations, and risk levels to support data-driven decision making. The proposed system demonstrates how real-time traffic monitoring, violation detection, and dynamic signal control can improve road safety and traffic efficiency, contributing to the development of advanced smart city traffic management solutions.
